### Claude account seed: a failed `claude-account.json` write no longer throws out of `tumwater start` or a live config reload (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts + test/claude-account.test.ts + test/startup-gate.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `runStartupCheck` (src/gates/startup-gate.ts) promises "never a throw, so a poll can ask it safely", and its comment on the claude seed says "If the seed fails, the first claude run's observation fills the file in". But `seedClaudeAccount` (src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts) calls `writeClaudeAccount(root, account)` with no guard, and `writeClaudeAccount` is a bare `writeJsonAtomic`. An unwritable `.tumwater/state/claude-account.json` therefore throws out of `runStartupCheck`. `tumwater start` then dies on a stack trace, and the supervisor/redeploy poll's `runStartupProblem` throws too. The other caller, the live-reload path in src/config/config-live.ts that seeds a newly routed claude backend, says "never a crash" and has the same unguarded call. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the throw with a scratch test (since deleted): with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set and a directory at `claudeAccountPath(root)`, `seedClaudeAccount(root, defaultConfig(), 123)` threw `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, rename …claude-account.json.tmp-… -> …claude-account.json`. This is the claude twin of the planned "OpenCode catalog seed" entry. That entry touches only src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts, so the two plans share no file except docs/invariants.md, where each appends its own section.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/claude/claude-account.ts, `seedClaudeAccount`: wrap the `writeClaudeAccount(root, account)` call in `try`/`catch`. The `catch` returns `null`, the same value as "billing cannot be decided", so neither caller changes. Neither caller reads the return value (`grep -rn 'seedClaudeAccount(' src`). Leave `writeClaudeAccount` strict: its test "writeClaudeAccount: a write that fails mid-way leaves the previous reading whole" asserts that it throws, and `observeClaudeAccount`'s callers depend on that. Add a sentence to `seedClaudeAccount`'s doc comment (or create one if it has none): a failed write returns null and never throws, so the first claude run's `observeClaudeAccount` fills the file in. Add no warning, because neither caller has a warn sink at this point and wiring one up is a separate change.
2. test/claude-account.test.ts: append "seedClaudeAccount: a failed account write returns null instead of throwing". Model it on "seedClaudeAccount: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY means API billing", including its save/restore of `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Before the call, run `fs.mkdirSync(claudeAccountPath(root), { recursive: true })`. Assert that `seedClaudeAccount(root, defaultConfig() as TumwaterConfig, 123)` returns `null` and that `readClaudeAccount(root, 123)` is `null`.
3. test/startup-gate.test.ts: append "an unwritable claude account file does not fail the startup gate". Copy the setup of "a claude seam that exists only as a fallback is checked and its account seeded" (fake `claude` script, `cfg.backends.claude.bin`, `cfg.fallback`). Before `runStartupCheck`, `fs.mkdirSync(claudeAccountPath(repo), { recursive: true })`, importing `claudeAccountPath` from src/paths.js if the file does not already import it. Assert that `runStartupCheck(repo, null)` resolves without `"problem"` and that `readClaudeAccount(repo)` is `null`. The fresh `makeRepo()` root keeps the module's `claudeSeedAttempted` set from skipping the seed.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## Claude account seed: a failed write never throws out of startup" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BX had merged and BY (Run end) and BZ (OpenCode catalog seed) were planned, so CA was free. Write one guarantee: `seedClaudeAccount` returns null instead of throwing when the account write fails, so `runStartupCheck` keeps its never-throws contract on a claude team. Binds `seedClaudeAccount` and `runStartupCheck`. Pinned by the two new tests, each cited by its full name.

### OpenCode catalog seed: a malformed models.dev body or a failed cache write no longer rejects `tumwater start` — done 2026-10-20 (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts + test/opencode-catalog.test.ts + docs/invariants.md)

**Goal.** `runStartupCheck` (src/gates/startup-gate.ts) awaits `refreshOpencodeCatalog` with no catch whenever a model job routes to opencode. Its comment says "a failed fetch keeps the last good cache (or an empty one) and never blocks startup". That holds only for a fetch that throws. Two other failures reject the refresh, and with it `runStartupCheck`, so `tumwater start` (src/cli/cli-start.ts awaits `runStartupCheck` with no catch) dies on a stack trace:
- `parseOpencodeCatalog` casts the fetched body instead of checking it. `Object.entries(providerInfo.models)` throws when a kept provider's `models` is `null`. `m.modalities.input.includes` throws when `input` is not an array or string, and `m.reasoning_options?.filter` throws when `reasoning_options` is not an array. A wrong-typed field passes through silently instead. `cost: { input: "0", output: 0 }` yields `inputPerM: "0"`, which the cache then holds, typed as a number, until the next read drops it.
- `writeOpencodeCache(root, cache)` in `refreshOpencodeCatalog` has no guard, so an unwritable `.tumwater/state/opencode-models.json` rejects the refresh. The cache stays stale, so every later start fails the same way.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed all of these with a scratch test (since deleted). Each of `{ opencode: { models: null } }`, `{ opencode: { models: { m: { modalities: { input: 5 } } } } }` and `{ opencode: { models: { m: { reasoning_options: { type: "effort" } } } } }` made `parseOpencodeCatalog(body, [])` throw a TypeError. The `cost` body above returned `{"opencode/m":{"free":false,"inputPerM":"0","outputPerM":0}}`. `refreshOpencodeCatalog` rejected when a directory sat at `opencodeModelsPath(root)`. "OpenCode catalog cache" in PLANS-DONE.md guarded the read side and deliberately left the parse out of scope; this plan covers the parse.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts, `parseOpencodeCatalog`: make it total over any `body`. Skip a provider unless `isJsonObject(providerInfo?.models)`, and skip a model entry unless `isJsonObject(raw)`. Read `cost` only when `isJsonObject(m.cost)` and `limit.context` only when `isJsonObject(m.limit)`, as today otherwise. Set `images` only when `Array.isArray(m.modalities?.input)`, with `modalities` checked by `isJsonObject` first. Compute `efforts` only when `Array.isArray(m.reasoning_options)`: keep the elements that pass `isJsonObject` and have `type === "effort"`, and flatMap each one's `values` when `Array.isArray`, else `[]`. Finally store the model only when `isOpencodeCatalogModel(model)` holds (the existing guard the cache read uses). That drops a model with a non-finite or non-number price, context or effort, so it reads as missing from the catalog, which means "not free", the safe direction for the budget gate. Add one sentence to the doc comment: the body is untrusted network data, and a malformed provider or model is skipped, never thrown on.
2. Same file, `refreshOpencodeCatalog`: wrap `writeOpencodeCache(root, cache)` in `try`/`catch`. The `catch` calls `opts.warn?.(\`could not save the open code model catalog: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` and the function still returns `cache`. Import `errorMessage` from wherever the other src/ files take it (`grep -rn 'export function errorMessage' src`). Extend the function's doc comment: a failed cache write warns and returns the fetched catalog, so the next start fetches again. Leave startup-gate.ts alone. It passes no `warn` today, and wiring that up is a separate change.
3. test/opencode-catalog.test.ts: append two tests.
   - "parseOpencodeCatalog skips a malformed provider or model instead of throwing": the body is `{ opencode: { models: { a: { modalities: { input: 5 } }, b: { reasoning_options: { type: "effort" } }, c: { cost: { input: "0", output: 0 } }, d: null, ok: { cost: { input: 0, output: 0 } } } }, "opencode-go": { models: null } }` with providers `["opencode-go"]`. `assert.deepEqual` the result to `{ "opencode/a": { free: false }, "opencode/b": { free: false }, "opencode/ok": { free: true, inputPerM: 0, outputPerM: 0 } }`.
   - "a failed catalog write warns and still returns the fetched catalog": on `tmpdir()`, `fs.mkdirSync(opencodeModelsPath(root), { recursive: true })` so a directory blocks the atomic rename. Call `refreshOpencodeCatalog` with `providers: []`, `fetch: fetchOf(catalogCapture())`, `cliVersion: "2.0.32"`, `now: () => 1_000` and a `warn` that collects messages. It resolves with `fetchedAt` 1_000 and `models["opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free"]?.free === true` (the model "a failed fetch keeps the old cache and logs one warning" already reads). Exactly one warning starts with `could not save the open code model catalog`.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## OpenCode catalog seed: a refresh never rejects the startup check" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BU, BV and BW had merged, BX (Merge write-back) and BY (Run end) were planned, and BZ was free. Write one guarantee: `refreshOpencodeCatalog` resolves for any fetched body and any cache-write failure. It drops a malformed upstream model rather than storing it or throwing, and a failed write warns through `opts.warn`. Binds `parseOpencodeCatalog`, `refreshOpencodeCatalog` and `isOpencodeCatalogModel`. Pinned by the two new tests plus "a failed fetch keeps the old cache and logs one warning". Cite each test by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 1 reverted, the first new test fails with a TypeError. With step 2 reverted, the second new test fails because the refresh rejects.
- The existing parse tests (the 2.0.32 capture) still pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts as the only changed src/ file.
- Each test name cited in the new section exists verbatim (`grep -rF` each one in test/).

### Run end: a failed role-state save in `finalizeRun` warns and still logs `run_end`, instead of rejecting the run task and skipping the breaker fold (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/run/run-finalize.ts + src/runner/runner-state.ts + test/run-finalize.test.ts + docs/invariants.md)

**Goal.** `finalizeRun` (src/run/run-finalize.ts) runs after the pi run, and for a `queued` result after the change is already in the merge queue. It folds the outcome with `applyRunOutcome`, releases a finished claim, calls `restoreMidRunWake`, then calls `saveRunnerState(root, s)` with no guard. After that come the streak warnings, the `observeClaudeAccount` fold and the `run_end` event. `runPhase` (src/runner/runner-run.ts) says it "Never throws", but a failed save rejects it: the `run_end` event is never logged (so the run's spend, duration and result never reach the feed the report and the failure digest read), and `ctx.setRunPair(undefined)` never runs. The rejection also skips the rest of the launch task in `launchDueRuns` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts): the fallback breaker's `recordFallbackRunAt` evidence fold and, for a probe, `abandonFallbackProbeAt`. That task's `.catch` only sets `running = false` and warns "run task rejected: …", so a probe run whose save fails leaves its claim on the pair. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the rejection with a scratch test (since deleted) in a copy of test/run-finalize.test.ts. It installed `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "feature-2"), "EACCES fake")` and called the file's `run(root, "feature-2", freshRunnerState("feature-2"), { result: "queued", summary: "x" })` helper. The call rejected with `Error: EACCES fake`, `s.running` was false (the fold had already happened in memory), and `eventsOfType(root, "run_end")` was empty. The in-memory state already holds everything the save would write, and the runner's next save (a skip reason, a merge write-back, the next run's end) writes it to disk. So a best-effort save loses nothing the team needs. This narrows the Poll-loop runner state plan's (PLANS-DONE.md) "run-end and CLI callers keep their errors": `saveRunnerState` itself stays strict, and CLI callers keep their errors.

**Approach.**
1. src/run/run-finalize.ts, `finalizeRun`: replace `saveRunnerState(root, s)` with `saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root, s)`. Swap the import from ../runner/runner-state.js (keep `hasOutstandingWork` and the `RunnerState` type, and drop `saveRunnerState` once `grep -n 'saveRunnerState(' src/run/run-finalize.ts` finds no other call). Add one sentence to the comment above the save, or to `finalizeRun`'s doc comment: a failed save warns and the run still ends normally, because the in-memory state already holds the fold and the runner's next save writes it.
2. src/runner/runner-state.ts, `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`'s doc comment: it now names two callers, not just "the orchestrator's poll loop, which has no catch". Reword it to cover the poll loop and the run's end, where a throw would skip `run_end` and the launch task's breaker fold. Do not change the code.
3. test/run-finalize.test.ts: after "an unwritable events feed cannot reject finalizeRun — the outcome still folds and saves", add "a failed role-state save cannot reject finalizeRun — run_end still logs and the run warns". Import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js, add `statePath` to the existing ../src/paths.js import, and add `warningMessages` to the existing ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js import. Use `initializedRepo()` and `freshRunnerState("feature-2")`. Install the fault before calling `run(root, "feature-2", s, { result: "queued", summary: "queued it" })`, and undo it in a `finally`. Assert that the call resolves with `result` `"queued"`, that `s.running` is false, that `eventsOfType(root, "run_end")` has one event with `result` `"queued"`, and that `warningMessages(root)` holds exactly one entry matching `/could not save the role's state: EACCES fake/`. Check `warningMessages`'s and `eventsOfType`'s signatures in test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts before using them.
4. docs/invariants.md: append "## Run end: a failed state save still ends the run" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BU, BV and BW had merged, BX (Merge write-back) was planned, and BY was free. Write one guarantee: `finalizeRun` resolves with the run's outcome and logs `run_end` even when the role's state save or the events feed fails; a failed save warns under the role's id. Binds `finalizeRun` and `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`. Pinned by the new test plus "an unwritable events feed cannot reject finalizeRun — the outcome still folds and saves" and "finalizeRun folds the outcome onto the state, persists it, and logs run_end". Cite each test by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 1 reverted (back to `saveRunnerState`), the new test fails because `finalizeRun` rejects with `EACCES fake`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows src/run/run-finalize.ts and src/runner/runner-state.ts as the only changed src/ files, and runner-state.ts's diff touches only a comment.
- Each test name cited in the new section exists verbatim (`grep -rF` each one in test/).

### Merge write-back: a failed role-state save in `writeMergeOutcome` warns and still drops the settled queue entry, instead of leaving a merged change queued for a second review (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts + test/merge-slot.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `writeMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) runs after a merge has settled, often after the change is already on main. Its order is `applyMergeOutcome`, then `saveRunnerState(root, state)` with no guard, then the streak warning, the best-effort `merge_done`/`merge_failed` event, and finally `dropMerge(file)`. Its doc comment says an unwritable feed "must not skip the drop, or the settled entry would stay queued and be re-verified and re-merged on the next drain". A failed state save skips the drop in exactly that way. The throw also skips the rest of `settleMergeOutcome` (src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts): `removeMergeChange` and `requeueKeptChange` never run. `guardMergeTask` catches it and logs "merge task for <role> could not settle". On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed this with a scratch test (since deleted) in a copy of test/merge-slot.test.ts. It queued an entry with the file's `queued(root)` helper, installed `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "EACCES fake")`, and called `writeMergeOutcome(root, entry, state, "changed", 7, { tokens: 0, cost: 0, providerCost: {} }, file)`. The call threw `Error: EACCES fake`, `queueDepth(root)` was 1, the queue file still existed, and the log held no events. The live `state` object is the runner's own state, so the outcome is already applied in memory, and the runner's next save writes it to disk.

**Approach.**
1. src/merge/merge-slot.ts, `writeMergeOutcome`: replace `saveRunnerState(root, state)` with `saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root, state)`. It is already imported, and on failure it warns under the role's id with "could not save the role's state: <message>". Add one sentence to the doc comment: a failed state save warns and does not skip the drop either, because the in-memory state already holds the outcome and the runner's next save writes it. Leave `saveRunnerState` in `requeueKeptChange` alone (its caller `settleMergeOutcome` already wraps it in a `try`). Leave merge-core.ts alone (its verdict save runs before the merge, not after a durable step). Keep the `saveRunnerState` import only while some other call in the file still uses it (`grep -n 'saveRunnerState(' src/merge/merge-slot.ts`).
2. test/merge-slot.test.ts: after "an unwritable events feed still drops the settled entry — the queue never retries", add "a failed role-state save still logs the outcome and drops the settled entry". Use `queued(root)` and `freshRunnerState("improve")`. Install `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "EACCES fake")` (add `failRenameSyncOn` to the existing ./helpers/fs-faults.js import and `statePath` to the ../src/paths.js import), call `writeMergeOutcome(root, entry, state, "changed", 7, { tokens: 0, cost: 0, providerCost: {} }, file)`, and undo the fault in a `finally`. Assert that `queueDepth(root)` is 0, that `fs.existsSync(file)` is false, that `state.commits` is 1 (the in-memory fold), that `readEvents(root, 10)` has one `merge_done` event, and that `warningMessages(root)` (from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js) is exactly one entry matching `/could not save the role's state: EACCES fake/`.
3. docs/invariants.md: append "## Merge write-back: a settled entry is always dropped" after the last section, using the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout. For the prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BU had merged, BV (OpenCode catalog cache) and BW (QA flow coverage) were planned, and BX was free. Write one guarantee: `writeMergeOutcome` drops the entry's queue file for every result, even when the role's state save or the event write fails; each failure warns and nothing throws. Binds `writeMergeOutcome` and `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`. Pinned by the new test plus "an unwritable events feed still drops the settled entry — the queue never retries" and "a merge's nonzero usage rides its merge_done event and the entry is dropped". Cite each test by its full name.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With step 1 reverted (back to `saveRunnerState`), the new test fails because the call throws `EACCES fake`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
- `git diff --stat` shows src/merge/merge-slot.ts as the only changed src/ file.
- Each test name cited in the new section exists verbatim (`grep -rF` each one in test/).

### OpenCode catalog cache: a foreign entry in `opencode-models.json` is dropped on read instead of throwing out of the poll loop's budget gate and `tumwater status`, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts + test/opencode-catalog.test.ts + test/status-budget.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `readOpencodeCache` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-catalog.ts) checks that `fetchedAt` is a number and that `models` is an object (`isJsonObject`). It does not check the entries, so anything inside `models` reaches callers typed as `OpencodeCatalogModel`. `opencodeModelFree` reads `entry.free` after testing only `entry !== undefined`, so a `null` entry throws a TypeError. `opencodeModelFree` is reached from `pollBudgetGate` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts, through `piPairFree` in src/pi/pi-models.ts; `pollTeamGates` in src/gates/gate-polls.ts calls it with no try), which means the throw escapes the poll loop. It is also reached from `collectBudget` (src/status/status-budget.ts), so it breaks `tumwater status` and the dashboards. `observeOpencodeRun` reads `entry.free` the same way. A wrong-typed field is quietly wrong instead of throwing. `free: "yes"` reads as free to the budget gate, which is the unsafe direction. `efforts: "high"` is a string, and the opencode backend's `entry?.efforts?.includes(thinking)` (src/agent/opencode/opencode-backend.ts) matches substrings of it. Any other field rides along unchecked. `readOpencodeCache` keeps its top-level checks. It returns `models` as a new object that keeps only the entries passing the guard, so a dropped entry reads as a model missing from the cache. ### QA flow coverage: a failed `qa-coverage.json` write warns instead of failing a run whose merge is already queued (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/run/run-stage.ts + src/run/run-verdict.ts + test/run-stage.test.ts + test/run-verdict.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `recordFlow` (src/run/qa-coverage.ts) writes the qa ledger with `writeJsonAtomic` and does not catch a write failure. Its two callers do not catch it either:
- `stageRunMerge` (src/run/run-stage.ts) calls `recordFlow` after the merge is queued, after the pin, and after the best-effort `merge_queued` event.
- `resolveRunVerdict` (src/run/run-verdict.ts) calls it on the no-change path, before returning `no_change`.

So a full disk, a read-only `.tumwater`, or any other failed ledger write throws out of the run. The catch in `runPhase` (src/runner/runner-run.ts) then turns the outcome into `error` and sets `lastError`. `finalizeRun` (src/run/run-finalize.ts) counts that toward the role's error streak, even when the work was committed and queued. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed this with a scratch test (since deleted). The test was a copy of "a qa flow record from the reply is written into the coverage file" with `failRenameSyncOn(qaCoveragePath(root), "EACCES fake")` installed. `stageRunMerge` rejected with `Error: EACCES fake` while `queueDepth(root)` was 1. A second scratch test called `resolveRunVerdict` with test/run-verdict.test.ts's `makeCtx(root, wt, "qa", { flow: { flow: "status", result: "passed" } })`. Without the fault it returned `no_change` and recorded the flow. With the same fault installed it rejected with `Error: EACCES fake`. The ledger only orders the qa role's flow menu. The run-stage comment beside `logEventBestEffort` already says that observability must not reject a run whose work is queued, and the ledger is in the same position.

**Approach.**
1. src/run/run-stage.ts: wrap the `recordFlow(…)` call in `try { … } catch (err) { ctx.warn(`qa flow "${ctx.flow.flow}" not recorded: ${errorMessage(err)}`); }`. Import `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js. Add a one-line comment saying the merge is already queued and the ledger only orders the qa menu, so a failed write warns rather than failing the run. Its return value and every other step stay as they are.

Install `failRenameSyncOn(qaCoveragePath(root), "EACCES fake")` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js, with `qaCoveragePath` from ../src/paths.js, and undo it in a `finally`. Assert that `outcome.result` is `"queued"`, that `queueDepth(root)` is 1, that `readQaCoverage(root)` deep-equals `{}`, and that `calls.warnings` holds exactly one entry matching `/qa flow "unit tests" not recorded: EACCES fake/`.

The outcome is `no_change`, `readQaCoverage(root)` deep-equals `{}`, and `warns` is exactly one entry matching `/qa flow "status" not recorded: EACCES fake/`.

### Image-probe cache: a foreign entry in `image-probes.json` is dropped on read instead of throwing out of `tumwater status`, the dashboards' snapshot and the doctor, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/doctor/image-probe.ts + test/image-probe.test.ts + test/status-data-models.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

### Post-merge reviews: a torn `post-review.json` entry or a failed `post-review.json` write warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop or wedging the merge slot, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/review/post-merge-review.ts + test/post-merge-review.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `drainMergeQueue` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) calls `drainPostReviews` (src/merge/merge-post-review.ts) on every poll that is not held. The poll loop is a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so a throw there ends the team. The post-review file (src/review/post-merge-review.ts) can break the pipeline in three places:
- `readPostReviews` returns `saved.pending` without checking its entries. With `{"pending":[null]}`, `drainPostReviews` throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'rejected')` from `pending.find`, and it throws again on every later poll.
- `startRevert` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts) calls `settlePostReview` in the revert task's `.finally`, before `p.merge = null`. When that write throws, `guardMergeTask` swallows the rejection, but `p.merge` stays set, so `drainMerge` never starts another merge or revert.
- In `drainPostReviews`, the revert skip check's `.then` calls `settlePostReview` before its warning. When that write throws, the chain rejects with no handler (`void`), and the "not reverting" warning is never logged.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the first two with scratch tests (since deleted). The first wrote `{"pending":[null]}` and called `drainPostReviews`, which threw. The second used this file's `setup("VERDICT: reject\n1. bad")`, polled until `p.revert` was set, installed `failRenameSyncOn(postReviewPath(root), "pr write refused")`, then ran `drainMerge` and awaited `p.merge!.promise`. `p.merge` was still non-null afterwards.
All three writes go through `writePostReviews`. So does `addPostReview`, which `startMerge`'s `settleOne` calls before `settleMergeOutcome`: a throw there would skip writing back the merged change's outcome. This plan fixes the reader and that one writer, and does not edit src/merge/merge-drain.ts (the in-flight "Pending reverts" plan edits that file).

**Approach.** All code changes are in src/review/post-merge-review.ts.
1. `readPostReviews`: keep only entries that are JSON objects (`isJsonObject` from ../files/json-object.js) with a string `commit`, a string `role` and a string `summary`. Drop an entry whose `rejected` is present and not an array. Rebuild each kept entry: `body` only when it is a string, `failures` only when it is a finite number, and `rejected` (when it is an array) from its string elements only. Add a doc comment: a torn or hand-edited entry is dropped, and the next write leaves it out.
2. `writePostReviews`: wrap `writeJsonAtomic` in `try`/`catch`. The `catch` calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, TUMWATER_SOURCE, \`could not write post-review.json: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)`; import both names from ../events/events.js, which this file already imports `logEventBestEffort` from. Give `addPostReview` and `settlePostReview` one doc sentence each: they never throw, and a failed write warns and leaves the file as it was. What that costs: a missed add leaves the commit unreviewed, with the warning naming the failure. A missed settle after an approval or a failed run means the commit is reviewed again. A missed settle after a revert keeps the rejected entry, and the next poll's `revertSkipReason` finds that its revert already merged and settles it.
3. Leave src/merge/merge-post-review.ts and src/merge/merge-drain.ts unchanged. Step 2 is what fixes their call sites.
4. test/post-merge-review.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `postReviewPath` from ../src/paths.js (the file already imports `rejectedRefName` and `mergeRefName` from there). Reuse `setup` and `drainUntilRevert`, and undo every fault in a `finally`. Append:
   - "a torn post-review.json entry is dropped and the well-formed one is still reviewed": `setup("VERDICT: approve\n1. fine")`, then overwrite `postReviewPath(root)` with `{ pending: [null, { commit: 7 }, { commit, role: "improve", summary: "s", rejected: "x" }, { commit, role: "improve", summary: "add x", failures: "2", rejected: ["r", 3] }] }`. `readPostReviews(root)` deep-equals `[{ commit, role: "improve", summary: "add x", rejected: ["r"] }]`. Then rewrite the file with that torn list minus its last entry, plus `{ commit, role: "improve", summary: "add x" }`. `drainPostReviews(ctx, p)` does not throw, `p.postReview` is non-null, and once its promise is awaited `readPostReviews(root)` is empty.
   - "a failed post-review.json write after a revert warns and still frees the merge slot": the scratch-test scenario above. After awaiting `p.merge!.promise`, `p.merge` is null, `readPostReviews(root)` still has one entry, and one `warning` event (`eventsOfType`, already imported) has source `tumwater` and a message containing `pr write refused`.
   - "a failed post-review.json write in the revert skip check still logs why it does not revert": `setup("VERDICT: approve\n1. fine")`, then overwrite the file with `{ pending: [{ commit, role: "director", summary: "s", rejected: ["r"] }] }`. `revertSkipReason` returns "the director merged it" before any git call. Install the fault, call `drainPostReviews(ctx, p)`, then poll (sleep 10 ms, up to 200 times) until a `warning` event's message contains `not reverting`. Assert that it appears, and that another warning contains `pr write refused`.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) drop step 1's filter — the torn-entry test throws; (ii) remove step 2's `try` — the revert test finds `p.merge` non-null, and the skip-check test never sees `not reverting`. Put in VERIFIED only what you saw.
5. docs/invariants.md: append "## Post-merge reviews: post-review.json never throws out of the merge drain" after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BQ had merged, BR (Poll-loop runner state) and BS (Pending reverts) were planned, and BT was free. Use the Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout:
   - 1: an entry that is not an object with a string commit, role and summary is dropped, as is one whose `rejected` is not an array. Binds `readPostReviews`. Pinned by the torn-entry test.
   - 2: a failed post-review.json write warns under `tumwater` and never throws, so a revert's settle still frees the merge slot and a skip check still logs its reason. Binds `writePostReviews`, `addPostReview`, `settlePostReview`. Pinned by the revert and skip-check tests, plus "a rejecting post-merge review reverts the commit and hands it back as a revision" (on the healthy path the entry is still dropped).
   Cite each test by its full name.

### Pending reverts: a torn `reverted.json` entry, a failed hand-back save or a failed `reverted.json` rewrite warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/merge/merge-drain.ts + test/main-revert.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** Every poll that is not held runs `pollMergeDrain` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts) → `drainMergeQueue` → `assignPendingReverts` (src/merge/merge-drain.ts). The orchestrator's poll loop is a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so a throw there ends the team. `assignPendingReverts` has three unguarded throws:
- `pendingReverts` returns `saved.reverted` without checking its entries. An entry of `null` makes `handBackRevert` throw on `pending.role`. An entry whose `reasons` is not an array throws in `recordRevertedChange` (`reasons.map`, src/merge/merge-core.ts).
- `handBackRevert` calls `saveRunnerState(ctx.root, taker.state)` with no guard.
- The `writeJsonAtomic(revertedPendingPath(ctx.root), { reverted: left })` rewrite has no guard.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed the first two with a scratch test (since deleted). In a temp root with no git repo, with runners `[fakeRunner("improve")]` (test/main-revert.test.ts's helper), `assignPendingReverts` rejects when reverted.json holds `{"reverted":[null]}`. It also rejects with "state write refused" when the file holds one well-formed entry for `improve` and `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "state write refused")` is installed.
A save that fails after `recordRevertedChange` has set `taker.state.revision` leaves the in-memory runner holding the revision. A failed rewrite then leaves the entry in the file. Today nothing stops the next poll from handing that same commit to a free sibling instance as well, so this plan also makes the hand-back skip a commit some runner already took.

**Approach.** All code changes are in src/merge/merge-drain.ts, which already imports `warnEventBestEffort`, `TUMWATER_SOURCE`, `errorMessage` and `writeJsonAtomic`.
1. `pendingReverts`: keep only entries that are JSON objects (use `isJsonObject`; find its module with grep and import it) with a string `commit`, a string `role`, and an array `reasons`. ### Poll-loop runner state: a skip-reason, claim-release or main_red re-queue save that fails warns and moves on instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a section for it (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/runner/runner-state.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts + src/merge/merge-slot.ts + test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts + test/merge-requeue.test.ts + docs/invariants.md) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The orchestrator's poll loop (`while (!signal.aborted)` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) runs inside a `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, so any throw from a poll step ends the team (`stopCause` stays `"error"`). Three poll-step writes of a runner's state file call `saveRunnerState` (src/runner/runner-state.ts, a `writeJsonAtomic`) with no guard:
- `noteSkip` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, which `pollRunnerReasons` calls whenever a role's skip reason changes;
- the claim-release save in `pollRunnerReasons` (`r.state.claim = undefined; saveRunnerState(root, r.state)`);
- both saves in `requeueMainRedPin` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts), which `pollMergeDrain` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts) calls for every runner, plus its `enqueueRetry` → `enqueueMerge` queue write.
On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted): in the existing claim-hold setup ("a sibling held by an unclaimed mid-entry runner records claim-hold, cleared once admitted"), making the rename of `statePath(root, "feature-2")` fail with `failRenameSyncOn` (test/helpers/fs-faults.ts) makes `pollRunnerReasons` reject with that error. A full disk (ENOSPC), a read-only `.tumwater/state` (EACCES) or a state path replaced by a directory reaches the poll loop the same way. The in-memory state is already updated before each of these saves, and the next successful save of that runner (its run end, or the next change) writes it, so a failed save loses nothing the team needs to keep running. The events feed beside these saves is already best-effort ("a claim release survives an unwritable events feed").

**Approach.**
1. src/runner/runner-state.ts: add `export function saveRunnerStateBestEffort(root: string, state: RunnerState): void` beside `saveRunnerState`. It calls `saveRunnerState` in a `try`; the `catch` calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, state.role, \`could not save the role's state: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` (import `warnEventBestEffort` from ../events/events.js and `errorMessage` from ../text/text.js; events.ts does not import runner-state, so there is no cycle). Doc comment: for writes in the orchestrator's poll loop, which has no catch; the in-memory state stays ahead of the file until the runner's next successful save. Leave `saveRunnerState` itself strict: run-end and CLI callers keep their errors.
2. src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts: `noteSkip` and the claim-release save in `pollRunnerReasons` call `saveRunnerStateBestEffort` instead of `saveRunnerState`. If `saveRunnerState` is then unused in the file, drop it from the import.
3. src/merge/merge-slot.ts, `requeueMainRedPin`: both `saveRunnerState(root, state)` calls become `saveRunnerStateBestEffort`. Wrap the final `enqueueRetry(root, retryEntry(kept.entry, sha, "main_red"))` in `try`/`catch` that calls `warnEventBestEffort(root, kept.entry.role, \`the kept main_red change could not be re-queued: ${errorMessage(err)}\`)` (import what is missing; check the file's existing imports first). Do not restore `state.mainRedRetry` on that failure: the role's leftover recovery re-queues a kept pin with no record, as `requeueKeptChange`'s doc says ("leftover recovery stays the backstop"). Extend `requeueMainRedPin`'s doc comment with one sentence: it never throws, since the poll loop calls it with no catch. Leave `requeueKeptChange` alone: it runs when a merge settles, not in the poll body.
4. test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js and `eventsOfType` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js (that module is already imported for `unwritableEvents`/`writeEvents`). Append two tests; undo each fault in a `finally`:
   - "a skip reason that cannot be saved warns and leaves the poll running": the claim-hold setup above, with `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "feature-2"), "state write refused")` installed before the poll. `pollRunnerReasons` resolves; `feature2.state.skipReason` is `"claim-hold"`; one `warning` event has source `feature-2` and a message containing `state write refused`.
   - "a claim release that cannot be saved warns and leaves the poll running": the "a claim release survives an unwritable events feed" setup (first poll assigns `beta` to feature-2, then `config.roles.feature = { enabled: true, instances: 1 }`), with the same fault on feature-2's state path before the second poll. It resolves and `feature2.state.claim` is undefined. `failRenameSyncOn` fails only the first matching rename, so do not assert on the file's contents.
5. test/merge-requeue.test.ts: import `failRenameSyncOn` and `patchFsMethod` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js, `statePath` and `mergeQueueDir` from ../src/paths.js. Append two tests built like "a main_red pin is re-queued once main's head moves, and not before" (`pinnedEntry`, `settleMergeOutcome(..., "main_red", ...)`, `noteGreenBaseline` on a moved head); install each fault after the settle and undo it in a `finally`:
   - "a main_red re-queue whose state save fails still queues the change": `failRenameSyncOn(statePath(root, "improve"), "state write refused")`. `requeueMainRedPin` resolves, `queuedMerges(root)` holds the entry with `retry: "main_red"`, and `state.mainRedRetry` is undefined.
   - "a main_red re-queue whose queue write fails warns instead of throwing": `patchFsMethod("renameSync", (orig) => (a, b) => { if (typeof b === "string" && b.startsWith(mergeQueueDir(root))) throw new Error("queue write refused"); return orig(a, b); })` (check `FsCall`'s type in fs-faults.ts and adapt the wrapper's signature to it). `requeueMainRedPin` resolves, `queuedMerges(root)` is empty, and a `warning` event's message contains `queue write refused`.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) `noteSkip` back to `saveRunnerState` — the skip-reason test rejects; (ii) the claim release back to `saveRunnerState` — the claim-release test rejects; (iii) `requeueMainRedPin`'s clearing save back to `saveRunnerState` — the state-save test rejects; (iv) the enqueue `try` removed — the queue-write test rejects. Claim in VERIFIED only what you saw.

For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries.    - 2: `requeueMainRedPin` never throws: a failed state save still re-queues the change, and a failed queue write warns and leaves the kept pin to the role's leftover recovery. ### Session retention: an OpenCode DB directory that cannot be created skips only the OpenCode session deletes instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a session-retention section (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/orchestrator/retention.ts + test/retention.test.ts + docs/invariants.md; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `RetentionPruner.prune` (src/orchestrator/retention.ts) calls `ensureParentDir(dbPath)` for `opencodeDbPath(root)` first, before any pruning, with no catch. It runs from the `RetentionPruner` constructor at startup (`new RetentionPruner(root, config.sessionRetentionDays)` in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) and from `RetentionPruner.poll` in the poll loop (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts). The `pruneOldFiles` doc comment in src/files/files.ts says a throw escaping this pass "would end the whole team". On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted): when `.tumwater/opencode` is a regular file, `new RetentionPruner(root, 7)` throws EEXIST, and so does `poll(root, 7)` on a pruner built with 0. A 30-day-old file in `toolOutputDir(root)` survives, because the throw comes before the file pass. A read-only `.tumwater` (EACCES) or a full disk (ENOSPC on the mkdir) leaves through the same call. A team that has never run OpenCode still pays this cost, because the directory is created unconditionally. If that directory cannot be created, the OpenCode DB cannot exist either, so no `opencode session delete` could succeed. Skipping the deletes loses nothing. docs/invariants.md has no section on retention.ts: `grep -n -i retention docs/invariants.md` finds nothing.

**Approach.**
1. src/orchestrator/retention.ts, `RetentionPruner.prune`: make `bin` a `let`. Wrap `ensureParentDir(dbPath)` in `try { … } catch { bin = undefined; }`. With no `bin`, `pruneOpencodeSessions` skips the session deletes but still prunes the spill dir. The file pass and the ledger line pass then run as before. Add a short comment: the directory cannot be created, so no OpenCode DB is there to delete from, and this pass runs in the poll loop, where a throw ends the team. Use plain vocabulary (no "tick", no "loop" for role). Change nothing else in src/.
2. test/retention.test.ts: append one test, "RetentionPruner: an OpenCode DB dir that cannot be created skips the session deletes and still prunes the rest". Write a regular file at `path.dirname(opencodeDbPath(root))` (import `opencodeDbPath` from ../src/paths.js; create its parent first). Add a 30-day-old file in `toolOutputDir(root)` with the existing `staleFile` helper. Record a 30-day-old `opencode` session with `recordSession`, as the idle-role test does, and point `TUMWATER_OPENCODE_BIN` at a `writeScript` capture bin, deleting the variable in a `finally`. Then:
   - `assert.doesNotThrow(() => new RetentionPruner(root, 7))`. The tool-output file is gone, and the capture log does not exist (no delete was attempted).
   - Make a new stale tool-output file. `const p = new RetentionPruner(root, 0)`, then `assert.doesNotThrow(() => p.poll(root, 7))`. The file is gone.
   Do not assert on the spill dir: `opencodeSpillDir` points under `os.homedir()` and is `""` for a root without commits.
   Mutations, each applied by hand and reverted: (i) remove the try/catch. The constructor throws EEXIST. (ii) Keep the catch but leave its body empty, so `bin` is not cleared. The capture log then holds `session delete`, and the test fails. Check whether any other test in test/retention.test.ts catches either mutation, and claim in VERIFIED only what you saw.
3. docs/invariants.md: append "## Session retention: the once-per-day gate, a re-prune on a window change, and a prune pass that never throws" after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BO had merged, BP was planned (Session ledger) and BQ was free. Use the existing Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout:
   - 1: a prune is due when the window is positive and a full day has passed since the last prune or none has run; a window of 0 disables pruning; startup prunes at once. Binds `dueForPrune` and the `RetentionPruner` constructor. Pinned by "dueForPrune: the once-per-day gate with fake timestamps", "RetentionPruner: construction runs the startup prune at a positive window" and "RetentionPruner: retention 0 disables the startup prune".
   - 2: a change in the live window logs one `retention_changed` per distinct value and re-prunes at once, even inside the daily window. Binds `RetentionPruner.poll`. Pinned by "RetentionPruner: poll re-prunes immediately on a window change and logs one event".
   - 3: the OpenCode purge reads a ledger before the file pass can age it out. Binds `RetentionPruner.prune`'s order. Pinned by "RetentionPruner: an idle role's expired opencode session is purged before its ledger ages out".
   - 4: a prune pass never throws. An unwritable event feed costs only its warnings, and an OpenCode DB directory that cannot be created costs only the OpenCode session deletes. Binds `RetentionPruner.prune` and `warnEventBestEffort`. Pinned by "RetentionPruner: a window change and a prune survive an unwritable events feed" and the new test. If the Session ledger plan's section (planned as INV-BP) has merged by then, add one sentence pointing to its ledger-rewrite guarantee. Otherwise, say nothing about the ledger rewrite.

### Session ledger: a retention trim that cannot rewrite a ledger leaves it as it was instead of throwing out of the poll loop, and docs/invariants.md gains a session-ledger section (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches src/agent/session-ledger.ts + docs/invariants.md + a new test/session-ledger-prune.test.ts)

**Goal.** `pruneSessionLedgers` (src/agent/session-ledger.ts) rewrites each ledger that lost a line with `writeTextAtomic`, and nothing catches a failure of that write. Its one caller is `RetentionPruner.prune` (src/orchestrator/retention.ts). That runs from the `RetentionPruner` constructor at startup (src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts) and from `RetentionPruner.poll` inside the poll loop (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts). The loop "and its finally run with no catch" (the `bestEffortEventLogger` comment in src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts), and `walkFiles`' doc comment in src/files/files.ts says that a throw escaping the retention pass "would end the whole team". So a full disk (ENOSPC on the temp file) or a read-only session dir holding one stale ledger line stops the team, or keeps it from starting. A full disk is the case where retention matters most. On 2026-10-20 the plan role confirmed with a scratch test (since deleted):
- a stale line in a session dir chmodded 0o555 makes `pruneSessionLedgers` throw EACCES;
- with `withThrowingFs("writeFileSync", errnoError("ENOSPC"), …)` (test/helpers/fs-faults.ts) it throws ENOSPC, and the ledger's bytes are unchanged and no temp file is left behind (`writeAtomic` removes it);
- a ledger with nothing past the window is not rewritten: its mtime and inode are unchanged;
- a ledger whose every line ages out stays in place as an empty file; a line whose `at` is not a number (`"x"`) counts as pruned;
- `hasResumableSession` is false for a missing dir and for a dir holding only `sessions.jsonl`, and true once another `.jsonl` file exists;
- `recordSession` into a path under a regular file does not throw, and `readSessions` of it is `[]`;
- `pruneOpencodeSessions` with no `bin` returns 0 and still deletes an old spill file; with a `bin` that exits 1 it returns 0; with a `bin` path that does not exist it returns 0 and does not throw.
docs/invariants.md names none of session-ledger.ts's functions. test/session-ledger.test.ts covers the record/read round trip, the resume selection and the main prune path, but none of the points above.

**Approach.**
1. src/agent/session-ledger.ts, `pruneSessionLedgers`: count the lines dropped from one file in a local, and add it to `pruned` only after that file's `writeTextAtomic` succeeds. Wrap the write in `try { … } catch { return; }`, matching the best-effort catches already in this module. A ledger that cannot be rewritten keeps all its lines and adds nothing to the count, so the `pruned N stale session ledger line(s)` warning in retention.ts never claims lines that are still there. Extend the doc comment by one sentence: a ledger that cannot be rewritten (a full disk, a read-only dir) is left as it was and not counted, because this pass runs in the orchestrator's poll loop, where a throw ends the team. Use plain vocabulary (no "tick", "loop" for role, "landing"); src/agent/ is already under the vocabulary guard. Change nothing else in src/.
2. New test/session-ledger-prune.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/session-ledger.test.ts. Import from ../src/agent/session-ledger.js, plus `tmpdir` and `skipIfRoot` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, `errnoError`, `withThrowingFs` and `withReadOnlyDir` from ./helpers/fs-faults.js, and `writeScript` from ./fakes/fake-commands.js. Build records inline, as test/session-ledger.test.ts's `record` helper does. Tests:
   a. "pruneSessionLedgers leaves a ledger it cannot rewrite as it was and counts nothing for it": record one line 30 days old and one fresh. Run `pruneSessionLedgers(root, 7)` inside `withThrowingFs("writeFileSync", errnoError("ENOSPC"), …)` under `assert.doesNotThrow`. Expect a return of 0, ledger bytes equal to those read before, and `fs.readdirSync(dir)` equal to `["sessions.jsonl"]`. Then a second case with `withReadOnlyDir(dir, …)`, guarded by `if (skipIfRoot(t)) return;`, with the same expectations. Then call it again with no fault: it returns 1 and `readSessions` holds only the fresh record. Mutation: remove the try/catch around the write. Both cases then throw.
   b. "pruneSessionLedgers does not rewrite a ledger with nothing past the window": one fresh record; set the ledger's mtime 3 days back with `fs.utimesSync`. Expect a return of 0 and the same `mtimeMs` and `ino`. Mutation: change `if (kept.length !== lines.length)` to `if (true)`.
   c. "pruneSessionLedgers empties a fully stale ledger in place and ages out a non-numeric stamp": one 30-day-old record plus one appended line that is valid JSON whose `at` is the current time as a string (`String(Date.now())`). Expect a return of 2, the file still existing, and its size 0. Mutation: change `typeof at === "number" && at >= cutoff` to `(at as number) >= cutoff`. JavaScript coerces the numeric string, so the string line is kept and the return is 1. A non-numeric string such as `"x"` would not catch this mutation, because `"x" >= cutoff` is false either way.
   d. "hasResumableSession counts a backend session file but never the ledger itself": a missing dir gives false; after `recordSession`, false; after writing `s.jsonl` beside it, true. Mutation: drop `&& f !== SESSION_LEDGER_FILE`.

### docs/invariants.md gains an orchestrator-info section, and one new test file pins that a publish writes once for a changed batch, never for an unchanged one, and warns rather than throws when the file cannot be written (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/orchestrator-info-publish.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `publishInfoFields` (src/team/orchestrator-info.ts) is the only way the orchestrator's poll publishes the info file that status, the TUI, the GUI and `tumwater start`'s second-team check read. Its callers are src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts (permits, check permits, slot pool, build) and src/gates/gate-polls.ts (the budget fields, disk). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name orchestrator-info.ts or any of its functions, and no test imported `publishInfoFields`. test/orchestrator-info.test.ts pins the tolerant reader, the atomic writer and `orchestratorAlive`, but not the publish rules the function's doc comment promises:
- an unchanged batch leaves the file untouched and returns false (the comparison is by JSON serialization, so a fresh but equal object is not a change);
- every field in a batch is staged, with no short-circuit, and a changed batch is one write that holds all of them;
- publishing `undefined` for a present field removes it from the file;
- a write that fails (for example, the path is a directory) does not throw. It logs one `warning` reading "could not publish orchestrator info: …", the in-memory `info` keeps the new value, and the function still returns true. Publishing the same value again returns false and does not retry. The doc comment says the field "is retried the next time its value changes".
The plan role confirmed all four behaviors on 2026-10-20 with a scratch test, then deleted it. The scratch test made the write fail by `fs.mkdirSync` on `orchestratorStatePath(root)`; on darwin the rename failed with EISDIR.

**Approach.**
1. New test/orchestrator-info-publish.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/orchestrator-info.test.ts. Import `publishInfoFields`, `readOrchestratorInfo`, `writeOrchestratorInfo` and the `OrchestratorInfo` type from ../src/team/orchestrator-info.js, `orchestratorStatePath` from ../src/paths.js, `tmpdir` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js and `warningMessages` from ./fixtures/log-fixtures.js. Each test starts from `const info: OrchestratorInfo = { pid: 1, startedAt: 2, roles: ["feature"] }` and calls `writeOrchestratorInfo(root, info)`.
2. Test "publishInfoFields writes every field of a changed batch in one publish". Publish `[["stopsAt", 5], ["slotPool", { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`. Expect a return of true, and expect `readOrchestratorInfo(root)` to deep-equal `{ ...base, stopsAt: 5, slotPool: { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 } }`. Then publish `[["stopsAt", 5], ["slotPool", { leased: 2, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`, where only the second field changes, and expect the file to carry `leased: 2`. Mutation: replace the loop with `const changed = fields.some(([field, value]) => assignInfoFieldIfChanged(info, field, value));`. The first batch then stages only `stopsAt`.
3. Test "publishInfoFields leaves the file untouched when no field changed". After the step-2 style publish, `fs.rmSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))`. Then publish the same values again as fresh object literals, plus `["disk", undefined]` for a field that was never present. Expect a return of false, and expect `fs.existsSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))` to be false. Mutations: (a) `if (changed)` → `if (true)` before the write, which recreates the file; (b) in `assignInfoFieldIfChanged`, compare `value === info[field]` instead of the two `JSON.stringify` calls, which makes the fresh `slotPool` object a change.
4. Test "publishInfoFields removes a field published as undefined". Publish `[["slotPool", { leased: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }]]`, then `[["slotPool", undefined]]`. Expect the second call to return true, and expect the read-back file to have no `slotPool` key (`assert.equal("slotPool" in readOrchestratorInfo(root)!, false)`). Mutation: in `assignInfoFieldIfChanged`, add `if (value === undefined) return false;` as its first line.
5. Test "publishInfoFields warns instead of throwing when the info file cannot be written". `fs.rmSync` the file and `fs.mkdirSync(orchestratorStatePath(root))`. Publish `[["stopsAt", 9]]`, wrapped in `assert.doesNotThrow`. Expect a return of true, `info.stopsAt === 9`, and exactly one message in `warningMessages(root)` that starts with "could not publish orchestrator info: ". Publish `[["stopsAt", 9]]` again. Expect false, with still exactly one such warning. Mutation: add `throw err;` after the `warnEventBestEffort(...)` call in `writeOrchestratorInfoBestEffort`. This type-checks and keeps every import used.
   Run the new file once. Before writing VERIFIED, apply each mutation by hand, check that it fails its new test, and check that the test passes again once you revert it. Also run test/orchestrator-info.test.ts and test/gate-polls.test.ts under each mutation, and drop any claim that only the new tests catch a mutation that one of them also catches.
6. docs/invariants.md: append "## Orchestrator info: a publish writes once for a changed batch and never for an unchanged one, a failed write warns rather than throws, and a reader drops a wrong-shaped field" at the end, after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BK had merged, BL, BM and BN were planned, and BO was free. Follow the existing Guarantee / Binds / Pinned by layout:

   - 2: A publish never throws: a failed write logs one `warning`, keeps the new value in memory, and is not retried until the value changes again. Startup's `writeOrchestratorInfo` stays strict and atomic. Binds `publishInfoFields`, `writeOrchestratorInfoBestEffort`, `writeOrchestratorInfo`. Pinned by the step-5 test plus "writeOrchestratorInfo leaves the previous file intact when a write is killed mid-flight" (test/orchestrator-info.test.ts).
   - 3: `readOrchestratorInfo` returns null for a missing, torn or non-object file, and drops each nested field whose shape is foreign while it keeps well-formed ones; `orchestratorAlive` is false with no info. Binds `readOrchestratorInfo`, `normalizeInfoFields`, `orchestratorAlive`. Pinned by "readOrchestratorInfo returns null for missing, torn, and non-object files", "readOrchestratorInfo drops nested fields with a foreign shape and keeps well-formed ones", "readOrchestratorInfo round-trips a well-formed providerHolds and drops foreign entries" and "orchestratorAlive is false with no info and reflects pid liveness otherwise" (test/orchestrator-info.test.ts), and "pollTeamGates publishes the measured disk state for observers" (test/gate-polls.test.ts).

### docs/invariants.md gains a git-diff-paths section, and one new test file pins that a tree diff tells an unreadable answer from an empty one, lists both ends of a move, and decodes non-ASCII names (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/git-diff-paths.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** src/git/git-diff.ts turns git's diff output into paths and capped diffs. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md did not name git-diff.ts or any of its functions. test/git-diff.test.ts covers `changedFiles`, `unquotePorcelainPath`, `aheadOfMainDiff` and the range of `aheadOfMainFiles`, but before this entry no test called `treeDiffFiles` directly. The merge path depends on it: `exemptTreeDelta` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) decides whether a stack is review-exempt, and the overwrite-blocker check in src/merge/merge-git.ts reads it. Three documented guarantees have no test that would catch them breaking:
- `treeDiffFiles` returns null when git fails (an unknown commit), and `[]` for identical trees. `exemptTreeDelta` relies on this, because "an unreadable diff is not exempt" only holds while null is kept separate from `[]`.
- `treeDiffFiles` passes `--no-renames`, so a file moved from `src/` to `docs/` lists both its old and its new path. With git's default rename detection, `git diff --name-only` lists only `docs/x.md`. The plan role checked this in a scratch repo on 2026-10-20. A code-to-docs move would then read as a docs-only, review-exempt delta.
- `treeDiffFiles` and `aheadOfMainFiles` decode git's C-quoted names. Under the default `core.quotePath`, `héllo.md` comes out as `"h\303\251llo.md"` (checked the same way), which is not a real path and does not match a `*.md` exemption.

**Approach.**
1. New test/git-diff-paths.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/git-diff.test.ts. Import `treeDiffFiles` and `aheadOfMainFiles` from ../src/git/git-diff.js, `commitAll` from ../src/git/git.js and `ensureWorktree` from ../src/git/worktree.js. Import `makeRepo`, `seedCommit` and `sh` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js. Use real git throughout, as test/git-diff.test.ts does.
2. Test "treeDiffFiles is null for an unknown commit and empty for identical trees". Use `makeRepo()`. Assert that `await treeDiffFiles(repo, "deadbeef", "HEAD")` is `null`, and that `await treeDiffFiles(repo, "HEAD", "HEAD")` deep-equals `[]`. Mutation: replace `out === null ? null : gitLines(out).map(unquotePorcelainPath)` with `gitLines(out).map(unquotePorcelainPath)`. This type-checks and returns `[]` for the unknown commit.
3. Test "treeDiffFiles lists a moved file under both its old and its new path". Use `makeRepo()` and `seedCommit(repo, "src/x.ts", ...)`, after first creating `src/` with `fs.mkdirSync`, because seedCommit writes the file directly. Then `fs.mkdirSync(docs)` and run `sh(repo, "git", "mv", "src/x.ts", "docs/x.md")` and `sh(repo, "git", "commit", "-m", "move")`. **Goal.** src/run/run-timing.ts holds the timing seams the orchestrator's poll loop and shutdown use. `runTimedRoleRun` returns the drain's p75 sample, `p75RunDurationMs` turns the samples into the drain window, and `drainInFlightWork` and `awaitMergeForHandoff` bound a restart's wait on the merge in flight. test/orchestrator-seams.test.ts and test/run-timing.test.ts cover most of their documented edges. Every restart test in test/run-timing.test.ts passes a single task. Swapping in `Promise.race(inFlight.map((t) => t.promise))` would let a restart hand off while a second merge task is still running. Taking `inFlight[0]!.roles` would leave the other tasks' roles out of the announcement. No test would notice either change.

Assert that `timers.delays` deep-equals `[5_000]`. Resolve t1 and `await flushImmediate()`. Assert that the drain has not returned and that `timers.pending()` is 1. Resolve t2 and await the drain. Assert that `aborts` is 0 and that `timers.pending()` is 0. Assert exactly one warning, matching `/^restart waiting on the merge in progress for clean, dedupe \(deadline 5s\)$/`. Mutations: (a) replace `Promise.allSettled(inFlight.map((t) => t.promise)).then(() => {})` with `Promise.race(inFlight.map((t) => t.promise))`; (b) replace `inFlight.flatMap((t) => t.roles)` with `inFlight[0]!.roles`. Both type-check.

### docs/invariants.md gains a staging self-check section, and one new test file pins that each git-level finding stops at its cap and says how many it left out (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/stage-path-caps.test.ts)

**Goal.** `gitLevelFindings` (src/run/stage-path-checks.ts) is the git-level half of the pre-commit self-check: `stageCheckFindings` (src/run/stage-check.ts) calls it, and the findings go back to the author's still-open session. Each finding is meant to stay bounded however large the change is. The caps are `MAX_STALE_PATHS` (stale-reference findings per change), `MAX_STALE_HITS` (`file:line` hits per stale reference), `MAX_MISSING_PATHS` and `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES` (all 10). `cappedList` appends `moreSuffix` (src/text/phrases.ts, ` (+N more)`) for what a missing-path or lost-newline finding leaves out. Before this entry, no test in test/stage-check.test.ts makes a change that exceeds any of these caps, and docs/invariants.md named neither stage-path-checks.ts nor `gitLevelFindings`. A regression that dropped a cap would send a 40-file rename's whole reference list into the session's prompt, and none of the tests would notice.

**Approach.**
1. New test/stage-path-caps.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/stage-check.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files. Copy that file's small `repoWith(files)` helper (`makeRepo`, `sh` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, `ensureWorktree(root, "improve", "main")` from ../src/git/worktree.js). Call `gitLevelFindings(wt, "main")` directly. Use two-digit, zero-padded names (`00`…`11`) so git's path order matches the numeric order and no name is a prefix of another.
2. Test "a missing-path finding names the first ten paths and counts the rest". Base: `src/keep.ts` and `README.md` (`Start.\n`). In the worktree, append twelve lines `See src/x/f00.ts.` … `See src/x/f11.ts.` to README.md. Assert exactly one finding. It contains `src/x/f09.ts`, does not contain `src/x/f10.ts`, and ends with ` (+2 more)`. Mutation: `MAX_MISSING_PATHS = 11`.
3. Test "a lost-final-newline finding names the first ten files and counts the rest". Base: `src/n00.ts` … `src/n10.ts`, each `export const n = 1;\n`. In the worktree, rewrite each without its trailing newline. Assert one finding matching `/removes the final newline from: /`. It contains `src/n09.ts`, does not contain `src/n10.ts`, and ends with ` (+1 more)`. Mutation: `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES = 11`.
4. Test "a change deleting more referenced paths than the cap reports only the cap's worth". Base: `src/d00.ts` … `src/d10.ts` (`export const d = 1;\n`), plus README.md with one line `See src/dNN.ts.` per file. Delete all eleven in the worktree. Assert that the findings matching `/ was deleted but is still named at: /` number exactly 10. Mutation: `MAX_STALE_PATHS = 11`.
5. Test "one stale reference lists at most ten of its hits". Base: `src/d.ts` plus a `docs/guide.md` naming `src/d.ts` on twelve separate lines. Delete `src/d.ts`. Assert one finding, and `/docs\/guide\.md:\d+/g` matches it exactly 10 times. Mutation: `MAX_STALE_HITS = 11`.
   Run the new file once. Before you write VERIFIED, apply each named mutation by hand (each is a one-constant edit that type-checks). Check that it fails its own new test, and that the test passes again once you revert it. Also run test/stage-check.test.ts under each mutation. If a test fails there too, drop any claim that only the new tests catch it.
6. docs/invariants.md: append "## Staging self-check: each git-level finding stops at its cap, and a check that cannot run adds nothing" at the end, after the last section. For the INV prefix, run `grep -n '^### INV-' docs/invariants.md | tail` and read the "was free" notes in PLANS.md's Planned entries. On 2026-10-20, BH, BI and BJ were planned and BK was free. Entries:
   - 1: the step-2 to step-5 rule. A finding names at most 10 paths, files or hits, and a missing-path or lost-newline finding counts the rest as ` (+N more)`. A change emits at most 10 stale-reference findings. Binds `gitLevelFindings`, `cappedList`, the `MAX_*` constants. Pinned by the four new tests.
   - 2: the git-level checks are best-effort, and the index is restored. A failed git command adds no finding and does not throw. `gitLevelFindings` resets the index to HEAD in `finally`, so the run's change detection still sees the worktree. Binds `gitLevelFindings`, `stageCheckFindings` (its `.catch(() => [])`). Pinned by "a git failure yields no findings instead of throwing", "the git-level check leaves the index clean, so change detection still sees the worktree" and "a clean change yields no findings" (test/stage-check.test.ts).

### docs/invariants.md gains a batch-merge section, and one new test file pins that a stack seeds main's baseline only when a full check passed on exactly the merged tip (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md + a new test/merge-stack-seed.test.ts) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** `mergeStack` (src/merge/merge-stack.ts) merges a batch of approved changes. It cherry-picks them onto main's tip, runs ONE scope-`batch` check over the combined tree, and fast-forwards main through the captured shas (`ffStackToMain`). When main moves mid-check, it re-stacks, up to `BATCH_RESTACK_ATTEMPTS` times. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named neither file nor function (`grep -c 'merge-stack\|mergeStack' docs/invariants.md` gave 0). After a merge, `mergeStack` calls `noteGreenBaseline(seed)` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts). That records the tip as green in the cache the main watch and the redeployer read. `seed` is set only when the batch check status is `"passed"` and `mergeCommandOf(ctx.config) === undefined`. A doc-only stack, a stack whose failures are all main's known failures (`onlyKnownMainFailures`), and a `check.mergeCommand` green seed nothing. Before this entry, no test read `cachedBaselineVerdict` after a batch merge: `grep -n cachedBaselineVerdict test/merger-*.test.ts test/merge-stack.test.ts` gave nothing. A regression that seeded a known-red or unchecked tip as green would skip the main watch's check on that tip and go unnoticed.

**Approach.**
1. New test/merge-stack-seed.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/merger-bisect.test.ts, test/merger-restack.test.ts or test/merge-stack.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files. Imports: `cachedBaselineVerdict` from ../src/baseline/main-baseline.js, `createMainWatch` from ../src/baseline/main-watch.js, `defaultConfig` from ../src/config/config.js, `mainSha` from ./fixtures/repo-fixtures.js, `withApprovePi` from ./fakes/fake-pi.js, and `batchFixture`, `runBatch`, `batchChecks`, `declareCheck`, `checkAfterGates`, `verifyThenMerge`, `makeBatchCtx`, `request` from ./fixtures/merger-fixtures.js. Copy the setup shapes from the merger-bisect.test.ts tests named below. Each test uses roles `["alpha", "beta"]` and first asserts that both results are `"changed"`.
2. Test "a stack whose batch check passed seeds the merged tip green". `checkAfterGates(root, 2, "true")`, then `runBatch`. ### docs/invariants.md gains a review-verdict and revision-finality section, and two tests pin that only a leading `(prior N)` with N ≥ 1 is a repeat tag and that a tag with no matching prior count still counts one revision (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md, a comment in src/merge/merge-core.ts + a new test/revision-prior-tags.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** The review gate depends on two things. First, src/review/review-verdict.ts's `parseVerdict` turns the reviewer's reply into a verdict and its reasons. It fails closed when no verdict line exists, and the last VERDICT line wins. It caps the reasons at `MAX_REASONS` and drops a leading prior-objection resolution from a rejection. Second, src/merge/merge-core.ts's `recordRejectedChange` uses `priorObjectionNumber` to decide when a revision chain ends. Each reason gets a persistence count: 0 for an untagged reason, and `1 + prior[n - 1] ?? 0` for a `(prior N)` restatement. The rejection is final when any count reaches `REVISION_FINAL_ON_REPEAT` or the round reaches `REVISION_BACKSTOP` (both in src/runner/revision.ts). Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named none of `parseVerdict`, `priorObjectionNumber`, `recordRejectedChange` or the two constants. Two edges are untested:
- No test calls `priorObjectionNumber` directly. Its only coverage is the `(prior 1)` reply in test/revision.test.ts's "a rejection whose objection has survived two revisions is final and deletes the rejected ref". Nothing pins the `^` anchor (a tag mid-line is not a tag), the case-insensitive match, the leading-whitespace trim, or the `n >= 1` guard.
- Two cases are untested: a `(prior N)` tag whose N is beyond the prior list, and a tag with no `priorCounts` at all (a recovery merge, or a first rejection). In both, `prior[n - 1] ?? 0` gives a count of 1. That is not final this round, but one more restatement makes it final. The doc comment on `recordRejectedChange` says such a tag "reads as a fresh objection", which a reader takes to mean count 0. The code gives 1, so the comment is corrected to match the code. The behavior does not change.

**Approach.**
1. New test/revision-prior-tags.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/revision.test.ts or test/review-verdict.test.ts: the waiting "Plain terms code cleanup" parts may touch test files. Import `priorObjectionNumber` from ../src/review/review-verdict.js. Import `verifyRequest` from ../src/merge/merge-batch.js, `refSha` from ../src/git/git.js, `rejectedRefName` from ../src/paths.js and `freshRunnerState` from ../src/runner/runner-state.js. Import `withPi` from ./fakes/fake-pi.js, and `batchWiring`, `makeCtx`, `pinnedFixture`, `request`, `reviewerPi` and `ROLE` from ./fixtures/merger-fixtures.js. These are the same imports test/revision.test.ts uses.
2. Test "priorObjectionNumber reads only a leading (prior N) tag with N of at least one". `"(prior 3) still wrong"` → 3. `"  (PRIOR 2) still wrong"` → 2 (trimmed, case-insensitive). `"(prior 0) still wrong"` → null. `"prior to the change, x"` → null. `"see (prior 1) above"` → null. `"(prior one) x"` → null. Mutations: drop the `^` from the regex (the mid-line case returns 1); drop `&& n >= 1` (the zero case returns 0).
3. Test "a (prior N) tag beyond the prior list, or with no prior list, counts one revision and is not final". (a) Under `withPi(reviewerPi("VERDICT: reject\n1. (prior 3) a stale number"), …)`, take `pinnedFixture()`, `freshRunnerState(ROLE)`, `makeCtx` and `batchWiring` as the sibling tests do. Call `verifyRequest(ctx, request(sha, { revisionRound: 1, priorReview: { sha, reasons: ["the bug"], counts: [1] } }), w)`. Assert `verdict.kind` is `"result"`, `state.revision?.round` is 2, `state.revision?.reasonCounts` deep-equals `[1]`, `state.lastReview?.exhausted` is undefined, and `refSha(root, rejectedRefName(ROLE))` equals `state.revision?.sha`. (b) Do the same with a fresh fixture and state, the reply `"VERDICT: reject\n1. (prior 1) still wrong"` and `request(sha, { revisionRound: 1 })` (no `priorReview`). Assert the same: round 2, `reasonCounts` `[1]`, not exhausted. Mutation: in `recordRejectedChange`, change `prior[n - 1] ?? 0` to `prior[n - 1] ?? 1`. Both cases then reach count 2 and go final (`state.revision` undefined).

4. src/merge/merge-core.ts, comments only. In `recordRejectedChange`'s doc comment, replace "a `(prior N)` tag then reads as a fresh objection" with wording that matches the code: the tag counts as having survived one revision (count 1), so it is not final that round. Make the same correction to the inline comment's "An out-of-range or missing tag (a stale prior list, no prior round) reads as a fresh objection". Change no code.

### docs/invariants.md gains a flake-quarantine section, and three tests pin that a list at the parser's cap is never quarantined nor counted as only-quarantined, that the store keeps the 100 most recently seen tests and reads malformed entries as defaults, and that a missing BUGS.md releases nothing (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; independent of every eligible plan; touches docs/invariants.md, src/review/known-flakes.ts (one `export`) + a new test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** src/review/known-flakes.ts keeps the flake quarantine in `.tumwater/state/quarantine.json` (`quarantinePath`). `quarantineTests` adds a test that failed and then passed on the same tree. `onlyQuarantined` returns the failing tests when every one is quarantined. `markQuarantineFiled` and `releaseQuarantine` take a test out once its BUGS.md entry leaves `## Open`. Before this entry, docs/invariants.md named none of these functions (`grep -c known-flakes docs/invariants.md` gave 0, and no heading mentions quarantine). test/known-flakes.test.ts covers the basic add/repeat/release path, but these edges have no direct test:
- The `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` guard (src/build/build-check-report.ts) in both `quarantineTests` and `onlyQuarantined`. A list of that length may have been cut short, so it is neither recorded nor counted as only-quarantined. test/main-watch.test.ts's "a failing list at the parser's cap is never counted as only known failures" pins the same guard in main-watch's own `onlyKnownMainFailures`, not in `onlyQuarantined`. `onlyQuarantined` is called from src/baseline/main-watch.ts and src/baseline/main-culprit.ts.
- `saveQuarantine` keeps the `QUARANTINE_MAX` (100) entries with the newest `lastSeen` and drops the rest.
- `loadQuarantine` reads a malformed file as an empty list. It skips an entry without a string `test`, defaults a missing or zero `count` to 1, and defaults a non-string `bug` to `""`. `quarantineTests` counts a test named twice in one call once.
- `releaseQuarantine` releases nothing when BUGS.md is missing, even for a filed test.

**Approach.**
1. src/review/known-flakes.ts: export `QUARANTINE_MAX` so the test does not repeat the literal. Change nothing else.
2. New test/known-flakes-quarantine.test.ts (node:test + `node:assert/strict`). Do not edit test/known-flakes.test.ts. Write a fixture file with `fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(quarantinePath(root)), { recursive: true })` and then `fs.writeFileSync`.

Then call `quarantineTests(root, names.slice(0, -1), "out")` and `quarantineTests(root, names.slice(-1), "out")`, so that every name is listed. Assert `onlyQuarantined(root, names.slice(0, -1))?.length` is `FAILING_TESTS_MAX - 1` and `onlyQuarantined(root, names)` is null.
