It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes. It is independent of the in-flight invariants plans above. Each of them appends a section, so whichever merges later appends after the others.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the very end of docs/invariants.md, after whatever section is last at that point. Title it `## History rows: each merge verdict shows once, and missing evidence keeps the raw label`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intro under the backlog-archive section): `runRows` is the pure collector the CLI, the GUI and the tests share; `readRunRows` (the last-N view) and `readRunRowsSince` (`--since`) feed it. Use the letter `S`. `grep -n 'INV-S' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first; if it finds something, use the next free letter.
- Add five entries, each with **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.** like the existing ones. Before writing each guarantee, read the cited tests and the matching code, and state only what the code does. Where a detail below turns out to be wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-S1: a row's duration and model come only from its own run_start`. Guarantee: `runRows` pairs each run_end with its run_start through the shared `runStartMap`/`runStartModelMap` (src/events/event-read.ts). A row whose start is not in the read gets `durationMs: null` (a dash), never a made-up span, and its model is null when the start is absent or carries no model. Rows come back newest first, at most `limit` of them, filtered by role. Binds: src/history/history-data.ts (`runRows`, `RunRow`), src/events/event-read.ts (`runStartMap`, `runSpanMs`, `runStartModel`). Pinned by: test/history-data.test.ts "runRows pairs each run_end with its run_start for the duration", "runRows renders no duration when the run's start is outside the scanned window", "runRows names the model its run_start carried, or none when the start is absent or unnamed" and "runRows returns the newest limit rows, newest first, and filters by role".
  - `### INV-S2: the last-N view grows its window, and only up to a ceiling`. Guarantee: `readRunRows` re-reads with a four-times larger tail window while the rows fall short of `limit` or a row's start is unpaired, but only if the read filled the window. It stops at `HISTORY_SCAN_MAX_EVENTS`. `history -n` accepts only 1..`HISTORY_MAX_RUNS`. The per-ask window memo (`runRowWindowMemo`) only changes where the ladder starts, never which rows come back. Binds: src/history/history-data.ts (`readRunRows`, `HISTORY_SCAN_MAX_EVENTS`, `HISTORY_MAX_RUNS`). Pinned by: test/cli-history.test.ts "history grows the scan window to pair a run_start the first window's boundary cut off", "history --role grows its scan window until it reaches the role's runs" and "history -n accepts 1..200 and fails zero, negative, non-numeric, and over-large values". If no test pins the memo's no-effect-on-rows claim, leave that sentence out rather than citing a test that does not check it.
  - `### INV-S3: a queued row reads its change's verdict, and each attempt's verdict shows on one row`. Guarantee: the authoring row takes the change's final verdict, walking forward through recovery re-enqueues (`isRecoveryPin`) and stopping at a pin that starts a fresh change. A recovery row takes the retriable verdict of the attempt it re-enqueued (`recoveredAttemptVerdict`). While a re-enqueued attempt is pending, the authoring row keeps "queued". The `claimTop` cursor hands each queued run the newest unclaimed pin at or before its end, so two runs never claim one pin. Binds: src/history/history-data.ts (`resolveQueuedResult`, `recoveredAttemptVerdict`, `isRecoveryPin`, `endsChange`, `bucketMergeEvents`), src/runner/leftover.ts (`recoverLeftover`, the "recovered leftover work from " summary prefix). Pinned by: test/history-data.test.ts "a queued run resolves to its change's merge outcome — merged or merge_failed (BUGS.md 2026-09-30)", "a queued run resolves past a rebased retriable failure to the recovery's merged verdict (BUGS.md 2026-10-10)", "while a re-queued attempt is pending, the recovery row shows the failure and the authoring row waits to merge", "a change re-queued after seven review timeouts and then rejected reads each attempt once (feature-3, 2026-10-18)", "a recovery pin after a change that ended is a fresh change's first attempt, read by the authoring rule" and "a retriable verdict is not swept up by the next FRESH change's merge (BUGS.md 2026-10-10)".
  - `### INV-S4: missing evidence keeps the raw label, and the join never crosses roles`. Guarantee: `resolveQueuedResult` returns null (the row stays "queued") when the merge has no outcome yet, when no outcome matches the pin's sha, or when the row's run_start sits before a since-read's `floorTs`. Pins and outcomes are bucketed per role (`bucketMergeEvents`), so a `--role` filter or a role list never lends one role's verdict to another. A torn outcome falls back to its type's default text. Binds: src/history/history-data.ts (`resolveQueuedResult`, `attemptVerdict`, `bucketMergeEvents`, `runRows`). Pinned by: test/history-data.test.ts "a queued run whose merge is still in the pipeline keeps the raw label", "a queued run stays raw when no merge outcome matches its pinned sha", "a queued row whose run_start predates the join read's floor keeps the raw label", "the resolution survives the --role filter and never crosses roles", "runRows takes a list of role ids, joining each queued row's merge verdict" and "a queued run's torn merge outcome reads as its type default, never [object Object]".
  - `### INV-S5: the --since view holds exactly the window's runs, with a wider read for the join`. Guarantee: `readRunRowsSince` returns the run_ends at or after the cutoff and drops everything before it. A run that spans the cutoff renders a dash, because the ts filter removes its start too. Its queued verdict still resolves, because the join reads `RUN_ROW_JOIN_BACKSLACK_MS` further back through `readEventsSinceJoined`. `covered` stays false while the log starts inside the window, and a missing or empty log reads as no rows over a covered window. Binds: src/history/history-data.ts (`readRunRowsSince`, `RUN_ROW_JOIN_BACKSLACK_MS`, `RunRowJoin`), src/events/event-window.ts (`readEventsSinceJoined`). Pinned by: test/history-data.test.ts "rows keep the in-window runs, newest first, and drop everything before the cutoff", "a run spanning the cutoff renders a dash: the ts filter removes its start too", "a queued run whose pin sits before the --since cutoff still resolves (BUGS.md 2026-09-30)", "covered is false while the log starts inside the window, true once an event predates the cutoff" and "a missing or empty log reads as no rows over a covered window".
- Keep the words "tick" and "loop" out of the new prose; the cited titles above contain neither. The Plain-terms series sweeps those words, and this keeps the section out of its way. Its wording rules apply to prose too: no "run … running" stacks. Say "the event log", not "the notebook".
- Before citing it, check every quoted title with `grep -nF '<title>' <file>`, and replace any that has changed with the test's exact current title. The guard in test/invariants-doc.test.ts fails on a title that is not in the cited file.

### docs/invariants.md gains a usage-report fold section, so a fixer touching the memoized event fold reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches docs/invariants.md only; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `foldWindowEvents` (src/report/report-fold.ts) memoizes the event-log half of the usage report per (root, fromKey), so a dashboard polling /api/report folds only appended lines. A memo like this is only correct if every warm answer equals the cold one, and its fallback arms (torn tail, rotated or shrunken log, a moved window) are where a fix goes wrong. Only test/report-fold-cache.test.ts and a few test/report-data.test.ts tests pin this. `grep -n 'src/report\|foldWindowEvents' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing. This plan adds the section, as the 2026-10-20 claims, backlog-archive, fallback-breaker and provider-concurrency sections did. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes. It is independent of the init invariants plan above; both append a section, so whichever merges second appends after the other.

**Approach.**

Where a detail below turns out to be wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-R1: a warm fold equals the cold read, and an appended event counts once`. Guarantee: a cache hit on an unchanged log (same dev, ino, mtime and size, `sameStatIdentity`) returns the stored fold; growth on the same file folds only the lines past the stored offset, and the offset a full pass seeds is the scan's own end (`raw.liveEnd`), not the earlier stat's size, so an event is never folded twice. A legacy `merged` line appended to a warm fold folds as `merge_done`. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`, `foldLineInto`, `foldEventInto`), src/files/files.ts (`sameStatIdentity`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "warm collectReport equals the cold read before and after appends", "a merge appended after a warm fold counts once, including in the role split" and "a legacy `merged` line appended after a warm fold folds as merge_done".

Guarantee: the append arm reads through `readCompleteLines`, which holds back a newline-less tail; a grown log with no complete new line returns the stored fold unchanged, and the next call folds the completed line whole. Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`), src/files/tail.ts (`readCompleteLines`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "a torn trailing write is ignored until its newline lands".

Binds: src/report/report-fold.ts (`foldWindowEvents`, `ReportFoldEntry`'s `dev`/`ino`). Pinned by: test/report-fold-cache.test.ts "a rotated log replaced by a fresh larger one refolds instead of folding the new log's bytes" and "a shrunken log (rotation) refolds instead of misaligning the byte offset".
  - `### INV-R4: the coverage proof follows the window`. ### docs/invariants.md gains an init section, so a fixer touching `tumwater init` reads what it promises a user's repo instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches docs/invariants.md only; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

### Self-redeploy's restart cooldown drops from 12 h to 4 h, so fixes merged on main reach the running team the same working day (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/redeployer.test.ts, test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts and test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS` (src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts) allows at most one completed auto-restart per 12 h. It was set for BUGS.md 2026-09-11, when a drain's measured p50 was 46 min and its p75 82 min, so back-to-back drains halted the team. Drains are now short. The `restart` events' `finishedMs` for the last eight restarts (2026-10-17T17:51Z to 2026-10-20T12:42Z) were 2 s, 487 s, 835 s, 1562 s, 1596 s, 385 s, 363 s and 44 s. That is a median of about 7 min, and only one of them aborted runs (two, on 2026-10-19). The 12 h wait now costs more than the drains it prevents. On 2026-10-20 the team ran build 9a8ff490 (05:40 PDT) from 12:42Z. Two fixes that landed after it waited for the next restart, allowed only at 2026-10-21T00:42Z:
- 36d70ba86 (06:15 PDT), "Stand down a primary whose eligible entries siblings all hold". Until it ran, the primary `feature` runner kept paying for model runs that could only end in nothing-to-do. There were 58 `run_end` `no_change` results on `feature` that day, mostly 3–10 s runs started on a `main moved` wake or right after its own claim was released.
- 5aed15103 (05:56 PDT), "Merge PLANS.md, BUGS.md and QUESTIONS.md conflicts entry by entry". Until it ran, 23 `conflict_handback` events that day named PLANS.md as the only conflicted file. `git merge-file --diff3` reproduces the conflict for each of the seven sampled.

Each self-check extension merged that day also waits up to 12 h before it can stop a rejection. A 4 h cooldown allows at most six restarts a day. At the median drain, that holds new runs for about 42 min a day, against about 14 min today. In return, a merged fix runs within 4 h instead of within 12 h.

**Approach.**
- src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts: set `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS = 4 * 60 * 60_000`. Rewrite its doc comment: keep the 2026-09-11 reason, then add the 2026-10-20 re-derivation with the drain figures above. Add `export const RESTART_COOLDOWN_HOURS = RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS / 3_600_000;` beside it, with a one-line doc comment modelled on `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MIN`'s: the one home of the ms→h division the operator-facing warning uses. In the `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MS` doc comment and in the red-build doc comment that names "the 12 h deferral", say "the ordinary cooldown" instead of "12 h".
- src/redeploy/redeployer.ts: in `poll`'s cooldown warning, replace the literal `" (at most one completed restart per 12 h)"` with `` ` (at most one completed restart per ${RESTART_COOLDOWN_HOURS} h)` `` and import the constant beside `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS`. Change the three comments that say "12 h": the `urgentLapseWarnedFor` doc, the `effectiveCooldownUntil` doc, and the comment above the urgent-lapse warning. Each should say "the ordinary cooldown" or "the announced deadline" in place of the hour count.
- src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts: in `prewarm`'s doc comment, "the 12 h rate limit" becomes "the restart rate limit".
- docs/how-it-works.md: in the self-redeploy paragraph, "at most once every 12 hours" becomes "at most once every 4 hours", and "the 12-hour clock" becomes "the 4-hour clock".
- Tests. The timing assertions already derive from `RESTART_COOLDOWN_MS`, and every hard-coded offset in test/redeployer.test.ts and test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts is 1 h or 2 h, which stays inside a 4 h cooldown. Do not change any offset. In test/redeployer.test.ts:
  - Change the two `assert.match(..., /per 12 h/)` to `/per 4 h/`.
  - Retitle "a red RUNNING build cuts the cooldown to the urgent window: the episode starts minutes, not 12 h, after the swap" so that it ends "…starts minutes, not the ordinary cooldown, after the swap".
  - Change the present-tense comments and assertion messages that say "12 h" (the waive-the-cooldown comment, "the urgent lapse starts the episode — not 12 h later", "the ordinary 12 h deadline stands", "keeps the full 12 h cooldown", "still inside the ordinary 12 h cooldown", "skips the 12 h cooldown", "its announced 12 h deadline") to say "the ordinary cooldown" or "its announced deadline".
  - Do the same for "inside the 12 h window" in test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts and "must not cut a 12 h cooldown" in test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.
  - Leave the two dated past-tense incident lines unchanged, since they describe what happened then: the "BUGS.md 2026-09-30 (urgency carve-out)" comment in test/redeployer.test.ts, and "The 2026-09-30 shape" in test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts.
- Out of scope: `RESTART_URGENT_COOLDOWN_MS`, `STALE_ESCALATE_AFTER_MS`, the drain window, the forced-restart path, and any new config knob. This is a default change, not a setting.

**Files touched.** src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts, src/redeploy/redeployer.ts, src/redeploy/redeploy-probes.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/redeployer.test.ts, test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts, test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -rn "12 h\|12-hour\|12 hours" src/redeploy docs/how-it-works.md` finds nothing.
- `grep -n "12 h" test/redeployer.test.ts test/redeploy-prewarm.test.ts test/redeploy-wiring.test.ts` prints only lines inside the two dated 2026-09-30 incident comments named above.

### docs/invariants.md gains a provider-concurrency section, so a fixer touching the semaphore or the provider lease reads what they promise instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches docs/invariants.md only; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `maxConcurrent` and `maxConcurrentPerProvider` are enforced by the counting semaphore (src/concurrency/semaphore.ts) and the provider lease that follows a run across providers (src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts). Their callers are src/merge/merge-drain.ts, src/merge/merge-verify.ts, src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts, src/git/worktree-pool.ts, src/config/config-live.ts and src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts. Their guarantees (no deadlock on re-key, no preemption on a cap change, a full key never delaying another key) are pinned only by tests: `grep -n -i 'semaphore\|provider-lease\|maxConcurrent' docs/invariants.md` finds nothing. The register exists so a fixer reads a subsystem's contract before changing its code; the 2026-10-20 claims, backlog-archive and fallback-breaker sections did this for their subsystems. This plan adds the section. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after `## The backlog archive: finished entries move once, and only the ones a change added`. Title it `## Provider concurrency: every run holds one team permit and at most one provider slot`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intro under the backlog-archive section): what the semaphore bounds, and that a lease moves with its run. Use the next free letter, `P`; `grep -n 'INV-P' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first.
- Add five entries, each with **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.** like the existing ones. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions' doc comments and the cited tests, and state only what the code does: where a detail below turns out wrong, correct the sentence to match the code, not the plan.
  - `### INV-P1: admission needs both a team permit and the provider key's headroom, and a full key never delays another`. Binds: src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (`Semaphore.acquireLease`, `enforcedKeyCaps`), src/merge/merge-pipeline.ts. Pinned by: test/semaphore.test.ts "semaphore bounds concurrency" and "two keys fill independently: a full key never delays a free key, FIFO within a key"; test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts "maxConcurrentPerProvider caps role-run admission per provider while others run beside (part 2/5)" and "a verify's reviewer and a role run on the same capped provider never overlap, while another provider runs beside (part 3/5)".
  - `### INV-P2: a cap change never preempts, and permits never leak`. ### Plain terms code run, part 15/20: Convert the status display and the TUI (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 14/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/*.ts + src/ui/tui/ + their tests; done 2026-10-20)

**Goal.** The status model and renderer, the run-progress model and the TUI use run names: `lastRunCell`, `runProgress`, `progressOfRun` and `runStat`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/ui/status-render.ts: `lastTickCell` → `lastRunCell` (aliased if src/text/ or src/budget/ still use it). src/ui/run-progress-model.ts: `tickProgress` → `runProgress` and comments ("a tick with no recorded start time" → "a run with …"); its `ProgressRunKind` already says run. src/ui/progress-data.ts: `progressOfTick` → `progressOfRun`, and its many "run" nouns that mean the agent run get the "agent run" rule. Comments in status-model.ts (about 50 lines), status-payload.ts, team-alerts.ts, tone.ts, badges.ts and transcript.ts.
- src/ui/tui/ (tui-keys.ts has about 54 lines, plus tui-history.ts, tui-pane.ts, tui.tsx, tui-editors.ts and tui-frame.ts): the local `tickStat` → `runStat`; migrate `renderRunDetail`, `readRunRows`, `readRunDetail`, `RunRow`, `RunDetail`, `runRowCells`, `HISTORY_DEFAULT_RUNS`, `runRowsMatchingGrep`, `runDetailStat` and `runRowGrepHaystack`; then delete each of those aliases that no other file still names. Comments.
- Tests: test/status-model.test.ts, test/status-render*.test.ts, test/status-payload.test.ts, test/team-alerts.test.ts, test/progress.test.ts, test/tui*.test.ts and test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.ts.
- Wording (replanned 2026-10-20 by plan: the review rounds on this part rejected garbled English the word swap left, plus once an event-loop "tick" renamed by mistake, and never the renames themselves). Reread every comment and test title you change as a sentence, and reword rather than swap when "run" lands next to another "run" or a form of it. The shapes reviewers rejected, each with a fix: "the role's next run runs" (also split across a line break) → "the role's next run is in progress"; "while the role's runs run off-model" → "while the role's runs use another model"; "with no director run running" → "while no director run is in progress"; "the run's own run" / "the authoring run's finished run" → "the authoring agent run" / "the authoring role's finished run"; "never-ran role" → "role that has never run"; "has actually ran" → "has actually run". Also: "this run's pi run" / "the new run's run" → "this run's agent run" / "the new agent run"; "across runs and runs" → reword per the "agent run" rule. Keep "tick" where it means the JavaScript event-loop tick, such as the src/ui/tui/tui.tsx comment "the test harness waits a tick before pressing keys"; mark that line `// retired-name-ok: event-loop tick`. The pre-queue self-check's `GARBLED_WORDING` (src/run/stage-check.ts) catches some of these shapes but not "run runs" or "run running", so do not rely on it alone. In test/progress.test.ts, rename the `"never-ran"` role-name fixture to `"idle-role"`.

(a|the|no|its|their) run\b" src/ui test/status-*.test.ts test/team-alerts.test.ts test/progress.test.ts test/tui*.test.ts test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.ts | grep -v '^src/ui/gui/'` prints nothing (on main before this part it prints only the test/progress.test.ts `"never-ran"` fixture).

### The pre-queue self-check runs a finished plan's "prints nothing" acceptance greps, so a change stops being rejected for an acceptance grep that still matches (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Adds src/run/acceptance-greps.ts and test/acceptance-greps.test.ts and wires them into `stageCheckFindings` in src/run/stage-check.ts, which also holds the merged garbled-wording self-check (`garbledWordingFindings`); leave it unchanged; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Plans state acceptance criteria as grep commands: PLANS.md and PLANS-DONE.md hold over 40 criteria of the form "`grep …` finds nothing / prints nothing / is empty". Today nothing runs them before review. Between 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-20, 42 `review_rejected` events cite an acceptance or VERIFIED grep that still matched. One example is the 2026-10-20 05:00Z feature-3 rejection: "`grep -rn "logs --role" src docs/cli.md` still matches `docs/cli.md:40`". Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue. If the self-check runs the grep, the fix-up turn sees the hits and fixes them first. This plan covers only the strict "matches nothing" form. Criteria worded "prints only …" / "lists only …" need judgement: handing their hits to the fix-up turn would invite it to rename the serialized names those criteria deliberately keep. So they stay out.

**Approach.**
- **New module src/run/acceptance-greps.ts.** Give it a module doc comment, plus a doc comment on each export.
  - `export function emptyGrepCriteria(body: string): string[]`. Collapse the body's whitespace to single spaces. Return each backticked span (`` `…` ``) that:
    - starts with `grep ` or `git grep `;
    - is followed, after optional spaces, by one of: `finds nothing`, `prints nothing`, `returns nothing`, `outputs nothing`, `matches nothing`, `lists nothing`, `is empty`, `lists none`, or `prints|finds|lists|returns|gives|shows` followed by `no` and then `lines?|hits?|matches?|output`. Match case-insensitively.
    - Drop a criterion whose text from that phrase to the next `.` or `;` contains `apart from`, `except`, `excluding`, `other than`, `besides` or `beyond`. Such a criterion allows some hits.
    - Return the spans' inner text without duplicates, in body order, at most 5.
  - `export function grepArgv(cmd: string): { file: "grep" | "git"; args: string[] } | undefined`. A minimal shell-word splitter. Single quotes are literal. In double quotes, only `\"` and `\\` are escapes. Outside quotes, a backslash keeps the next character. Return undefined when an unquoted `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `$`, `(`, `)` or backtick appears, or when a quote is left open. `git grep …` gives `{ file: "git", args: ["grep", …] }`; `grep …` gives `{ file: "grep", args: […] }`. Nothing goes through a shell, so `*` stays literal (grep's own `--include=*.ts` handles it).
  - `export async function acceptanceGrepFindings(wt: string, entries: { title: string; body: string }[]): Promise<string[]>`. For each entry and each criterion with a non-undefined argv, run `execFileAsync(file, args, { cwd: wt, timeout: 20_000 })` (src/process/process.ts).
    - An exit code of 1 with empty stdout is a pass. Any other failure (exit 2, a timeout, a spawn error) skips that criterion: an unrunnable command is not evidence.
    - Exit 0 with non-empty stdout yields one finding: `PLANS.md's finished entry "${truncate(title, 160)}" says \`${cmd}\` matches nothing, but it prints ${n} line(s): ${first 5 lines, each cut to 200 chars, joined with "; "}${more suffix} — fix those lines, or correct the claim if the criterion is wrong`.
    - Give at most one finding per entry: the first failing criterion's. `truncate` is in src/text/text.ts.
- **Wiring in src/run/stage-check.ts.** In `stageCheckFindings`, the `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` block already reads head and base text for `PLANS.md`/PLANS-DONE.md. For the `PLANS.md` spec only, collect the entries this change finished:
  - `## Done` entries of the head `PLANS.md` whose `finishedKey` (the existing helper) is not among the base `## Done` keys;
  - plus PLANS-DONE.md `## Done` entries whose key is not among the base archive's keys.

  Run `acceptanceGrepFindings(wt, entries)` on them, inside the existing `.catch(() => [])` pattern, and push its findings. Add a sentence to the module header doc comment's staging-only paragraph: `acceptanceGrepFindings` runs only at staging and runs the strict "matches nothing" greps of the plan entries the change finished. The gate does not run it.
- **No prompt change.** `buildStageFixPrompt` (src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts) already passes each finding's text to the fix-up turn.

**Files touched.** src/run/acceptance-greps.ts (new), src/run/stage-check.ts, test/acceptance-greps.test.ts (new). docs/invariants.md stays unchanged: no Binds list there pins a staging-only finding of this kind. Check with `grep -n "finishedDuplicateFindings\|strayPlaceholder" docs/invariants.md`, which finds nothing.

**Acceptance criteria.** In test strings, build the trigger phrases (for example "finds" + " nothing") by concatenation. That way this change's own PLANS.md Done entry is the only text that matters to its own self-check. That entry's criteria must hold on the finished tree.
- "emptyGrepCriteria picks the matches-nothing greps and skips qualified or only-kind ones": a body holding `` `grep -rn foo src` finds nothing``, `` `git grep -n bar` is empty``, `` `grep -rn baz src` prints only kept names`` and `` `grep -rn qux src` prints nothing apart from a fixture`` gives exactly the first two commands.
- "grepArgv splits quotes and refuses shell syntax": `grep -rnE 'a|b' "src dir" --include=*.ts` gives `["-rnE", "a|b", "src dir", "--include=*.ts"]`; `git grep -n x` gives file `git` and args `["grep", "-n", "x"]`; `grep x | wc -l` and `grep 'x` give undefined.
- "acceptanceGrepFindings reports a matches-nothing grep that still matches": in a temp dir holding `src/a.ts` with the text `leftoverName`, an entry whose body says `` `grep -rn leftoverName src` `` + " finds nothing" yields one finding that names the entry's title and contains `src/a.ts:1`. Removing the text yields no finding. An entry whose grep exits 2 (a missing path) yields no finding.
- A test in test/stage-check.test.ts, "a finished plan whose matches-nothing grep still matches yields the acceptance-grep finding": use `repoWith` with a base PLANS.md and a `src/a.ts` containing `oldName`. In the worktree, add a `## Done` entry to PLANS.md whose body says the grep for `oldName` over `src` finds nothing. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` then includes a finding that contains `src/a.ts:1`. The same entry already present under `## Done` on the base yields no acceptance-grep finding.
- `grep -rn "acceptanceGrepFindings" src` lists the definition in src/run/acceptance-greps.ts and its call and doc mention in src/run/stage-check.ts.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check's garbled-wording check catches "run" stacked on "run", "run" + "running", "run's … run", and a garbled phrase split across a line break (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, which already hold the merged stray-placeholder self-check (`strayPlaceholderFinding`); leave it unchanged; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `GARBLED_WORDING` (src/run/stage-check.ts) has caught broken participles ("has … ran", "X-ran") and a few stacked shapes ("run is still running", "run a/the/no run") since 2026-10-20 07:21 PDT. The plain-terms rename parts kept being rejected after that for shapes it misses. In the events log, 10 `review_rejected` events quote one of them, nine from 2026-10-20 (feature, feature-2, feature-4 on parts 13–15; the latest at 14:21Z and 14:27Z on part 15/20). The shapes: "run" directly followed by "run"/"runs" ("the role's next run" + " runs", "while the role's runs" + " run off-model"); "run" directly followed by "running" ("no director run" + " running"); a possessive "run's"/"runs'" followed, with at most one word between, by "run"/"runs" ("this run's pi" + " run", "the authoring run's" + " run", "the run's own" + " runs'"); "runs and runs"; and the same phrases split across a line break inside a comment ("the role's next run" / "runs and clear only", src/ui/status-model.ts in the 14:27Z rejection). Eleven parts of the series are still to come (16/20–20/20 and cleanup 1/7–7/7). Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue; a finding costs one fix-up turn.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Append three patterns to `GARBLED_WORDING`, in this order:
  - `/\bruns?\s+run(?:s|ning)?\b/i` ("run" stacked on "run", "runs" or "running");
  - `/\bruns?'s?\s+(?:(?!agent\b)[a-z]+\s+)?runs?\b/i` (a possessive run followed by run, with at most one word between; "agent" is excluded because "this run's agent run" is the wording the rename series prescribes);
  - `/\bruns?\s+(?:and|or)\s+runs?\b/i`.
  The first covers both the "run" + "runs" and the "run" + "running" shapes. Extend the doc comment above `GARBLED_WORDING` to describe them in words, without writing a garbled phrase out in full: the change's own self-check reads its added lines, so a comment that spells out one of these phrases flags itself. (The existing comment already does this, and the patterns' own source text does not match, because `\s+` is not whitespace.)
- In `garbledWordingFindings`, also check a phrase split across two lines. While walking a hunk, remember the previous added line's text (`prevAdded`; reset it to null on each `diff --git` header, on each `@@` hunk header and on any line that is not an added line). For an added line with no single-line hit and a non-null `prevAdded`, build `joined = prevAdded.trimEnd() + " " + cur.replace(/^\s*(?:\/\/+|\*|#)\s*/, "")`. For the first `GARBLED_WORDING` match in `joined` that starts before `prevAdded.trimEnd().length` and ends after it (so it spans the join and was not already reported for the earlier line), push `${file}:${lineNo - 1}-${lineNo} "${m[0]}"`. Use a global copy of each regex (`new RegExp(re.source, re.flags + "g")`) with `matchAll` to find a spanning match. Record prose stays skipped as before.
- Fix the module header doc comment: the paragraph that starts "A fifth check, `garbledWordingFindings`" repeats "fifth" (the detached-doc paragraph above it is the fifth, `movedSourceFindings` the sixth). Make it "A seventh check", and extend its parenthetical list with the new shapes (described in words, as above) and "including a phrase split across two added lines".

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts. The gate does not run this check, and no docs/invariants.md Binds list names `garbledWordingFindings` (check with `grep -n garbled docs/invariants.md`; it was empty when this was planned), so that file stays unchanged. Main already holds lines with these shapes (`grep -nE "\bruns?\s+runs?\b" src` hits src/runner/runner-run.ts and src/run/run-resume.ts); the check reads only added lines, so they are not reported unless a change rewrites them. Leave them alone; the series parts reword them.

**Acceptance criteria.** Build every garbled sample in the tests by string concatenation (as the existing garbled-wording tests do), so test/stage-check.test.ts's own added lines do not match.
- A new test, "added lines that stack run on runs or running, or a run's run, yield the garbled-wording finding": in `src/a.ts`, add the lines `// while the role's next run` + ` runs`, `// with no director run` + ` running`, `// the authoring run's` + ` run`, `// this run's pi` + ` run` and `// across runs and` + ` runs`. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` gives one garbled-wording finding that names each of those five `src/a.ts:N` lines.
- A new test, "a garbled phrase split across two added comment lines yields the garbled-wording finding": two added lines `// the alert stays up while the role's next run` and `// runs and clears after`, with the garbled part concatenated as above. The finding contains `src/a.ts:2-3`.
- A new test, "the prescribed agent-run wording yields no garbled-wording finding": the added lines `// this run's agent run`, `// the role has run twice; it ran once` and `// a run, and then the next` give no garbled-wording finding.
- The existing garbled-wording tests ("added lines with a broken participle…", "added lines that stack run on run…", "garbled wording in record prose…", "garbled wording already on the base…") pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a `_None yet._` placeholder the change added to a backlog section that still holds entries (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. The in-flight moved-source self-check plan also adds a check to src/run/stage-check.ts, so whichever merges second rebases over a neighbouring hunk; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** A feature run that finishes the last entry under `## Planned` sometimes writes `_None yet._` where that entry used to be, even though the section still holds other entries. `_None yet._` is the skeleton placeholder that marks an empty section (init-templates.ts, `PLACEHOLDER` in src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts), so the file then says `## Planned` is empty while it lists open plans. Reviewers rejected this five times: 10-09 13:12, 10-16 18:30, 10-19 14:47 (feature-4, head 97f625eee), 10-20 00:20 (feature-3) and 10-20 13:43 (feature-3, head 8c45509f9). In both heads checked, the PLANS.md hunk adds `+_None yet._` directly above `## Done`. Each rejection cost a review round and a re-queue for a one-line deletion. No current check catches it: `grep -n 'None yet' src/run/stage-check.ts src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts` is empty. A staging finding gives the fix-up turn the exact line to delete before the change is queued.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `const PLACEHOLDER_LINE = "_None yet._";` with a one-line doc comment ("the skeleton placeholder that marks an empty backlog section"). Also add `const PLACEHOLDER_FILES = ["PLANS.md", "BUGS.md", "QUESTIONS.md"] as const;` (the live backlog files; the archives have no placeholder sections).
- Add a module-private helper `placeholderSections(md: string): Map<string, number>`. For each `## ` section title in `md` (`fenceAwareHeadingLines(md, "## ").map((l) => headingTitle(l, "## "))`), when `sectionBodyLines(md, title).some((l) => l.trim() === PLACEHOLDER_LINE)` and `parseEntryDetails(md, title).length > 0`, it maps the title to that entry count. Import `fenceAwareHeadingLines`, `headingTitle` and `sectionBodyLines` from `../backlog/backlog-md.js`, where `parseEntryDetails` is already imported. Fenced lines are excluded because `sectionBodyLines` strips them, so a quoted placeholder never counts.
- Add an exported `strayPlaceholderFinding(file: string, head: string, base: string): string | undefined`. It returns undefined unless some section is in `placeholderSections(head)` but not in `placeholderSections(base)`, so damage already on main is not blamed on this change. For the first such section in file order, it returns `` `${file}'s "## ${title}" section holds ${n} entr${n === 1 ? "y" : "ies"}, but this change left the empty-section placeholder ${PLACEHOLDER_LINE} in it — delete that line: it marks a section with no entries` `` followed by `moreSuffix(count - 1)`, the way `waitingNoteFinding` reports the rest. Give it a doc comment in the style of `waitingNoteFinding`'s.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the `waitingNoteFinding` block, add a loop over `PLACEHOLDER_FILES` that skips files not in `files`. ### The pre-queue self-check flags a reference to a file that the change moved code out of, so a split stops being rejected for a doc that still says the moved code lives in the old file (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, like the garbled-wording and detached-doc self-check plans above; whichever lands later rebases onto the others' `gitLevelFindings` line and header paragraph; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Three organize changes were rejected on 2026-10-20 for the same defect. Each one moved code out of a file that still exists, and left a reference elsewhere saying the moved code lives in the old file. At 11:28 (head 7fe012b38), tests moved from test/gate-prompts.test.ts to the new test/gate-notes.test.ts, but the `entryRangeLines` doc in src/prompt/gate-notes.ts still said "pinned in tests (test/gate-prompts.test.ts)". At 13:37 (head 9c1bbe9f2), the `eventMessage` cases moved out of src/events/event-format.ts into new `event-message-*.ts` modules, but the **Binds** list in docs/invariants.md still named `src/events/event-format.ts` for the `image_reroute` lines. At 03:31, an open PLANS.md entry still named src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts as the home of moved code. The existing checks miss this shape. `staleReferenceFindings` only greps `D` and `R` paths, and the old file here is `M`. `staleNameFindings` exempts a name the change re-declares (a move), and neither stale line named a moved declaration. A move can be read from the `-U0` diff that `gitLevelFindings` already builds: lines removed from one file and added verbatim to another. Grepping the staged tree for the old file's full path then lists the lines to re-check, so the author's fix-up turn can repoint them before a review is spent. The 11:28 and 13:37 cases would both have been caught. The 03:31 case sits in record prose, which every path check deliberately skips (`isRecordProse`).

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `movedSourceFindings(wt: string, diff: string, entries: NameStatusEntry[]): Promise<string[]>`. Call it in `gitLevelFindings` after `staleNameFindings`. Give it a `/** (f) … */` doc in the style of the `(a)`–`(d)` docs, and add one sentence to the module header's paragraph on the git-level checks. Letter it after the last existing check letter: (f) if the detached-doc plan's (e) has landed, else (e).
- Collect moves from the diff. Walk it like `staleNameFindings`, tracking the current file from `diff --git a/.* b/(.*)`. For each file, keep `removed: string[]` and `added: Set<string>` of lines with the `-`/`+` marker stripped and `.trim()` applied. Keep only trimmed lines of at least `MOVED_LINE_MIN_CHARS = 12` characters, so braces, `});` and blank lines never count. A source is a file whose `entries` status is `M`. Its moved count is the number of its `removed` lines found in some other file's `added`. Its receivers are those other files, in diff order. A source qualifies when its moved count is at least `MOVED_LINES_MIN = 10`. Add both constants beside `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES`, each with a one-line doc.
- For each qualifying source, stopping after `MAX_STALE_PATHS` sources, run `gitTry(wt, "grep", "-n", "-F", "-I", "--cached", "-e", source)`. Parse hits with the same `^([^:]+):(\d+):(.*)$` regex that `staleReferenceFindings` uses. Skip a hit that is in the source file itself, in record prose (`isRecordProse`), or whose line fails `hasStandalonePathOccurrence(text, source)`. Keep up to `MAX_STALE_HITS`. Do not exclude receivers: the 11:28 stale line was itself a moved line, so it sat in the receiver. Emit nothing for a source with no remaining hits.
- Wording, one finding per source: `` `${source} had ${n} lines moved to ${cappedList(receivers, MAX_STALE_PATHS)}, but it is still named at: ${hits.join(", ")} — check each still describes what stays in ${source}, and point any that describes the moved code at its new file` ``. A correct reference is answered in RISK, as `buildStageFixPrompt` already allows.
- Out of scope: basename-only or extension-swapped references (`gate-prompts.ts`, `./event-format.js`), record prose, and moves into a file the change does not touch.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. No docs/invariants.md section covers the self-check's advisory findings (`grep -n "self-check" docs/invariants.md` is empty), so it stays unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts under a `// Moved-source check: …` comment. Each builds with `repoWith`, edits the worktree with `fs.writeFileSync`, and calls `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`. `BODY` is 12 distinct lines such as `export const valueNumber${i} = ${i} * 1000;`.
- "moving code out of a file that a doc still names yields the moved-source finding". Base: `src/big.ts` = `export const keep = 1;\n` + BODY, `docs/x.md` = `The bodies live in src/big.ts.\n`. Head: `src/big.ts` = `export const keep = 1;\n`, new `src/small.ts` = BODY. Exactly one finding matches `/src\/big\.ts had 12 lines moved to src\/small\.ts, but it is still named at: docs\/x\.md:1/`. After rewriting `docs/x.md` to name `src/small.ts`, no finding matches `/lines moved to/`.
- "a reference inside the receiving file is reported too". Same move, with no docs/x.md, but the receiver's head starts with `// pinned in tests (src/big.ts)\n`. The finding names `src/small.ts:1`.
- "a move below the line threshold, a pure deletion, or a reference in record prose yields no moved-source finding". Three repos, each giving no finding that matches `/lines moved to/`. (a) Move only 5 BODY lines. (b) Delete BODY from `src/big.ts` with no receiver. (c) The full move, with the reference only in `PLANS.md`.
- "a basename-only reference is not reported". The full move, with `docs/x.md` = `See big.ts.\n`. No finding matches `/lines moved to/`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The self-check's outcome warning carries the finding texts, so the log shows which checks fire and which ones a fix-up turn leaves open (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/run-stage.ts, test/run-stage.test.ts and the `"warning"` line of the event-type union in src/events/events.ts. The two in-flight self-check plans edit src/run/stage-check.ts only, so neither conflicts)

**Goal.** `stageRunMerge` (src/run/run-stage.ts) ends the pre-queue self-check with one `warning` event. Its message holds counts only: "stage self-check: N findings — fixed by the follow-up turn", "…; M still open, queued for the gate", or "the follow-up turn left no change; nothing to land". The events log holds 49 of these in the seven days before this plan. Several of them read "10 findings; 10 still open" or "11 findings; 11 still open" (feature-3 on 10-18, others on 10-17), and nothing records what those findings were. That leaves three questions the log cannot answer. Which checks fire? Which findings does an author ignore? Did a check miss the defect a reviewer later rejected? For example, the 13:36 rejection on 2026-10-20 named `deferTick` and `restoreMidTickWake` comments left in tests. The log has no self-check warning for that run, so it cannot show whether the staleName check, merged at 13:22, was part of the running build. The plan role picks its self-check work from rejection themes, and it is planning more checks now (garbled wording, detached doc comments). Recording the finding texts lets it measure a check after it lands instead of guessing.

**Approach.** All in src/run/run-stage.ts:
- Add a module-level constant `SELF_CHECK_LOGGED_FINDINGS = 12` (the most findings one outcome event carries) and `SELF_CHECK_FINDING_CHARS = 300` (the cap on each finding's text), each with a one-line doc. Add a module-private helper `findingDigest(findings: readonly string[]): string[]` that returns `findings.slice(0, SELF_CHECK_LOGGED_FINDINGS).map((f) => squash(f, SELF_CHECK_FINDING_CHARS))`. Import `squash` from `../text/text.js`.
- In `stageRunMerge`'s self-check block, the three outcome `ctx.warn(...)` calls become `logEventBestEffort(ctx.root, { source: ctx.role, type: "warning", message, findings: findingDigest(findings) })`. `message` is the exact string each one passes today. The "still open" outcome also carries `open: findingDigest(remaining)`. `findings` is the list handed to `requestStageFix`, so it includes the `assignedMoved` and `heldMoved` findings pushed onto it. Every other `ctx.warn` call in the file stays as it is. Add a one-line comment saying why these three bypass `ctx.warn`: they carry fields beyond a message, and `ctx.warn` only takes a message. The runner's `warn` → `warnEventBestEffort` writes the same `{ source: role, type: "warning", message }` shape, so feeds, `formatEvent`'s `warning: <message>` line and any warning counter see an unchanged event. Only the extra fields are new.
- In src/events/events.ts, add a trailing comment to the union's final `| "warning";` line: `// something is off but the loop continues: message; the stage self-check's outcome warnings (run/run-stage.ts) also carry findings (the finding texts, capped) and, when some stayed open after the fix-up turn, open`.

**Files touched.** src/run/run-stage.ts, src/events/events.ts (one comment), test/run-stage.test.ts. No docs/invariants.md section covers the self-check's warnings (`grep -n "self-check" docs/invariants.md` is empty), so it stays unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/run-stage.test.ts, import `readEvents` from `../src/events/event-read.js`. Update the five tests that now assert one of these messages through `calls.warnings`. They are "a self-check finding triggers one follow-up and queues with the fixed warning", "a finding the follow-up leaves unfixed still queues, with the still-open warning", and the other still-open and no-change tests that assert those exact strings (`grep -n '"stage self-check' test/run-stage.test.ts`). Each one reads `readEvents(root, 50).filter((e) => e.type === "warning")` and asserts:
  - the fixed case: one event with the same message, `source: "improve"`, `findings` deep-equal to `["md-only BUGS.md edit moves X to Fixed, but none of its symbols exist"]`, and no `open` key;
  - the still-open case: the same message, `findings: ["a finding"]` and `open: ["a finding"]`;
  - the no-change case: message "stage self-check: the follow-up turn left no change; nothing to land" with `findings: ["a finding"]`.
  Where a test's `calls.warnings` had held only that message, it now asserts `calls.warnings` is `[]`.
- A new test, "the self-check outcome warning caps the logged findings and their length", sets `stageChecks: [Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, i) => \`finding ${i} \` + "x".repeat(400)), []]`. It asserts that the warning's `findings` has length 12, that each entry has at most 300 characters and ends with `…`, and that the first one starts with `finding 0 `.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a doc comment that the change detached from its declaration (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, like the garbled-wording self-check plan above; whichever lands second rebases onto the other's `gitLevelFindings` line and header paragraph; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Ten `review_rejected` events between 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-20 name the same mechanical defect: a JSDoc block that no longer sits on the declaration it documents. Two edits cause it. (1) New code is inserted between an existing `/** … */` block and its declaration. The doc then describes the inserted code, and the old declaration is left with none. Examples: `postReviewDue` between `drainMergeQueue`'s doc and its declaration (feature-5, 10-20), `quietHoursLine` inside `scheduleLine`'s doc (10-16), `entryRevisionFields` under `enqueueMerge`'s doc (dedupe, 10-18), `outcomeOrBadRequest` in src/gui/gui-backlog-commands.ts (dedupe, 10-18). (2) A declaration is deleted but its doc is kept, so the doc lands on the next declaration. Example: the `/** @deprecated Use …. */` line left above `export async function mergeHead` in test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts (feature, 10-20 13:12), which marked a live fixture deprecated. Both shapes can be read straight from the `-U0` diff the self-check already builds in `gitLevelFindings`, so the author's fix-up turn can repair them before a review is spent.

**Approach.** All in src/run/stage-check.ts:
- Add `detachedDocFindings(wt: string, diff: string): string[]`. Call it in `gitLevelFindings` after `newlineFindings(diff)`. Put a `/** (e) … */` doc on it in the style of `newlineFindings`'s `(c)` doc, and add a sentence about it to the module header's paragraph on the fourth check.
- Walk the diff like `newlineFindings`: `diff --git` starts a file, and `+++ ` gives the path through `diffPlusPath`. Consider only paths matching the existing `JS_FILE` and not `/dev/null`. For each such file, read the head text once with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, file))`, split it on `"\n"`, and collect every hunk as `{ c, d, removed: string[], added: string[] }`. The header is `@@ -a[,b] +c[,d] @@`, and an omitted count means 1. `-` lines go into `removed` and `+` lines into `added`, without the marker. Lines are 1-based into the head file.
- Two module-level helpers:
  - `DOC_TARGET`: a regex for a line that can carry a doc comment. It is either a keyword declaration, `^\s*(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:abstract\s+)?(?:async\s+)?(?:function\b|const\b|let\b|var\b|class\b|interface\b|type\b|enum\b)`, or a class member or field, `^\s*(?:(?:public|private|protected|static|readonly|async|get|set|override)\s+)*#?[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*\??\s*[(<:=]`. Combine them with `|` into one regex.
  - `closesDocComment(lines: string[], i: number): boolean` (0-based `i`). It is true when `lines[i].trim()` ends with `*/` and the nearest line at or above `i` that contains `/*` has a trimmed form starting with `/**`. This covers one-line blocks like `/** @deprecated Use b. */`.
- Rule (1), insertion. The hunk has `removed.length === 0` and `d > 0`. Head line `c - 1` must exist, closes a doc comment, and is not an added line of any hunk in this file. At least one `added` line matches `DOC_TARGET`. Head line `c + d` exists and matches `DOC_TARGET`. Report the site as `` `${file}:${c - 1}` ``.
- Rule (2), deletion. The hunk has `d === 0` and at least one `removed` line matching `DOC_TARGET`. Head line `c` (git's convention: the line before the deleted range) closes a doc comment and is not an added line. Report `` `${file}:${c}` ``.
- Emit at most one finding per rule, each listing its sites with `cappedList(sites, MAX_DETACHED_DOCS)`. Add the constant `MAX_DETACHED_DOCS = 10` beside `MAX_NEWLINE_FILES`, with a one-line doc. Wording:
  - (1) `code was inserted between a doc comment and the declaration it documents, so the doc now describes the inserted code: ${list} — move the inserted code above the doc comment or below that declaration`
  - (2) `a declaration was deleted but its doc comment was kept, so the doc now documents the next declaration: ${list} — delete the doc comment with it`
- Out of scope: a doc that disagrees with its own declaration's text, `//` line comments, and non-JS files.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts. No invariants section names these findings (the self-check findings are advisory), so docs/invariants.md is unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts. Each builds with `repoWith`, edits the worktree with `fs.writeFileSync`, and calls `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`:
- "code inserted between a doc comment and its declaration yields the detached-doc finding": base `src/a.ts` is `/** Doc A. */\nexport function a() {}\n`. Head is `/** Doc A. */\n\nfunction ins() {}\n\nexport function a() {}\n`. There is exactly one finding matching `/inserted between a doc comment/`, and it names `src/a.ts:1`.
- "a documented helper inserted under another doc also yields it": the same base, with head `/** Doc A. */\n\n/** Doc ins. */\nfunction ins() {}\n\nexport function a() {}\n`. The finding names `src/a.ts:1`.
- "a deleted declaration whose doc comment stays yields the finding": base `test/f.ts` is `/** @deprecated Use b. */\nexport const old = b;\n\nexport function c() {}\n`. Head deletes only line 2. One finding matches `/its doc comment was kept/` and names `test/f.ts:1`.
- "deleting a declaration with its doc, adding a function after a declaration, or editing a declaration line yields no detached-doc finding": three edits on the Doc A base, each giving no finding that matches either regex. (a) Delete both lines of the deprecated alias in the `test/f.ts` base. (b) Append `\n/** Doc z. */\nexport function z() {}\n` after `a`. (c) Change `export function a() {}` to `export function a(x = 1) {}`.
- "a line comment inserted between a doc and its declaration yields no finding": the head inserts `// eslint-disable-next-line no-console` between `/** Doc A. */` and `export function a() {}`. No finding matches `/inserted between a doc comment/`.
- "a detached doc in a non-JS file is not reported": the rule (1) shape in `docs/a.md` gives no detached-doc finding.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags the garbled wording a word-swap rename leaves in added lines (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts test/stage-check.test.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The plain-terms rename series swaps "tick" words for "run" words by rote, which leaves two kinds of garbled English that reviewers reject change after change. One is a broken past participle: an auxiliary followed by "ran" ("would have" + " ran", "has actually" + " ran"), or "ran" hyphenated onto another word ("never" + "-ran", "least-recently" + "-ran", "stale" + "-ran"). The other is "run" stacked on "run": "the run is" + " running", "a run already" + " running", "run the" + " run", "running a" + " run", "runs no" + " run". In the events log, 11 `review_rejected` events quote one of these phrases in their reasons, and ten of them are from 2026-10-20 alone (feature, feature-2, feature-4, on parts 13–15). Twelve parts of the series are still to come (16/20–20/20 and cleanup 1/7–7/7). Each such rejection costs a review round and a re-queue. The pre-queue self-check (`stageCheckFindings`, src/run/stage-check.ts) already gives the author one bounded fix-up turn for heuristic findings like path drift and stale names, and any finding left open still goes to the gate (run-stage.ts "…still open, queued for the gate"). So a mechanical check for these phrases can turn most of those rejections into a fix-up turn, and a false positive costs only that turn.

**Approach.**
- src/run/stage-check.ts:
  - Add `function garbledWordingFindings(diff: string): string[]`, and call it in `gitLevelFindings` right after `newlineFindings(diff)`. It reads the `-U0` diff that function already has.
  - Walk the diff by line. On `diff --git a/… b/<path>`, set the current file to `<path>`. On `@@ … +<c>[,<d>] @@`, set the next new-side line number to `c`. On a `+` line that is not a `+++ ` header, test the text after the `+`, then add 1 to the line number. Skip files where `isRecordProse(file)` holds: history in the backlog quotes old wording.
  - Use one case-insensitive pattern list, `GARBLED_WORDING`, with a doc comment saying what each pattern catches and why (rote "tick → run" swaps):
    - `/\b(?:has|have|had|having)\s+(?:\w+ly\s+|never\s+|not\s+|already\s+|just\s+)?ran\b/i`
    - `/[A-Za-z]-ran\b/i`. Keep the character class: if it were written as `\w-ran\b`, this source line would match itself.
    - `/\bruns?\s+(?:is|are|was|were|already|still)\s+(?:still\s+|already\s+)?running\b/i`
    - `/\b(?:run|runs|running)\s+(?:a|the|no)\s+run\b/i`
  - Record a hit as `<file>:<line> "<matched text>"`. Keep at most one hit per line (the first pattern that matches). The check returns at most one finding: ``added lines carry garbled rename wording (reword them; a rote "tick" → "run" swap reads wrong here): `` followed by `cappedList(hits, MAX_STALE_HITS)`.
  - In the module's top doc comment, add a sentence after the `staleNameFindings` paragraph: a fifth check, `garbledWordingFindings`, reports added lines (outside record prose) that carry the broken participles and doubled "run" wording a word-swap rename leaves. Like the path checks, the gate does not run it. Describe the phrases with ellipses (for example "has/have/had … ran"), never as a literal phrase, so the comment does not match its own check.
- No docs/invariants.md change: like the path-drift and lost-newline findings, this is a staging heuristic and not a gate guarantee (the "merge gate's deterministic rejections" section binds stage-check.ts only for the protected-edit and secret checks).

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- In test/stage-check.test.ts, write each fixture the way "removing a file's final newline yields the finding" does: `repoWith({...})`, write the file, then `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")`. Build every garbled phrase by string concatenation (for example `"would have " + "ran"`), so the test file's own lines do not match the check:
  - "added lines with a broken participle yield the garbled-wording finding": base `src/a.ts` holds `export const a = 1;\n`. Append a comment line `// the role would have ` + `ran twice` and a second line `// a never` + `-ran role`. There is exactly one finding matching `/garbled rename wording/`, and it names `src/a.ts:2` and `src/a.ts:3`.
  - "added lines that stack run on run yield the garbled-wording finding": an added `test/b.test.ts` line `assert.ok(x, "no run was ` + `running");` gives a finding that names `test/b.test.ts:1`.
  - "garbled wording in record prose, and a correct participle, yield no finding": the same broken-participle phrase added to `PLANS.md`, and a `src/a.ts` comment `// the role has run twice; it ran once today`, give no finding matching `/garbled rename wording/`.
  - "garbled wording already on the base is not reported": a base file that already holds the phrase, plus an unrelated added line elsewhere in that file, gives no garbled-wording finding.
- `grep -nE "(has|have|had|having) ran|[A-Za-z]-ran\b" src/run/stage-check.ts test/stage-check.test.ts` prints nothing. Neither file trips the new check.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A `main_red`-kept change stays parked while main's new head is still red, instead of re-queuing on any move of main (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/merge/merge-slot.ts src/runner/runner-state.ts test/merge-requeue.test.ts test/runner-state.test.ts)

**Goal.** A merge ends `main_red` when the change's check failed on tests main does not already know about and main's tip was red (`attributeRedCheck`, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts, and merge-core.ts's `gate.mainRed` branch). Both comments say the kept pin is re-merged "once main is green". But `requeueMainRedPin` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) puts the pin back on the queue on the first poll where main's head differs from `RunnerState.mainRedRetry.head`. Any merge onto a red main counts as a move, even a docs-only plan merge or a fix that does not fix, so the retry pays a full gate check (224–754 s per `main_red` attempt in the 10-18..10-20 log) and gets `main_red` again. The log shows repeat attempts on one commit: ccf1224e three times on 10-20 07:07–07:28, 313597d9 three times on 10-18 07:04–07:16, and 08eb565e, 6ac7a001 and 1fb03be5 twice each. Today those repeats come mostly from leftover recovery, which the in-flight plan "A change kept by a `main_red` merge waits for main to move…" fixes; once it lands, `requeueMainRedPin` is the only re-queue path, and its "any move" rule is what remains. The main watch (src/baseline/main-watch.ts) runs the full check on every new main head and records the verdict in the baseline cache, so the poll can ask that cache instead of guessing. This change only touches `requeueMainRedPin` and the state record, not leftover.ts, so the two plans can merge in either order.

**Approach.**
- src/merge/merge-slot.ts:
  - Import `cachedBaselineVerdict` from `../baseline/main-baseline.js`.

### Plain terms code run, part 14/20: Convert the event and report and file and text helpers (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 13/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/events/ + src/report/ + src/files/ + src/text/ + their tests + test/fakes/log.ts + test/fixtures/log-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The event readers, report fold, file helpers and text helpers use run names: `eventRun`, `runSpanMs`, `runStartMap`, `runStart` and `runEnd`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):

Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message. `normalizeLegacyEvent`'s map from `tick_*` types to `run_*` types is a legacy reader: its old names stay.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
