### A change kept by a `main_red` merge waits for main to move instead of being re-queued by its author's next run (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20 feature-4's change ccf1224e went through three full gate checks against a red main in 22 minutes. Its `merge_failed main_red` events came at 07:07:06, 07:16:04 and 07:28:47, and the next attempt merged at 07:31. Each failure was followed within 2 s by a `run_start` and a `merge_queued` "recovered leftover work from feature-4: …". feature-5 (07:12, 07:22) and the 10-18 07:04–07:20 cluster (feature-2, feature-3, dedupe) show the same loop. The design already has a wait for this: `requeueKeptChange` (src/merge/merge-slot.ts) records a `main_red` pin as `RunnerState.mainRedRetry = { head, entry }`, and the orchestrator poll's `requeueMainRedPin` re-queues it only once main's head differs. But `recoverLeftover` (src/runner/leftover.ts) never reads `mainRedRetry`. The author's next run, which starts at once because roles keep authoring while main's red names its failing tests, finds the pin with nothing queued and enqueues it straight away, against the same red head. The two comments that promise a wait are wrong today: `attributeRedCheck`'s doc comment (src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts) says "recovery re-merges it once main-red.ts's repair turns main green", and `gateBuildPrecheck`'s main-red branch (src/review/review-precheck.ts) says "the author's next tick re-merges the change once main is green again".

**Approach.**
- src/runner/leftover.ts:
  - `LeftoverContext` gains `mainRedRetry?: RunnerState["mainRedRetry"]`, documented as the record of a `main_red` pin waiting for `requeueMainRedPin`.
  - `LeftoverRecovery` gains `| { kind: "main_red_wait"; sha: string; message: string }`.
  - In `recoverLeftover`, put the new check right after the `reviewHold` check, so the stale and dangling pin drops still run first. When `ctx.mainRedRetry` is set, return `{ kind: "main_red_wait", sha, message: \`kept change ${shortSha(sha)} waits for main to move past red ${shortSha(ctx.mainRedRetry.head)} before its next merge\` }`. Nothing is enqueued and the pin is kept. Add a comment saying that `requeueMainRedPin` owns this re-queue and why: re-queuing against the same red head pays a full gate check whose result is already known.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: pass `mainRedRetry: s.mainRedRetry` in the `recoverLeftover({...})` call. The new kind reaches `ctx.finishRecoveryRun` through the existing `else if (recovered)` arm, so that arm needs no change.
- src/runner/runner-recovery.ts `finishRecoveryRunPhase`: add a branch after the `held` one. When `recovered.kind === "main_red_wait"`, set `ctx.state.lastError = recovered.message` and return `{ result: "main_red", summary: recovered.message, error: recovered.message, recoveredLeftover: true }`. Do not reset the worktree. `main_red` schedules on the idle ladder (the final `else` in src/run/run-apply.ts). The role's status reads "main red" through `heldByMainRed` (src/status/status-polls.ts), and the run's cause is itemized like the authoring gate's `main_red` (INV-C1). Do not use `error`: that would put a wait on the error ladder and count it as a failure.
- No change to `requeueMainRedPin`. It still clears the record and enqueues the entry under its original summary once main's head moves. After that, the role's next run sees `already_queued`, as it does today. If the poll finds the pin gone, the record is cleared, so recovery goes back to its normal path.
- Make the two comments match the code: in `attributeRedCheck`'s doc and `gateBuildPrecheck`'s main-red comment, say the kept pin is re-queued by the orchestrator poll (`requeueMainRedPin`) once main's head moves, and leftover recovery holds it until then.
- Out of scope: waiting for a green verdict rather than any move of main's head. The baseline cache (`cachedBaselineVerdict`, src/baseline/main-baseline.ts) is per process and often has no verdict for a new head yet, so that would be a separate change.

**Files touched.** src/runner/leftover.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/runner/runner-recovery.ts, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts (comment), src/review/review-precheck.ts (comment), test/leftover.test.ts, test/runner-recovery.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/leftover.test.ts, new test "a pin waiting on a main_red retry is held, not re-queued": pin a commit as the existing "a pinned commit not in main is put on the merge queue, not merged" test does. Call `recoverLeftover` with `mainRedRetry: { head: <main's sha>, entry: { role, run: 1, summary: "x", enqueuedAt: 0 } }`. It returns kind `main_red_wait` with the pinned sha, and its message contains `waits for main to move past red`. `queuedMerges(root)` is empty, the merge ref still points at the sha, and no `merge_queued` event is logged. The same call without `mainRedRetry` returns `enqueued`.
- test/leftover.test.ts: with `mainRedRetry` set and a pin that main already contains, the stale pin is still deleted and the call returns null.
- test/runner-recovery.test.ts, beside "finishRecoveryRunPhase ends error on a held pin and keeps its message": a new test "finishRecoveryRunPhase ends main_red on a pin waiting for main to move". The outcome's `result` is `main_red`, its `summary` and `error` are the message, `recoveredLeftover` is true, `state.lastError` is the message, and the worktree reset is not called.
- The existing test/merge-requeue.test.ts test "a main_red pin is re-queued once main's head moves, and not before" passes unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The gate stops rejecting a change for a test that its base commit already failed and main has fixed since (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/review/review-precheck.ts, which the blocked Plain terms code run part 18/20 also edits; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20, between 07:31 and 07:36 UTC, three changes were rejected for one test that their own diffs did not touch: feature (ab6d53e2), feature-2 (c671a472) and feature-5 (08eb565e). Each rejection had 13 reasons, all "check failed (`npm run test:gate`): ✖ report --role takes a comma list and sums the listed roles". Main 13c3c497 was red on that test (`main_red_hold` 07:16). Bugfix's "Make the report --role comma-list test immune to the midnight hour" merged at 07:26, so main's tip a23befe4 was green. The three branches still sat on the red base, so their gate check failed the old test twice. `gateBuildPrecheck` (src/review/review-precheck.ts) then asks only main's tip: `mainTipVerdict(..., true)` returned green, so the failure was blamed on the change and went through `reject`. Main's known-failure excuse (`onlyKnownMainFailures`, src/baseline/main-watch.ts) did not help either. The watch's newest verdict was the green tip, so the known list was empty. The verdict that answers the question is the one for the change's base, and the baseline cache already holds it: the main watch recorded 13c3c497 red, with its `failingTests`.

**Approach.** Only src/review/review-precheck.ts.
- Add a module-private `async function staleBaseFailures(wt: string, mainBranch: string, head: string, mainTip: string, failingTests: readonly string[] | undefined): Promise<{ base: string; tests: string[] } | null>`:
  - Return null when `failingTests` is empty or undefined, or its length is at least `FAILING_TESTS_MAX` (src/build/build-check-report.ts). A list that long may have been cut short, which is the same rule `onlyKnownMainFailures` uses.
  - Take `base = await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch, head)` (src/git/git.ts). Return null when `base === mainTip`, because then the tip verdict already judged the same base.
  - Take `verdict = await watchedBaseline(wt, base)` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts). That is the cached verdict for the base or its nearest first-parent ancestor, and it runs nothing. Return null unless `verdict?.status === "red"` and every failing test is in `verdict.failingTests ?? []`. Otherwise return `{ base, tests: [...failingTests] }`.
  - Wrap the body in try/catch and return null on a throw, so a git problem falls back to today's attribution.
- In `gateBuildPrecheck`, in the main-green branch (after the `main.status === "red"` block, before the `return { resolved: await reject(...) }`), add: when `main.status === "green"`, call `staleBaseFailures(wt, mainBranch, head, main.sha, outcome.failingTests)`. When it returns a result, `warnEventBestEffort(root, role, \`gate check fails only tests its base ${shortSha(base)} already failed, and main ${shortSha(main.sha)} is green: ${tests.join(", ")}; going on to review\`)` and `return { knownMainFailures: tests }`. This is the same hand-off the known-failure branch uses: no `verifiedHead`, so nothing seeds a green. The merge path rebases onto main, and its own merge check judges the rebased tree. If that tree still fails, `attributeRedCheck` sees a green main and rejects as it does today. Add a short comment that names this incident (2026-10-20, report --role) and explains why the tip verdict alone is the wrong question for a branch behind a fix.
- src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts: the `knownMainFailures` paragraph now says "only on tests main already fails — main's known failures, not this change's". That would be false for this case. Reword it to "only on tests main already fails, or that failed at this change's base and pass on main's tip now — not this change's failures". Keep the following "Do not count them against the change unless the diff touches what they test." No test pins the old sentence (`grep -rn "known failures, not this" test` is empty on 2026-10-20).
- Out of scope: the merge-check path (`attributeRedCheck`, src/merge/merge-check-failures.ts). It checks the tree rebased onto main, so its base is main's tip. A base with no cached verdict on it or its ancestors keeps today's rejection.

**Files touched.** src/review/review-precheck.ts, src/prompt/gate-prompts.ts, test/review-precheck.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/review-precheck.test.ts, beside the known-failure tests ("a gate failure of only main's known failures goes on to review with no fresh run on main"):
- Add a fixture `fixedOnMainFixture(alsoY: boolean)`. It follows `gateBuildFixture`'s steps in a different order, because the base has to be red before the worktree branches. The steps: `makeRepo()`; install a `buildcheck-tool` that prints `✖ X (1ms)` when `x-broken.txt` exists in its cwd and `✖ Y (1ms)` when `y.txt` exists, exits 1 if it printed anything and 0 otherwise; write the root `package.json` with `projManifest({ build: "buildcheck-tool" })`. Then commit `x-broken.txt` on main and call `uniqueMain(root)`, so the base SHA is unique to this test (the baseline cache is process-wide). Poll a `createMainWatch(root, "main")` on that tip and await `idle()`, which records the base red with failing test X. Then `ensureWorktree(root, ROLE, "main")`, write the worktree's `package.json`, and commit a change (plus `y.txt` when `alsoY`). Then `git rm x-broken.txt` and commit on main, poll the same watch, and await `idle()`, which records the tip green. The test asserts that `knownMainFailures(root)` is now empty.
- "a gate failure of only tests the change's base already failed goes on to review once main is green": `reviewGate` is approved, the reviewer ran, `result.verifiedHead` is undefined, and the warnings include `gate check fails only tests its base <short base> already failed, and main <short tip> is green: X; going on to review`. No `review_rejected` event is logged.
- "a gate failure beyond the base's red failures is still rejected on a green main": with `alsoY` true, the result is a rejection (a `review_rejected` event whose reasons name Y), and no warning contains "already failed".
- The existing known-failure, red-main and "rejects a failing build with zero reviewer runs" tests pass unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### docs/invariants.md gains a backlog-archive section, so a fixer touching the archive sweep reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Docs only: touches docs/invariants.md, which the in-flight claims entry and the Plain terms parts also edit, so a conflict there only rebases) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** The backlog archive moves finished entries out of PLANS.md / BUGS.md into PLANS-DONE.md / BUGS-FIXED.md: at commit time (`archiveNewFinishedEntries`, called from src/run/run-stage.ts), in bulk (`archiveFinishedOnMain`, behind `tumwater archive` in src/backlog/backlog-cli.ts) and at team start (`archiveAtTeamStart`, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts). Its rules are easy to break and live only in src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts and test/backlog-archive.test.ts. The commit-time sweep moves only what the change added. An entry is never archived twice. A repository with no archive keeps its layout until the bulk archive runs. docs/invariants.md has no section for any of them.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after the last section there when the change is made (the claims section, INV-N, if that entry has merged). Title it `## The backlog archive: finished entries move once, and only the ones a change added`. Use the next free id letter: `O` if INV-N exists or is still planned (the claims entry reserves N). Check with `grep -o 'INV-[A-Z]' docs/invariants.md | sort -u`.
- Add three entries. Each has **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.**, matching the existing entries. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions and state only what they do:
  - `### INV-O1: the commit-time sweep moves only the entries the change added, to the top of the archive`. Guarantee: `archiveFinishedText` with a `baseKeys` selection moves only the finished-section entries whose heading key (`archiveKey`) the change's merge-base did not hold. They go above the archive's existing entries, in their live order. Entries the base already held stay in the live section. A `_None yet._` placeholder and the next section's heading are left in place. `archiveNewFinishedEntries` computes the base from the worktree's merge-base with main. Binds: src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts (`archiveFinishedText`, `archiveNewFinishedEntries`), src/run/run-stage.ts (its call before the commit). Pinned by: test/backlog-archive.test.ts "the commit-time sweep moves only the entries the change added, newest first, into a new archive", "the sweep prepends to an existing archive and leaves entries the base already had", "the sweep keeps a placeholder in the live section and a following section's heading intact" and "archiveNewFinishedEntries writes the move in a worktree against its merge-base".
  - `### INV-O2: an entry the archive already holds is never archived twice`. Guarantee: a selected entry whose heading key the archive already holds does not move (`entryFates`). With the same text (blank edges and trailing whitespace ignored) it is dropped from the live section. With other text it stays in the live section, where the author and the reviewer see it. This holds for the commit-time sweep, the bulk archive whatever it keeps, and `archiveFinishedOnMain`. Binds: src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts (`entryFates`, `entryText`, `archiveFinishedText`, `archiveFinishedOnMain`). Pinned by: test/backlog-archive.test.ts "the sweep drops an added entry the archive holds verbatim and leaves an edited copy in the live section", "a sweep that only finds re-pasted entries empties the live section and leaves the archive as it was", "the bulk archive skips entries the archive already holds, whatever it keeps" and "archiveFinishedOnMain drops a hand commit's re-pasted entries instead of archiving them twice".
  - `### INV-O3: with no archive file, the commit-time sweep leaves a live section that holds older entries as it is`. Guarantee: when the archive file does not exist and the live finished section would still hold other entries after the move, `archiveFinishedText` returns null for a `baseKeys` selection. Nothing is written, so an archive never sits above older live history. The bulk archive (`keep`) still creates the archive from `archiveTemplate`. Binds: src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts (`archiveFinishedText`, `archiveTemplate`). Pinned by: test/backlog-archive.test.ts "the sweep moves nothing while legacy entries sit in the live section and no archive exists" and "the bulk archive moves the whole body, one-line records included, or all but the newest kept entries".
- Do not claim the archive-first write order in `writeMove` (a crash leaves entries in both files, never in neither). No test pins it ("Do not state a guarantee here that no test pins").
- Replace each quoted title above with the test's exact title as it stands when the change is made. Check every one with `grep -nF '<title>' test/backlog-archive.test.ts`. The guard in test/invariants-doc.test.ts fails on a quoted title its cited file does not contain. If a title was renamed, cite the new one. If a test was removed, drop the citation, and if no test then pins a sentence, drop the sentence too. None of the titles above contains "tick", so the Plain terms renames should leave them alone.

**Files touched.** docs/invariants.md only.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n '^### INV-O' docs/invariants.md` (or the letter actually used) lists three entries under the new section, each with the three field labels.
- Every quoted title in the new section is found by `grep -F` in its cited test file.
- Each function named under **Binds.** is found by `grep -n` in the file it is attributed to.
- test/invariants-doc.test.ts passes unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 13/20: Convert the budget and failure modules (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 12/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/budget/ + src/failure/ + their tests; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The budget breaker and the failure digest use run names: `recordFallbackRun`, `RUN_TIMEOUT_KEY` and `prevRuns`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Settled collisions: `runTick` → `runOnce`, `runTimedRoleTick` → `runTimedRoleRun`, `tickModel` → `runModelPair`, `ticksRun` → `runsDone`, `cmdTick` → `cmdRunDetail`.
  - A bare `tick` binding or in-process field holding a run number → `runNumber`; `ticks` holding a count → `runs`, or `runCount` if `runs` is bound in scope. Never shadow an existing binding such as `run`.
  - Keep `backtick*`, `process.nextTick`, `processTicksAndRejections`, `sticky`, node:test mock-clock `tick(ms)` calls and their helpers, and serialized names; name any leftover serialized name in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - Comments and test titles: "tick" → "run" (and "ticks", "ticked", "mid-tick", "per-tick" alike), `tumwater tick <role> <n>` → `tumwater history <role> <n>`, `tumwater run` → `tumwater start`. A bare noun "run" meaning one agent invocation → "agent run". Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - An export used outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen, unless it has about five or fewer outside use lines, which you migrate instead. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Members get no alias. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias nothing else names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts and budget.ts: `recordFallbackTick` → `recordFallbackRun` and `recordFallbackTickAt` → `recordFallbackRunAt` (aliased if the orchestrator still names them, otherwise migrate its two uses). Comments.
- src/failure/ (failure-data.ts, time-spend.ts, failure-render.ts, failure-cluster.ts, failure-state-change.ts): `TICK_TIMEOUT_KEY` → `RUN_TIMEOUT_KEY`, `TICK_TIMEOUT_PROGRESSING_KEY`, `TICK_TIMEOUT_PROGRESSING_REVIEW_KEY` and `TICK_TIMEOUT_PROGRESSING_REVIEW_RESUME_KEY` → `RUN_TIMEOUT_…` (migrate their uses in src/team/). These are names of in-process cluster keys; if a key's string value is persisted or printed, leave the value, which Plain terms text or event log owns. The `RoleStats` member `prevTicks` → `prevRuns`; locals `tickEvents` → `runEvents` and `tickEnd` → `runEnd`. The failure digest's comments speak of "the telemetry role"; that role id is Plain terms code cleanup's.
- Tests: test/budget*.test.ts, test/fallback-breaker.test.ts, test/failure*.test.ts and test/time-spend.test.ts.

**Files touched.** src/budget/*.ts, src/failure/*.ts, the `TICK_TIMEOUT_*` uses in src/team/, and the tests listed above.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `recordFallbackRun`, `recordFallbackRunAt` and `RUN_TIMEOUT_KEY` are declared; old names survive only as aliases still used elsewhere.
- `grep -rnE '[Tt]ick[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Tick|TICK_|\bticks?\b' src/budget src/failure` prints only aliases and serialized names.

### A commit body's WHY, RISK and VERIFIED lines are kept whole up to 1000 characters, so a reviewer stops rejecting a change because the harness cut its own RISK line mid-sentence (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/git/commit-message.ts and test/commit-message.test.ts, which no Planned entry names; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `extractCommitBody` (src/git/commit-message.ts) caps each of WHY, RISK and VERIFIED at `COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX = 200` characters with `truncate`, which ends a cut line with "…". At that size the cap cuts ordinary answers, not just verbose ones. In the 1306 commits on main since 2026-10-13, 1554 of the 3741 `WHY:`/`RISK:`/`VERIFIED:` lines end in "…". 1344 of them are exactly 200 characters long and 210 are 199 (`truncate` trims a trailing space before the ellipsis). Reviewers read that commit message and reject the change over it. Between 2026-10-19 08:58 and 2026-10-20 00:57 UTC there were seven `review_rejected` reasons from feature-3 and feature-5 like "WHY, RISK and VERIFIED each end mid-sentence with "…" in the commit message itself" and "the RISK list stops at `` (`src/… ``". They came from Plain-terms parts whose series rules ask for any leftover name to be listed in the commit message. The author cannot fix this in a revision: each new round truncates the line again. The cap exists so that a verbose model cannot bloat every commit. 1000 characters still does that job and fits a full list of leftovers.

**Approach.**
- **src/git/commit-message.ts.** Set `COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX` to `1000`. Reword its doc comment to give the reason: the cap only bounds a runaway reply, and at 200 it cut almost half of all body lines, which reviewers rejected as incomplete claims. Change "capped at 200 chars" in `extractCommitBody`'s doc comment to name the constant. Leave the rest as it is: `truncate` still cuts a field that is over the cap. `parseCommitMetadata` re-extracts the body through `extractCommitBody`, so leftover recovery reads a whole field back under the same cap. Leave `COMMIT_SUMMARY_MAX`, `summaryOverCap` and `SUMMARY_BLOCK` (src/verdict/reply-contract.ts) alone. This plan adds no follow-up turn for an over-long body field.
- **test/commit-message.test.ts.** Rename "extractCommitBody caps each field at 200 chars with an ellipsis" to "extractCommitBody caps each field at 1000 chars with an ellipsis". Feed it a 1500-character WHY, and assert the result is exactly 1000 characters long, ends in "…", and leaves RISK untouched. Add "extractCommitBody keeps a 600-character field whole": a 600-character RISK made of words and spaces comes back unchanged, with no "…".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n 'COMMIT_BODY_FIELD_MAX = ' src/git/commit-message.ts` shows `1000`. `grep -rn '200 chars' src/git/commit-message.ts` finds nothing.
- Both tests named above pass. Every other test in test/commit-message.test.ts passes without edits, including "extractCommitBody pulls all three fields, trimmed" and "extractCommitBody tolerates any subset and returns null when none are present".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### docs/invariants.md gains a claims section, so a fixer touching claim assignment or part dependencies reads what they promise instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Docs only: touches docs/invariants.md, which the in-flight fallback-breaker entry and the Plain terms parts also edit, so a conflict there only rebases) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** Claims decide which work-role instance takes which backlog entry. Their guarantees live in src/scheduling/claims.ts (`assignNext`, `heldKeys`, `claimReleaseReason`) and src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts (`entryHoldAgainst`, `requiredParts`, `eligibleEntries`), and docs/invariants.md has no section for them. The rules are easy to break and hard to rebuild from the code: the queue is file order, a dependency holds only in the `requires part N/M landed` heading form, and a release rule depends on whether the runner is idle. A fixer has to piece them together from three test files today.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after the last section there when the change is made. If the fallback-breaker entry has merged, that is its INV-M section. Title it `## Claims: one entry, one holder, in queue order`. Use the next free id letter: `N` if INV-M exists or is still planned (the fallback-breaker entry reserves M), checked with `grep -o 'INV-[A-Z]' docs/invariants.md | sort -u`.
- Add three entries. Each has **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.**, matching the existing entries. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions and state only what they do:
  - `### INV-N1: each listed, eligible entry has at most one claim holder, and assignment takes the first free entry in file order`. Guarantee: `assignNext` returns the first free entry in `## Planned` / `## Open` file order. `heldKeys` keeps every same-base claim that is still listed and eligible out of the free set, and a busy base runner with no claim holds the group. `eligibleEntries` drops an entry claimed by another base role, but keeps the queried base's own claims. Binds: src/scheduling/claims.ts (`assignNext`, `heldKeys`), src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts (`eligibleEntries`), src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts (the scheduling poll that calls `assignNext`). Pinned by: test/claims.test.ts "assignNext takes the first free entry in file order" and "heldKeys counts a claim still listed and eligible and drops the rest"; test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts "two feature instances take distinct entry claims in one poll" and "a busy unclaimed base holds the group so a new instance cannot take its entry"; test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts "eligibleEntries holds a plan another role's base has claimed, but keeps the owner's own claim".
  - `### INV-N2: a plan is held while a prerequisite named in its heading's requires clause is still planned, and only that clause holds it`. Guarantee: `entryHoldAgainst` holds an entry whose heading's trailing parenthetical (or a parenthetical left open by a wrapped heading) names, through `requiredParts`, a part still listed under `## Planned`. Once no named part is planned, the hold lifts. A `requires` mention in the body never holds. A note line (Refused, Needs review, Needs replan, Waiting for the next failure) holds as well. `planDependencyProblems` reports a still-planned prerequisite named without the clause. Binds: src/backlog/backlog-eligibility.ts (`requiredParts`, `entryHoldAgainst`, `prerequisitesMerged`, `planDependencyProblems`), src/run/stage-check.ts and src/doctor/doctor-backlog.ts (where the wording problem is reported; confirm both call sites with grep). Pinned by: test/backlog-eligibility.test.ts "requiredParts reads the trailing parenthetical, expands ranges, and resolves bare refs to the own series", "a body mentioning 'requires' never blocks — only the heading's clause does", "entryHold blocks a wrapped heading while its prerequisite is planned", "prerequisitesMerged returns the refs only when none is still planned", "entryHold reports blocked, refused, needs-review and needs-replan, and null when eligible", "a waiting-for-the-next-failure note holds a bug, only as a line prefix" and "planDependencyProblems flags a still-planned prerequisite named without a requires clause".
  - `### INV-N3: a claim on an entry that left or turned ineligible is released outright; disabled, paused and stale release only an idle runner`. Guarantee: `claimReleaseReason` returns `left` or `ineligible` whatever the runner is doing. It returns `disabled`, `paused` (own instance id paused while the base role is not) or `stale` (idle past `CLAIM_IDLE_MAX_MS`) only for an idle runner: one that is not running and has no queued merge and no outstanding work. Pausing the whole base role keeps every claim. A released claim is saved before the runner runs again. Binds: src/scheduling/claims.ts (`claimReleaseReason`, `CLAIM_IDLE_MAX_MS`), src/runner/runner-state.ts (`hasOutstandingWork`). Pinned by: test/claims.test.ts "claimReleaseReason releases left, ineligible, disabled-idle, paused-idle and stale-idle claims" and "an idle extra with a revision, a queued merge, a resume or a run in progress keeps its claim"; test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts "a claimed entry that merges releases the claim on the next poll", "pausing one instance releases its claim so a sibling can take the entry", "pausing the whole feature role keeps every instance's claim" and "a released claim is saved to disk before the runner runs again".
- Cite only test titles that do not contain "tick". The Plain terms series renames "tick" in test titles, including in test/backlog-*.test.ts, test/orchestrator*.test.ts and src/scheduling/, so a "tick" title cited now would break the citation guard when a later part merges. The titles above contain no "tick" today.
- Replace each quoted title above with the test's exact title as it stands when the change is made. Check every one with `grep -nF '<title>' <file>`. The guard in test/invariants-doc.test.ts fails on a quoted title its cited file does not contain. If a title was renamed, cite the new one. If a test was removed, drop the citation, and if no test pins a sentence, drop the sentence too ("Do not state a guarantee here that no test pins").

**Files touched.** docs/invariants.md only.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `grep -n '^### INV-N' docs/invariants.md` (or the letter actually used) lists three entries under the new section, each with the three field labels.
- Every quoted title in the new section is found by `grep -F` in its cited test file, and none of them contains the word "tick".
- Each function named under **Binds.** is found by `grep -n` in the file it is attributed to.
- test/invariants-doc.test.ts passes unedited, including its check that this repo's register resolves every citation.

### docs/invariants.md gains a fallback-breaker section, so a fixer touching the breaker reads what it promises instead of rebuilding it from tests (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** The fallback breaker (src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts) decides whether the engaged free fallback is still allowed to serve. Its guarantees are spread across eight test files and several modules. After the 2026-10-20 merge "A window move's runs feed the fallback breaker…" it also binds the window-move path in src/gates/gate-polls.ts and src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts. docs/invariants.md has no section for any of this (`grep -n -i 'breaker' docs/invariants.md` finds only the one INV-F1 citation of test/orchestrator-probe.test.ts). That register exists so a fixer reads a subsystem's contract before changing its code. Without a section, a breaker fix has no guarantee to check against, and a change that breaks one is caught only if its test happens to fail. This plan adds the section. It is docs only: every guarantee must already be pinned by an existing test. No code or test changes.

**Approach.**
- Append a new section at the end of docs/invariants.md, after `## Main's red culprit`. Title it `## The fallback breaker: a free fallback that cannot serve is demoted, not retried forever`. Give it a two- or three-sentence intro in the register's style (see the intros under `## Bounded waits…` and `## Hermetic, deterministic gating tests`). Use the next free letter, `M`; `grep -n 'INV-M' docs/invariants.md` must find nothing first.
- Add three entries. Each has **Guarantee.**, **Binds.** and **Pinned by.**, matching the existing entries. Before writing each guarantee, read the named functions' doc comments and the cited tests. State only what the code does: if a detail below turns out wrong, correct the sentence to match the code rather than the plan.
  - `### INV-M1: consecutive fallback failures demote the fallback, and a demoted fallback admits one probe run per cool-down`. Guarantee: `FALLBACK_BREAKER_POLICY.failureLimit` consecutive `error` outcomes on an engaged fallback pair demote it. The count is team-wide; any served run in between resets the streak. While the pair is demoted, `fallbackServing` is false and roles on it are paused. After the cool-down, exactly one probe run is admitted while other due roles wait. A served probe closes the breaker. A failed probe re-opens it with the cool-down doubled, capped at `maxCooldownMs`. A probe that never ran, or produced no evidence, hands its slot back. Binds: src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts (`fallbackServing`, `fallbackProbeDue`, `startFallbackProbe`, `abandonFallbackProbe`), src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts. Pinned by: test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts "a free fallback whose runs keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves"; test/orchestrator-probe.test.ts "a demoted fallback admits exactly one probe run per cool-down; other due roles wait"; test/budget.test.ts "each failed probe doubles the cool-down up to its cap; a probe with no evidence frees the slot"; test/fallback-breaker.test.ts "fallbackServing is false exactly while the breaker holds a demotion, probe included"; test/orchestrator-launch.test.ts "a probe turned away by the held start gate has its claim handed back".
  - `### INV-M2: a change of subject re-trusts the fallback`. Guarantee: editing the cap, changing the fallback pair, or the gate leaving the fallback (local midnight) replaces a demoted breaker with a fresh, trusted one on the next poll. Evidence about a pair that is no longer engaged is dropped. Binds: src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts (`rekeyFallbackBreaker`, `rekeyFallbackBreakers`), src/gates/gate-polls.ts. Pinned by: test/fallback-breaker.test.ts "rekey keeps the same breaker while the subject is unchanged, re-trusts on any change"; test/budget.test.ts "rekeyFallbackBreaker clears a demotion when the cap, the pair, or the day changes"; test/budget.test.ts "a served straggler closes a demoted breaker; evidence about another subject is dropped".
  - `### INV-M3: runs a window move put on a fallback feed the breaker below the cap, and its demotion holds the moved tier`. Guarantee: when a used-up claude window moves tiers to a fallback pair, those roles' run outcomes fold into that pair's breaker even though the daily cap is not reached. A demoted pair holds the moved tier's roles, with the same one-probe admission as INV-M1. Binds: src/gates/gate-polls.ts (`pollTeamGates`, its `windowMovedRoles`), src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts. Pinned by: test/gate-polls.test.ts "pollTeamGates: a used-up window's demoted fallback holds the moved tier's roles below the cap"; test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts "a window move's failing fallback is demoted and its tier held, below the cap".
- Cite only test titles that do not contain "tick". The Plain-terms series (PLANS.md parts 12/20–20/20) renames "tick" in test titles and in `recordFallbackTick`. Avoiding those keeps this section out of its sweep. For the same reason, do not name `recordFallbackTick` in the prose: say "the evidence fold" instead.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a finished entry that the archive already holds under another done date, so a revision stops being rejected for leaving the same plan twice in PLANS-DONE.md or in both PLANS.md and its archive (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts, which the in-flight stale-name self-check plan also edits; whichever lands second only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** Between 2026-10-19 08:58 and 2026-10-20 13:22 UTC, seven `review_rejected` events from feature instances were for one finished entry recorded twice. Three examples: "`PLANS-DONE.md` now has the same plan entry twice. Line 8 says "done 2026-10-20 by the feature role" and line 23 says "done 2026-10-19 by the feature role"" (feature, 10-20 07:38); "`PLANS-DONE.md` has the "Pi built-in image capability, part 2/2" entry twice (lines 8 and 38), left over from this revision's `PLANS.md` conflict resolution" (feature-2, 07:40); "The finished plan entry "A window move's runs feed the fallback breaker…" appears in both `PLANS.md` `## Done` and `PLANS-DONE.md`, and the two copies disagree" (feature-2, 13:22). Each one cost a review round and a revision. Today's guards miss both shapes because they compare whole headings (src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts `archiveKey`, src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts `readdedHeadings`):
- A revision re-finishes its plan with a new `done` date. The heading differs from the archived copy's, so the commit-time sweep (`archiveNewFinishedEntries`, called in src/run/run-stage.ts after the self-check) moves it as a new entry, and `readdedHeadings` sees no repeat.
- The heading matches but the text differs. `entryFates` then gives the entry the `stay` fate, which is by design: the sweep leaves it in `PLANS.md ## Done` for the reviewer to see, and the reviewer rejects it.

The self-check runs before the sweep, while the author can still fix the change in one fix-up turn, so it is the place to catch both.

**Approach.** Only src/run/stage-check.ts.
- Add `finishedKey(title: string, dateRe: RegExp): string`, which returns `collapseWhitespace(finishedTitle(title, dateRe))`. `finishedTitle` is in src/backlog/backlog-structure.ts and `collapseWhitespace` is in src/text/text.ts. The key drops the completion stamp and the `(planned …)`/`(found …)` parenthetical, so "X (planned …; done 2026-10-19 …)" and "X (planned …; done 2026-10-20 …)" key equal. It also handles a heading whose done date wraps onto the next line: an unclosed `(` is cut.
- Add the exported pure function `finishedDuplicateFindings(spec: FinishedArchive, live: { head: string; base: string }, archive: { head: string; base: string }): string[]`. `FinishedArchive` comes from src/backlog/backlog-md.ts. Use `DONE_DATE_RE` for PLANS.md and `FIXED_DATE_RE` for BUGS.md (both from src/backlog/backlog.ts). Read entries with `parseEntryDetails(md, spec.section)`. It returns at most one finding per rule:
  - **Live copy of an archived entry.** Find the first entry under the head live file's `spec.section` whose key is (1) absent from the base live file's `spec.section` keys and (2) held by an entry under the head archive's `spec.section`. Skip it when one of those archived entries has the same whitespace-collapsed heading and the same `body`, because the sweep drops that exact copy (`drop` fate). Wording: `` `${spec.file}`'s "## ${spec.section}" entry "${truncate(title, 160)}" is already archived in ${spec.archive} — the commit-time sweep would leave two copies; edit the archived entry in place (its text and its stamp) and delete this copy ``.
  - **Second archive copy.** Find the first key whose count under the head archive's `spec.section` is above 1 and above its count in the base archive. Skip this rule when `readdedHeadings(archive.base, archive.head)` is non-empty, because `backlogStructureReason` already reports that case. Wording: `` `${spec.archive} holds "${truncate(title, 160)}" ${n} times — this change added a copy under a different heading or stamp; keep the archived entry once, edited in place, and delete the other copies` ``. Use the first head copy's title. `truncate` comes from src/text/text.ts.
- In `stageCheckFindings`, after the `PLANS.md` dependency block, loop over `FINISHED_ARCHIVES` (src/backlog/backlog-md.ts). For each `spec` where `files` includes `spec.file` or `spec.archive`, read both heads with `readTextOrNull(path.join(wt, …)) ?? ""` and both bases with `fileContentAt(wt, await changeBaseRev(wt, mainBranch), …)`. Wrap the whole block in `.catch(() => [])`, matching the module's rule that a git hiccup yields no finding. Push the returned findings.
- Add a sentence to the module header comment: like `planDependencyFinding`, `finishedDuplicateFindings` runs only at staging. The gate does not run it, because the sweep that creates the second copy runs after it.
- Out of scope: changing the sweep's `archiveKey` or `entryFates` (an edited archived entry legitimately stays visible to the reviewer), and repairing duplicates already on main. Checked 2026-10-20: PLANS-DONE.md has none under this key, and BUGS-FIXED.md has one pair, which the base-count comparison never flags.

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts:
- A unit test, "finishedDuplicateFindings flags a re-finished plan that the archive holds under another done date", calls `finishedDuplicateFindings(FINISHED_ARCHIVES[0], …)` on hand-built markdown. The head PLANS.md `## Done` holds "### X (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)" with some body. The base live file is empty. Both the head and base archives hold "### X (planned 2026-10-18 by the plan role; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)" with another body. Exactly one finding matches `/PLANS\.md's "## Done" entry "X .*" is already archived in PLANS-DONE\.md/`.
- In the same test: when the live copy has the archived copy's exact heading and body, the result is `[]`. When the base live file already had X under `## Done`, the result is `[]`.
- "finishedDuplicateFindings flags a second archive copy under a new stamp, and leaves an exact re-paste to the structure check": the head archive holds X twice with two different done dates, and the base holds it once. Exactly one finding matches `/PLANS-DONE\.md holds "X .*" 2 times/`. A head that adds an exact copy of the base heading gives `[]`. A base that already held two copies and a head that still holds two gives `[]`.
- A BUGS.md case: a head `## Fixed` entry "### Y (found by the qa role 2026-10-18) — fixed 2026-10-20 by the bugfix role", while BUGS-FIXED.md holds Y "— fixed 2026-10-19 by the bugfix role". It yields the live-copy finding naming BUGS-FIXED.md.
- An integration test, "a re-finished plan the archive already holds yields the finished-duplicate finding". It is built with `repoWith` like "a duplicated ## Done heading yields the structure finding". The repo commits PLANS.md (empty `## Done`) and PLANS-DONE.md holding X under `## Done`. The worktree pastes X with a new done date into PLANS.md `## Done`. `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` returns exactly one finding, the live-copy one.
- The existing stage-check tests pass unedited, including "a duplicated ## Done heading yields the structure finding" and "a clean change yields no findings".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code run, part 12/20: Rename the scheduler's deferral and wake names and convert the gates (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 11/20 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/scheduling/ + src/gates/ + their tests + test/fixtures/gate-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The scheduler and the gates use run names: `deferRun`, `deferRunReason`, `restoreMidRunWake` and `runOnPair`.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-run part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "tick": `tick`/`Tick`/`TICK` → `run`/`Run`/`RUN`, `ticks` → `runs`, `ticked` → `ran`. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.

### A window move's runs feed the fallback breaker, so a dead window fallback is demoted and its tier held instead of failing every run until the window resets (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** At 06:11 UTC on 2026-10-20 the claude usage window ran out, and `fallback_switched` (reason `window`) moved the small, default and strong tiers to `qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b`. That endpoint was down. For the next 29 minutes the moved runs kept failing with "Connection error.", and the team-wide `rate_limit_hold` on `qwenrunner` escalated through holds of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 15 minutes. The tiers stayed on that step until the window reset at 06:40 (`fallback_switched` reason `available`). The fallback breaker (src/budget/fallback-breaker.ts) exists to demote a free fallback whose runs keep failing, then let a probe through after a cool-down. But it only learns from runs made while the daily cap is reached. In `launchDueRuns` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts), `ranPair` is non-null only when `budgetActive`. The input's own doc comment gives the reason: "only a budget hold puts role runs on fallback pairs". A window move below the cap also puts role runs on fallback pairs, so its runs never reach the breaker. Every price-free chain step already has a breaker entry (`chainPairs` in `pollBudgetGate`, src/gates/budget-gates.ts), and the `chain` block already resolves through `servingResolved`. A demotion would therefore already log `fallback_switched` with reason `demoted`. The only missing pieces are the evidence and the per-tier hold.

**Approach.**
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts, `pollTeamGates`: compute `windowMovedRoles`. It is the set of non-director runners whose `roleSeamTier(liveConfig, r.role)` is a key of the budget gate's `windowTiers`, and it is empty while `windowTiers` is empty. A role whose own seam is not claude (pinned to another model) keeps its model through the move, so it is left out. Return it beside `budgetActive`, with a doc comment on the result type: the roles a window move put on a fallback pair, whose run outcomes fold into the breaker even below the cap.
- In the same function, extend the `budgetPausedRoles` loop. Today it runs only `if (budgetActive)`. Keep that branch as it is, and add an `else` branch: a role in `windowMovedRoles` whose `servingResolved[roleSeamTier(liveConfig, r.role)].pair === null` joins `budgetPausedRoles`. Below the cap a role on an unmoved tier is never added. The scheduling pass already folds `budgetPausedRoles` and lets `probeRoles` pierce it (`pollDeferralInputs` and the `budgetPausedRoles.has(role) && !probeRoles.has(role)` check in src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts), so the probe needs no change. Update the `budgetPausedRoles` doc comment to cover the window case.
- src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts: add `windowMovedRoles: ReadonlySet<string>` to `LaunchContext` beside `budgetActive`. Change the `ranPair` condition to `(budgetActive || windowMovedRoles.has(runner.role)) && cfg?.model !== undefined`, and leave the rest of the fold unchanged. A pair with no breaker entry is still skipped by `ranOn !== undefined`. Update the `budgetActive` doc comment, which says only a budget hold puts runs on fallback pairs. src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts passes `gates.windowMovedRoles` next to `gates.budgetActive`.
- Out of scope: `reviewStrongPaused` stays cap-only, so a demoted strong window step still serves the reviewer until the window resets. Leave the breaker's rekey and policy, `budget_paused`/`budget_fallback` (cap-only events) and the hand-back alone.

**Files touched.** src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, test/gate-polls.test.ts, test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/gate-polls.test.ts, "pollTeamGates: a used-up window's demoted fallback holds the moved tier's roles below the cap". Set it up like "a used-up claude window moves claude roles to the fallback and hands them back at the reset": `writeClaudeAccount` with a rejected `five_hour` window, a claude tier, a free fallback, and spend under the cap. Seed `states.budget.breakers[<fallback pair>]` as demoted (`failures: 3, probeAt: <now + 60_000>`), the way "budgetPausedRoles holds the tiers that resolved to pause…" seeds its breaker. Assert that the moved role is in `windowMovedRoles` and in `budgetPausedRoles`, and that the director is in neither. With the breaker entry trusted (`IDLE_FALLBACK_BREAKER`), the moved role is in `windowMovedRoles` but not in `budgetPausedRoles`. With no used-up window, `windowMovedRoles` is empty.
- New e2e test in test/orchestrator-budget.e2e.test.ts, "a window move's failing fallback is demoted and its tier held, below the cap". Model it on "a free fallback whose ticks keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves". Use a tier `{ provider: "claude", model: "claude-opus-5-5" }`, the fallback `local/local-free` (failing until `healed`), a cap that is never reached, and a rejected `five_hour` window written with `writeClaudeAccount`. Use `fallbackBreakerPolicy: { failureLimit: 2, cooldownMs: 1500, maxCooldownMs: 1500 }`. Assert that after two failed fallback runs a `fallback_switched` event with a tier `to: null` appears (reason `demoted` needs a further chain step: with a lone fallback the tier resolves to no pair, so the event reads `to: null`) and no further role run starts while demoted. After `healed` is written, one probe run on `model=local-free` serves and the tier is back on the fallback. If startup refuses because the claude binary is missing, put the fake claude from test/orchestrator-mixed.e2e.test.ts on PATH. The moved roles never run on it.
- The existing tests "a free fallback whose ticks keep failing is demoted to a pause, then probed back once it serves" and "budgetPausedRoles holds the tiers that resolved to pause, and every demotion is published" pass unedited.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The invariants register's guard checks each quoted test title against the cited test file, so a renamed test can no longer leave a **Pinned by.** citation pointing at nothing (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches test/invariants-doc.test.ts and docs/invariants.md; a Plain terms part that also edits docs/invariants.md only rebases) — done 2026-10-20 by the feature role

**Goal.** docs/invariants.md's "Keep it honest" paragraph promises that "a stale citation is a visible broken link, not silent drift". `invariantProblems` (test/invariants-doc.test.ts) keeps that promise only for paths: it reports a missing field, a malformed or duplicate id and a cited path that does not exist. It never reads the quoted test titles that each **Pinned by.** field names after its `test/*.test.ts` path, and the tick→run renames have already broken two of them. INV-C1 quotes "a main_red tick's cause is clustered with the tick errors, not left a bare count", but test/failure-render.test.ts now titles that case "a main_red tick's cause is clustered with the run errors, not left a bare count". INV-J1 quotes "a blind image read fails the tick with an error naming the file and the model", but test/run-verdict.test.ts now says "fails the run". The remaining Plain terms parts rename many more test titles, so a guard is needed before more citations drift.

**Approach.** Test file and doc only. No src change.
- In test/invariants-doc.test.ts, add `TITLE_RE`, which matches a `test(`, `it(` or `describe(` call (optionally `.skip`/`.only`/`.todo`) whose first argument is a `"…"`, `'…'` or `` `…` `` literal, and `testTitles(source: string): string[]`, which returns each title with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. A template-literal title keeps its `${…}` placeholders. test/run-stage.test.ts titles its cases `` `a commit made in the ${label} follow-up folds into the harness commit` ``, and INV-H1 cites two expansions of that title.
- Add `titleMatches(cited: string, title: string): boolean`. It returns true when the two are equal. It also returns true when `cited` ends with `…` and `title` starts with the text before the ellipsis, because INV-L1 cites "a named culprit is reverted on main…". Finally, it returns true when `title` has `${…}` placeholders and `cited` matches the title with each placeholder read as a non-empty wildcard (the literal parts regex-escaped and the match anchored at both ends).
- Add `citedTitles(pinned: string): { file: string; title: string }[]` over the text from `**Pinned by.**` to the entry's end. Scan it with one alternation, `` /`([^`]*)`|"([^"]+)"/g ``. A backtick code span is consumed whole: if it is a `test/….test.ts` path it becomes the current file, otherwise it is skipped. This keeps the quotes inside a span such as INV-A4's `` `helpTopic("config")` `` from counting as a title. A `"…"` quote after a current file is a cited title, with its whitespace collapsed, since titles wrap across doc lines. A quote before any test path is ignored.
- `invariantProblems` takes an optional `readTest: (rel: string) => string | undefined`, which defaults to reading `path.join(ROOT, rel)` and returning `undefined` when the file is missing. For each cited title whose file reads, and where no `testTitles` entry satisfies `titleMatches`, it pushes `` `${label}: cited test title not found in ${file}: "${title}"` ``. A missing file is already reported by the path check, so no title problem is added for it.
- Fix the citations that the new check finds in docs/invariants.md, using the titles the tests carry when the change is made. Today those are the INV-C1 and INV-J1 citations quoted above. Run the guard to get the current list, because an in-flight Plain terms part may rename more.
- Extend the "Keep it honest" paragraph in docs/invariants.md by one sentence: each title quoted after a cited test path must name a test in that file, and a trailing `…` cites by prefix.

**Files touched.** test/invariants-doc.test.ts, docs/invariants.md.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/invariants-doc.test.ts, built with the file's `register`/`entry` helpers or with hand-built markdown as "a test path cited outside **Pinned by.** does not satisfy the pin check" does, and passing a `readTest` stub so no fixture file is written:
- "a quoted title that no test in the cited file carries is reported": the stub serves `test("the real title", …)`, and the entry cites "the old title". There is exactly one problem, and it names the entry, the file and "the old title". Citing "the real title" yields `[]`.
- "a wrapped, truncated or template-expanded citation matches its test": a citation split across two lines matches. A citation of "the real…" matches `test("the real title", …)`. A citation of "a commit made in the missing-SUMMARY follow-up folds" matches `` test(`a commit made in the ${label} follow-up folds`, …) ``, and a citation of "a commit made in the  follow-up folds" (empty placeholder) does not.
- "quotes inside a code span and before any test path are not titles": a **Pinned by.** field reading `` `test/x.test.ts` — "the real title" (reads `helpTopic("config")`) `` yields `[]`. So does a quote placed before the first test path.
- The existing test "this repo's docs/invariants.md is honest" passes against the corrected doc, with its assertion unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The pre-queue self-check flags a removed identifier that a comment or doc still names, so a rename stops being rejected for a comment pointing at a name that no longer exists (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry. Touches src/run/stage-check.ts and test/stage-check.test.ts; a blocked Plain terms part that also edits them only rebases; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** In the 48 hours to 13:15 UTC on 2026-10-20 there were 205 `review_rejected` events. Several were for a leftover name that a mechanical check could have caught before the change queued. Two from 2026-10-20: "`src/run/run-timing.ts:233` still says `tickStartHeld`, which this change renamed to `runStartHeld`" (feature-2, 11:45), and "`src/redeploy/redeploy-policy.ts:91` … still says … `abortedTicks`. The field the redeployer emits is `abortedRuns`" (feature-2, 11:56). The 11:52 review of the same change rejected it for "a comment points at a name that no longer exists". The compiler catches code that still uses a removed name, but nothing catches a comment, an assertion message or a doc that still names it. Each one costs a gate check, a review and a revision. The pre-queue self-check (`stageCheckFindings`, src/run/stage-check.ts) already does this for paths: `staleReferenceFindings` reports a renamed or deleted path that is still named in the tree, and `requestStageFix` (src/run/run-stage.ts) gives the author one fix-up turn while its session is still open. This plan adds the same check for identifiers.

**Approach.** Only src/run/stage-check.ts.
- Add `staleNameFindings(wt: string, diff: string): Promise<string[]>`. Call it from `gitLevelFindings` on the `-U0` cached diff that function already computes, after `newlineFindings`. It is best-effort like its siblings: a git failure contributes nothing.
- Candidates: walk the diff, tracking the current file from `+++ ` headers as `missingPathFindings` does. Removed lines start with `-` but not `---`. A removed line belongs to the file named by the b-path of the last `diff --git a/<x> b/<y>` header. That path is used rather than `+++ `, which reads `/dev/null` for a deleted file, and only its extension matters. Only removed lines in `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js` and `.mjs` files count. Take the names declared there with an exported `declaredNames(line: string): string[]`, which uses two patterns:
  - keyword declarations `\b(?:function\*?|const|let|var|class|interface|type|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)`;
  - property or field signatures at the start of the line, `^\s*(?:(?:readonly|public|private|protected|static)\s+)*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\??\s*:`.

  Keep a name only if it is compound, so common words never count: it contains a lowercase letter followed by an uppercase letter (`tickStartHeld`, `RunnerState`), or it is UPPER_SNAKE with at least one underscore (`MAX_STALE_HITS`). Drop every name that `declaredNames` also finds on an added `+` line anywhere in the diff, because the change re-declared it, for example by moving it. Cap the candidate set at `MAX_STALE_NAMES = 40` in first-appearance order.
- One `gitTry(wt, "grep", "-n", "-w", "-I", "--cached", "-e", n1, "-e", n2, …)` call covers every candidate. Attribute each hit line to the candidates it contains as a whole word. A candidate is still live, and is dropped, when any hit line in a `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` file declares it according to `declaredNames`. Another module may still own the name. For each remaining candidate, keep the hits that pass all three filters:
  - the file is not record prose (`isRecordProse`);
  - the line does not carry `retired-name-ok`;
  - the occurrence is not inside a `"…"` or `'…'` string literal. Legacy-name tables and serialized keys spell old names as strings on purpose. Backticked names in comments and markdown still count.
- Emit one finding per name, at most `MAX_STALE_PATHS` names and `MAX_STALE_HITS` hits each, worded like the path finding: `` `tickStartHeld` was removed by this change but is still named at: src/run/run-timing.ts:233 ``. Use `cappedList` for the hits.
- Extend the module's header comment (the "Part 2/2 appends git-level … findings" paragraph) with this fourth check and the reasons for its exemptions.
- Out of scope:
  - test titles that docs quote (docs/invariants.md citations are test/invariants-doc.test.ts's concern);
  - non-JS languages;
  - the review gate (like the other git-level checks, this one is a staging-time heuristic and the gate does not run it).

**Files touched.** src/run/stage-check.ts, test/stage-check.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.** New tests in test/stage-check.test.ts, built with `repoWith` and `stageCheckFindings(wt, "main", EXEMPT, "feature")` like "a remaining reference to a renamed path yields the stale-reference finding":
- "a comment still naming a renamed function yields the stale-name finding": `src/a.ts` holds `export function tickStartHeld() {}` and `src/b.ts` holds `// see tickStartHeld\n`. The worktree renames the function to `runStartHeld` in a.ts. Exactly one finding matches `` /`tickStartHeld` was removed by this change but is still named at: src\/b\.ts:1/ ``. Updating the comment as well leaves `[]`.
- "a removed interface field still named in a doc yields the finding": the field `abortedTicks: number;` is renamed in an interface, and README.md still names it. The finding names README.md.
- "a removed name that is still declared elsewhere, quoted as a string, marked retired-name-ok or named in record prose yields no stale-name finding": four sub-cases, each giving `[]`. In the first, the name is still declared in another src file. In the second, the remaining hit is `"tickStartHeld"` in a string. In the third, the hit line carries `// retired-name-ok: …`. In the fourth, the hit is in PLANS.md.
- "a removed single-word name is never a candidate": removing `const status = 1;` while a comment says "status" gives `[]`.
- A `declaredNames` unit test covers `export const FOO_BAR`, `async function fooBar(`, `interface FooBar {`, `  readonly fooBar?: string;`, and a call line `fooBar(x);`, which yields nothing.
- The existing stale-reference, missing-path and newline tests pass unedited. So does "the git-level check leaves the index clean, so change detection still sees the worktree".
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI's per-key editor guards ask the session's held registry instead of hand-listing editors, so a newly added editor can no longer be typed over by Ctrl+P/A/W/V, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+N or Ctrl+E (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry) — done 2026-10-20

**Goal.** `createTuiEditorSession` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`) already keeps a registry of which editors hold the prompt line: `heldEditorFlash` walks the six special holders plus `HOLDER_SUBJECTS`, and `anyEditorHeld` wraps it. Five key-entry guards still list `!session.held.<x>` flags by hand, though, and each list has fallen behind the editors added since it was written:
- `createPauseEditor`'s per-role Ctrl+P/A/W/V arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`) and `createPromptEditor`'s Ctrl+R arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-prompt.ts`) run on the transcript views. Neither checks `held.instances`, even though `createInstancesEditor`'s Ctrl+G opens on those same views. With the instances editor open, Ctrl+P therefore opens the pause editor on top of it, and Ctrl+R opens the role-prompt editor on top of it. The pause arm also skips `attach`, `brief`, `providerCaps`, `slots`, `backends`, `fallback`, `model` and `claudeReserve`. The prompt arm also skips `retire`, `attach`, `brief`, `providerCaps`, `slots`, `fallback`, `model` and `claudeReserve`.
- The answer editor's Ctrl+A arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-answer.ts`), the entry editor's new-entry Ctrl+N arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-entry.ts`) and the queued editor's Ctrl+E arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-queued.ts`) each check at most eight holders.

Every new editor plan has had to find and patch these lists. Reviewer rejections in the 24 hours to 13:00 UTC 2026-10-20 include "missed this sibling" findings of exactly this kind: a `held.slots` or `held.concurrency` left out of some guards but added to others.

**Approach.**
- **`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`**: widen `anyEditorHeld(except?: "pause")` to `anyEditorHeld(...except: ReadonlyArray<"pause" | "rolePromptFor" | "search">)`. It returns true when any holder `heldEditorFlash` checks is set and is not named in `except`. The holders are `search`, `pause`, `queued`, `answer`, `entry`, `rolePromptFor` and every `HOLDER_SUBJECTS` mode. Implement it as its own walk over those flags, so `heldEditorFlash`'s ordering and wording stay unchanged. The existing `anyEditorHeld()` / `anyEditorHeld("pause")` call sites keep their meaning. `quietTeam` and the `pauseEdit*` fields are sub-state, not holders, and stay out. Update its doc comment.
- **`tui-editor-pause.ts`**: replace the per-role arm's hand list with `!session.anyEditorHeld("rolePromptFor", "search")`. Role prompt and search stay excepted because the arm deliberately still lets Ctrl+P resume a paused role and Ctrl+A/Ctrl+V act while they are held, and its inner branches already flash `busyFlash("role prompt"/"search")` for the editor-opening cases. Leave those inner branches as they are.
- **`tui-editor-prompt.ts`**: replace the Ctrl+R arm's list with `!session.anyEditorHeld("rolePromptFor")`. A second Ctrl+R still has to reach the arm to exit role-prompt mode.
- **`tui-editor-answer.ts`, `tui-editor-entry.ts`** (the new-entry branch only, after the existing plan↔bug flip branch), **`tui-editor-queued.ts`**: replace each list with `!session.anyEditorHeld()`. In the entry and queued arms, the module-local `entryEditFor`/`queuedEditFor` checks are mirrored in `session.held.entry`/`session.held.queued`, so the registry covers them.
- A blocked key keeps today's behaviour at every site: the arm returns false and the key falls through. No new flash is added.
- Out of scope: `onArrow`'s history-recall list in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts`. It deliberately leaves out holders such as `rolePromptFor`, whose mode keeps its own recall pair, so it is not the same guard.

**Files touched.** `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts`, `tui-editor-pause.ts`, `tui-editor-prompt.ts`, `tui-editor-answer.ts`, `tui-editor-entry.ts`, `tui-editor-queued.ts`; tests in `test/tui-instances.test.ts` (the fixture `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` from `test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`, as in "Ctrl+G is mutually exclusive with the other prompt-line editors, flashing the way out").

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test: on clean's transcript, after Ctrl+G opens the instances editor, Ctrl+P does not open the pause editor (no `pause clean:` prompt in the frame) and Ctrl+R does not open the role-prompt editor. The frame still shows the instances editor's prompt, and Esc then exits it as before.
- The existing tests that cover the per-role pause/wake/abort keys, Ctrl+R role-prompt toggling, Ctrl+A answer, Ctrl+N new entry and Ctrl+E queued edit pass unchanged. That includes the role-prompt/search cases where Ctrl+P on a paused role still resumes it.
- After the change, `grep -n '!session.held\.' src/ui/tui/tui-editor-{pause,prompt,answer,entry,queued}.ts` finds no multi-flag guard chain.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A feature or bugfix primary whose eligible entries are all held by siblings stands down instead of running a model run that can only end in nothing-to-do (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** In the 24 hours to 13:11 UTC on 2026-10-20, the primary `feature` runner ended 52 runs with `no_change`. Their median length was 4.5 s, and together they cost $1.65 notional on the claude subscription window. A typical one: at 09:00:32 a `wake` ("main moved") was followed by `run_start` with no `claim` event and then `run_end` `no_change` 5.7 s later. In a multi-runner group, `pollRunnerReasons` (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts) skips an extra instance with no free entry ("no-free-entry"). The feature stand-down added 2026-10-12 skips the primary only when `eligible.length === 0`. When eligible entries exist but siblings hold every one, the claim block finds no `pick`, sets `runner.state.heldElsewhere`, and admits the primary unassigned. `buildHeldEntriesNote` (src/prompt/gate-notes.ts) then tells the run to "treat the backlog as having nothing to do for you". The run is paid for, but the only outcome it can have is no change. That is the waste the 10-12 stand-down was meant to remove, and the same holds for a bugfix primary whose open bugs are all held by siblings.

**Approach.** Only `pollRunnerReasons`, in the claim block's `else if (instanceIndex(runner.role) >= 2)` branch:
- Widen the condition to `!pick && (instanceIndex(runner.role) >= 2 || (heldTitles.length > 0 && !freshlyWoken(runner.state)))`. The branch body stays as it is: `noteSkip(root, runner, "no-free-entry")`, the `once.settle(runner.role, "no free entry")` call, and `continue`. `nextRunAt`/`backoffSeconds` are untouched, so the first poll after a sibling releases its entry or main moves starts the primary again.
- Keep `runner.state.heldElsewhere` as the line above sets it. The branch is reached only for reasons other than inbox/resume, but a later inbox or resume run reuses the stored list in its `<held-entries>` note.
- Without `heldTitles`, behavior does not change: a bugfix primary with no open bugs (an empty `claimGroup.eligible`) still runs in search mode, and so does any multi-runner role whose `eligibleEntries` is empty. An operator wake (`freshlyWoken`) still gets its run, the same exemption the stand-down above uses. A runner with a claim or outstanding work never reaches this branch.
- Update the claim block's comment ("the primary runs unassigned only while some eligible entry exists (all of them held by siblings)") to say the primary now stands down in that case too, unless an operator wake is fresh.

**Files.** `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts`, `test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts`, `docs/how-it-works.md` (the "Parallel work instances" bullet: an instance, the first included, also skips while every eligible entry is held by a sibling, and an operator wake still runs).

**Acceptance criteria.** In `test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts`:
- Rename "an unassigned primary is told the entries its siblings hold, and the prompt names them" to say the primary stands down. Keep its `heldElsewhere` and prompt assertions, and add these: `reasons.has(feature)` is false, `feature.state.skipReason` is `"no-free-entry"`, and `nextRunAt`/`backoffSeconds` are unchanged.
- A new test with the same three-feature setup, where the primary carries `wokenAt` later than `lastRunEndedAt`: the primary is admitted unassigned, with `heldElsewhere` set.
- A new bugfix case: with two bugfix runners, BUGS.md holding one open eligible bug, and `bugfix-2` holding its claim, the primary `bugfix` is not admitted and records `"no-free-entry"`. With BUGS.md holding no open bugs, the primary is still admitted (search mode).
- The existing tests "an extra instance with no free entry is skipped and keeps its schedule", "a once round settles an extra feature instance with no free entry" and the bugfix held-only tests pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### A per-run provider-failure warning names the provider/model it failed on, so a mixed-provider team can tell which backend is down from the feed alone (planned 2026-10-20 by the plan role; no dependency on any Planned entry; done 2026-10-20 by the feature role)

**Goal.** On 2026-10-20 the claude window fallback (`fallback_switched`, 06:11 UTC) moved every tier to `qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b`. That endpoint was unreachable, and from 06:11 to 07:20 UTC the feed carried 14 `run_end` "Connection error." failures and 26 warnings reading only `provider backend failure (connection error) — the transient retry does not cover this kind; the team-wide wait watches for a storm`. Claude, huggingface and qwenrunner seams were all in use that week, and the per-run warnings in src/runner/runner-pi.ts name none of them. The team-wide `rate_limit_hold` does carry `provider`, but it forms only on a storm. A single role's failure, or a retry line ("provider rate-limited the request (429 …) — retrying the agent run once"), leaves the operator guessing which backend misbehaved. `runWithTransientRetry` already knows the seam: `opts.config` is the config this agent run actually ran on (a fallback pair included; see its `seamHoldKey(opts.config)` comment). So naming it costs one string.

**Approach.**
- In `runWithTransientRetry` (src/runner/runner-pi.ts), compute once `const on = opts.config.model !== undefined ? \` on ${seamPairName(opts.config)}\` : "";`. With no model (pi's own saved default), `seamPairName` would print `?/?`, so the label is omitted rather than guessed.
- Insert `on` into each retry-branch warning right after its leading phrase and parenthetical, before the ` — ` separator. The results: `pi crashed on malformed JSON (<detail>)${on} — resuming the session once`, `provider rate-limited the request (429…)${on} — retrying the agent run once`, `provider severed the in-flight stream (terminated)${on} — …`, `provider request timed out after accepting the connection${on} — …`, `model server timed out an idle predict stream (e.g. machine sleep)${on} — …`.
- `warnBackendKindFloor(run)` takes the same label as a second parameter (`warnBackendKindFloor(run: PiRunResult, on: string)`), passed at both call sites. Its text becomes `provider backend failure (${backendKindPhrase(run.backendKind)})${on} — the transient retry does not cover this kind; …`. The retry runs on the same `opts` (`runPi({ ...opts, continueSession: true })`), so one label serves both attempts.
- Do not touch the `fallbackClone` warning (it names its model already), the 429/backend folds, or any event shape. These are `warning` messages only.
- Update the `warnBackendKindFloor` docblock to say the line names the seam's pair.

**Files touched.** src/runner/runner-pi.ts, test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- Existing assertions keep matching with no edit, because the label lands after the substrings they test. That covers test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts's `/provider backend failure \(connection error\)/` and `/rate-limited the request \(429, retry after 3s\)/`, test/runner-2.test.ts's pi-crash regex, and the `retrying the agent run once` substring checks in test/runner-4.test.ts and test/runner-transient-retry.test.ts. `defaultConfig()` sets no model, so those tests' warnings carry no label.
- New test in test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts, "the backend-kind floor warning names the seam's provider/model pair". A `cfg` with `agent = "pi"`, `provider = "omlx"`, `model = "qwen"` (the shape of "a 429 agent run folds its seam hold key …") and a first run of `errorLine("Connection error.")` produce exactly one warning that starts with `provider backend failure (connection error) on omlx/qwen — `.
- New test in the same file, "a retry warning names the seam's provider/model pair": the same cfg with a 429 first run (retry after 3s) yields `warns[0]` matching `/^provider rate-limited the request \(429, retry after 3s\) on omlx\/qwen — retrying the agent run once$/`.
- New assertion: "a backend-kind failure the retry does not cover warns once and earns no retry" (default config) also asserts `!warns[0]!.includes(" on ")`, so no `?/?` label appears.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.
