### `tumwater report --role` takes a comma-separated list of role ids, so one usage report or failure digest covers every role an operator is comparing (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — fast merge 14/14 edits the merge path, runner 9/14 status data and scheduling, the TUI Ctrl+Y entry src/ui/tui, and the wake entry src/operator plus the wake/reset-counters help lines and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row; none of them is src/report, src/failure/failure-data.ts or the report stanza of src/cli/help.ts, and this edits docs/cli.md's Audit row only; the blocked plain-terms parts reach src/report only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/report/report.ts src/report/report-fold.ts src/report/report-data.ts src/failure/failure-data.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/report.test.ts test/help.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `history --role` takes a comma list (`parseRoleListScope`, src/cli/cli-args.ts), and the pause/resume/wake work does the same for the operator commands. `report --role` still takes one id: `tumwater report --role clean,dedupe` fails with `unknown role: clean,dedupe`, so an operator comparing the maintenance roles' spend against their output runs one report per role and adds the numbers by hand. Accept the comma list on every report shape: the day report, `--since`, and `--failures` (day and `--since`).

**Approach.**
- `src/report/report.ts` `cmdReport`: replace `parseRoleScope(root, args)` with `parseRoleListScope(root, args)`. It already validates each piece, canonicalizes, deduplicates in first-seen order and fails `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR` on an empty list. Pass `roles ?? undefined` to the four collectors. Update the import and the `--role` comment.
- `src/report/report-fold.ts`:
  - Add an exported `scopeBases(role: string | readonly string[] | undefined): string[] | undefined`. It maps undefined and an empty array to undefined (the team report). Otherwise it maps each id through `baseRoleOf`, deduplicated in first-seen order, so `feature-2,feature` is one base.
  - Widen `roleSum(record, role)` to `roleSum(record, bases: string | readonly string[])`. It sums every key whose `baseRoleOf` is one of the bases. A single string behaves as today.
  - Widen `narrowToRole` the same way. It returns one entry per base with a nonzero `roleSum`, keyed by that base, and keeps the zero-means-absent rule.
  - Widen `scopedByRole(record, base)` to take `readonly string[] | undefined`.
  - Update the three doc comments: "one base role" becomes "the scoped base roles".
- `src/report/report-data.ts`:
  - `collectReport` and `collectReportSince` widen `role?: string` to `role?: string | readonly string[]`. Each computes `const bases = scopeBases(role)` once, and every `base === undefined` test becomes `bases === undefined`. The `roleSum`/`narrowToRole`/`scopedByRole` calls take `bases`.
  - The day branch's work/maintenance split no longer uses `commitTier(base)` on one base. `workCommits` sums `roleSum(fold.commitsByRole, b)` over the bases whose `commitTier(b)` is `"work"`, and `maintenanceCommits` sums those whose tier is `"maintenance"`. With one base this gives the same numbers as today.
  - The output's `role` field stays a string: `bases.join(",")`. The JSON shape does not change, a single-role report keeps the same `role` value, and the render's `role: <id>` header line prints `role: clean,dedupe`. Update the `role?: string` field comments on `ReportData` and `SinceReport` to say this.
  - The callers that pass one string keep compiling unchanged: `reportScope`'s `/api/report` path in src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts and `scope` in src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts. Do not edit them.
- `src/failure/failure-data.ts`:
  - `collectFailureReport`, `collectFailureReportSince` and the shared collector they call take `role?: string | readonly string[]` and compute `bases` through `scopeBases`.
  - `scopeToRole(events, base)` becomes `scopeToRole(events, bases: readonly string[])` and tests membership with `includes`.
  - The memo key uses `bases?.join(",") ?? ""`.
  - The output `role` is `bases.join(",")`, as in the usage report.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the report usage lines become `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. In the three descriptions, "--role <id> scopes … to one role's" becomes "--role <id>[,<id>...] scopes … to the listed roles'". Update the `help.test.ts` regexes that pin the old usage lines (`report --failures [--days N] [--since <duration>] [--role <id>] [--json]` and the `--failures --since` one) in the same change.
- `docs/cli.md`, Audit row: `tumwater report --role <id>` (scopes … to one role's …) becomes `tumwater report --role <id>[,<id>...]` (scopes … to the listed roles' …, summed; the by-role lines keep one entry per listed role).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New case in `test/report.test.ts`, "report --role takes a comma list and sums the listed roles". It uses `writeEvents` with `run_end` events (tokens/cost) for `clean`, `dedupe` and `feature`:
  - `report --role clean,dedupe --json` (day report) has `role` `"clean,dedupe"`. Its days' `runsByRole`/`costByRole` hold exactly the `clean` and `dedupe` keys, and their `tokensOut`/`costUsd` equal the two roles' sum, with `feature` absent.
  - The `--since 6h` form behaves the same: `totals.runs` is the two roles' run count, and the render prints `role: clean,dedupe`.
  - `report --role dedupe,clean,dedupe --json` dedupes, giving `role` `"dedupe,clean"`.
- New case: `report --failures --role clean,dedupe --json` scopes the digest to both roles: `role` is `"clean,dedupe"`, and no row names `feature`.
- New case: `report --role clean,ghost` exits nonzero with `unknown role: ghost`, and `report --role ,` exits nonzero with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.
- The existing single-role cases keep passing unchanged, among them "report --since narrows Revisions by role to the scoped base role" and "report --since folds failed ticks by role and narrows to the scoped base role".
- `tumwater help report` shows `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater wake --role` and `reset-counters --role` take a comma-separated list of role ids, the twin of `pause --role clean,dedupe` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it touches only `targetRoles` and its callers in src/operator/operator-commands.ts, help and docs) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `pause --role` and `resume --role` take a comma list (`pauseTargetRoles`, src/operator/operator-commands.ts), and so do `history`/`logs` (`parseRoleListScope`, src/cli/cli-args.ts). `wake --role` and `reset-counters --role` still take one id: an operator who held `clean,dedupe,organize` and resumed them must wake each one with its own command. `wake --role clean,dedupe` fails today with `unknown role: clean,dedupe`. The writers `requestWake(root, roles, inMs)` and `requestResetCounters(root, roles)` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts) already take a role array. Only the flag parsing is missing.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`:
  - Add `namedRoleList(root, args): string[] | null`. It returns null when `flagValue(args, "--role")` is null. Otherwise it splits the value on `,`, trims each piece and drops empty pieces. When none remain (bare `--role`, `--role ""`, `--role ,`), it calls `fail(ROLE_VALUE_ERROR)`. Each piece resolves through `namedRole(root, ["--role", piece])`, so built-ins skip the config read and an unknown id fails with the existing `unknown role: <id> (valid ids: …)` message. The result is deduplicated in first-seen order. Every piece resolves before the caller writes anything.
  - `pauseTargetRoles` keeps its instance-1 exception (`feature-1` kept verbatim). It is rewritten to share the split/empty/dedupe steps with `namedRoleList`: extract one small private splitter that both call, `rolePieces(args): string[] | null`. Behaviour of pause/resume is unchanged.
  - `targetRoles(root, args)` becomes `namedRoleList(root, args) ?? Object.keys(loadConfig(root).roles)`. This makes `cmdResetCounters` and `cmdWake` (both the immediate and the `--in` scheduled path) accept the list with no other change.
  - `wake --cancel` and `wake --list` keep one role: `cancelWakes`/`listWakes`/`renderWakeList` take `role?: string`, and widening them is not needed for this change. Before the `namedRole` call in each branch, a `--role` value containing `,` fails with `wake --cancel and --list take one --role id`. This replaces the misleading `unknown role: clean,dedupe`.
  - Update the doc comments of `targetRoles`, `cmdResetCounters` and `cmdWake` to name the comma list.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the usage lines become `tumwater reset-counters [--role <id>[,<id>...]]` and `tumwater wake [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--in <dur> | --cancel | --list [--json]]`. Keep the description column aligned, with the `pause` stanza as the model.
- `docs/cli.md`, "Control the roles" row: `tumwater reset-counters [--role <id>]` becomes `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. The `tumwater wake` clause gains `wake --role clean,dedupe` wakes each listed role, the same as one command per role.
- The TUI, the GUI endpoints (`/api/wake`, `/api/reset-counters`) and the intent writers do not change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New case in `test/operator-commands.test.ts`, "cmdWake and cmdResetCounters --role take a comma list":
  - Seed `clean` and `dedupe` with backoff and counters, and leave `organize` as is.
  - `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean, dedupe,clean"])` prints `wake requested for clean, dedupe`, clears both backoffs and leaves `organize`'s state unchanged. `wakeRequestPath`'s `roles` reads `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
  - `cmdResetCounters(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe"])` prints `counters reset for clean, dedupe`, zeroes both, and `resetRequestPath`'s `roles` reads `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
- New case: `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe", "--in", "45m"])` writes one scheduled-wake file whose `roles` is `["clean", "dedupe"]`.
- New case "wake and reset-counters: a comma list with an unknown id writes no marker":
  - `cmdWake(root, ["--role", "clean,ghost"])` fails with `unknown role: ghost`. Neither `wakeRequestPath` nor `clean`'s state changes.
  - `cmdResetCounters` behaves the same way.
  - `["--role", ","]` fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.
- New case: `cmdWake(root, ["--cancel", "--role", "clean,dedupe"])` and `["--list", "--role", "clean,dedupe"]` fail with `wake --cancel and --list take one --role id`.
- These cases keep passing unchanged:
  - in `test/cli-operators-team.test.ts`: "reset-counters --role targets one loop; unknown or missing role fails without side effects" and "wake --role targets one loop; …";
  - in `test/operator-commands.test.ts`: "cmdPause and cmdResume --role take a comma list" and "a comma list with an unknown id writes no marker".
- `tumwater help wake` shows `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The TUI History pane's `Ctrl+Y` cycles role summary → model summary → rows, the terminal twin of `tumwater history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the dashboard By-model entry edits src/gui and src/ui/gui, the pause/resume entry src/operator, the help lines and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row, fast-merge part 14/14 src/config, src/review and src/merge, and runner part 8/14 src/orchestrator, none of which is src/ui/tui; it shares docs/cli.md's "Watch run history" row with the dashboard By-model entry (a rebase: edit whichever wording is on main); the blocked plain-terms series renames identifiers in src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` tallies runs per model (`summarizeTickRowsByModel` in src/history/history-data.ts, rendered by `renderModelSummary` in src/history/history-render.ts). The TUI History pane's `Ctrl+Y`, though, only flips between the run rows and the per-role table (`renderSummary`). So an operator watching a mixed-provider team in the terminal cannot see what each model merged or cost. This plan makes `Ctrl+Y` a three-step cycle: rows → per-role summary → per-model summary → rows. The model table is folded over the same rows the pane's window, role, result and search already selected. Out of scope: the dashboard (its own Planned entry), and any new key.

**Approach.**
- `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`:
  - Session state: `let historySummary = false;` becomes `let historySummary: HistorySummaryGroup | null = null;`. Here `type HistorySummaryGroup = (typeof HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS)[number]`, imported from src/history/history-data.ts (`["role", "model"]`). Export the type from there if it is not already exported. `null` means the row list. Update the comment above it.
  - `historyPaneCache`'s `summary: boolean` parameter becomes `summary: HistorySummaryGroup | null`. The body becomes: `"role"` with rows present → `renderSummary(summarizeTickRows(filtered))`; `"model"` with rows present → `renderModelSummary(summarizeTickRowsByModel(filtered))`; otherwise `historyPaneText(filtered)`. Keep the non-empty guard and its comment. Import both new helpers alongside the existing ones.
  - The `Ctrl+Y` arm: replace `historySummary = !historySummary` with the cycle `null → "role" → "model" → null`. Write it inline as `historySummary = historySummary === null ? "role" : historySummary === "role" ? "model" : null;`. Keep the `promptLineFree(ctx.es)` guard, `recompute()` and `requestRender()`. Update the comment to name the three steps.
  - `state()` returns `historySummary` unchanged by name, now with the new type.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`: in the state interface, `historySummary: boolean` becomes `historySummary: "role" | "model" | null`, or the imported `HistorySummaryGroup | null`. Update the doc comment to name the cycle. `src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts` and `src/ui/tui/tui.tsx` pass the value through unchanged and need no edit beyond what the compiler asks.
- `src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts`: the history view kind's `summary?: boolean` becomes `summary?: "role" | "model" | null`. The hint token `["Ctrl+Y", view.summary ? "rows" : "summary"]` names the next step: `!view.summary` → `"summary"`, `"role"` → `"by model"`, `"model"` → `"rows"`.
- `docs/cli.md`:
  - TUI-keys table, `Ctrl+Y` row: "on History, toggle the per-role Summary table" becomes "on History, cycle the per-role Summary table, the per-model table (`history --summary --by model`), and the run rows".
  - "Watch run history" row: the clause "the TUI's History pane shows the same per-role summary with `Ctrl+Y`" also names the per-model table, as the second `Ctrl+Y` press.
  - `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` compares only the set of Ctrl letters, so it needs no change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/tui-keys.test.ts`:
  - The existing case "Ctrl+Y toggles the History pane between the run rows and the per-role Summary table" is renamed to say "cycles", and its assertions are updated: `historySummary` is `null` on entry and `"role"` after one `Ctrl+Y`, with the same per-role table assertions. The fixture gains `run_start` events with `model: "m-a"` for feature #1 and `model: "m-b"` for qa #1. A second `Ctrl+Y` gives `"model"`, and the pane's first line matches `/model/`, `/runs/` and `/cost/`. The pane has lines starting `m-a` and `m-b` and a `total` line, and no `#1`. A third `Ctrl+Y` gives `null` and restores `feature #1`.
  - A `run_end` with no `run_start` shows as `(unknown)` in the model table.
  - The budget-mode-inert and Activity-vs-History `Ctrl+Y` cases keep passing, with their `true`/`false` expectations updated to `"role"`/`null`.
- `test/tui-frame.test.ts`: the hint assertions cover all three states: `summary: null` → `Ctrl+Y summary`, `"role"` → `Ctrl+Y by model`, `"model"` → `Ctrl+Y rows`.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### The dashboard History view gains a "By model" summary mode, the twin of `tumwater history --summary --by model` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — none of them names src/gui, src/ui/gui, src/history or the history row of docs/cli.md; the blocked plain-terms parts that rename symbols in src/history mean a rebase at most; touches src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts docs/cli.md test/gui-endpoints.test.ts test/gui-client-history.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater history --summary --by model` (`summarizeTickRowsByModel`, src/history/history-data.ts) tallies runs per model, but its plan scoped the dashboard out. So the History view's Summary toggle can only group by role, and an operator watching a mixed-provider team in the browser cannot see what each model merged or cost. This plan adds a third mode, "By model", next to Table and Summary. It shows one row per model with the same columns, `(unknown)` for the null bucket, then the total. Out of scope: the TUI History pane (`Ctrl+Y` keeps the per-role table).

**Approach.**
- `src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts`, `handleHistory`: in both arms (the `sinceMs` window and the `n` count), when `summary` is present, add an additive `modelSummary: summarizeTickRowsByModel(<the served rows>)` beside `summary`. Use the same rows that `summary` folds: `matched` in the window arm, the grep-filtered `rows` in the count arm. Import `summarizeTickRowsByModel` from src/history/history-data.ts. Without `summary` the response keeps today's shape, with no `modelSummary` key. Extend the doc comment's `summary` sentence to say that it also adds `modelSummary`, `{ models, total }`, the `history --summary --by model` tally of the same rows. Do not add a new query parameter: one fetch carries both, so switching modes never refetches, as Summary already doesn't.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-history.ts`:
  - State: add `let histModelSummary = null;` beside `histSummary`. The mode restore becomes `const m = recall("hist-mode"); let histMode = m === "summary" || m === "models" ? m : "table";`.
  - `HIST_MODES` becomes `[["table", "Table"], ["summary", "Summary"], ["models", "By model"]]`. The toolbar's `histsum` segment and its click handler (`store("hist-mode", histMode)`) need no other change.
  - `fetchHistory`: beside the `histSummary = …` line, set `histModelSummary = d && d.modelSummary && Array.isArray(d.modelSummary.models) ? d.modelSummary : null;`. A server too old to send it leaves the value null.
  - Inside the `// history-summary:start` … `:end` block, factor the table out of `histSummaryHtml` into `summaryTableHtml(header, entries)`. Here `entries` is `[{ label, row, total }]`. The function keeps the existing cells, the `hist-total` class on the total row, and the `<th>` header text, with the first `<th>` replaced by `header`. `histSummaryHtml(summary)` maps roles to `{ label: roleLabel(r.role), row: r }` and appends `{ label: "total", row: summary.total, total: true }`, so its HTML stays the same for the same input. Add `histModelSummaryHtml(summary)`, which maps `summary.models` to `{ label: r.model === null ? "(unknown)" : r.model, row: r }`, then the total, under the header `Model`. Labels go through `esc`, as today.
  - `renderHistory`: hide `histfilter` when `histMode !== "table"`. Pick the body as follows: in `"summary"` mode with `histSummary` and rows present, `histSummaryHtml`; in `"models"` mode with `histModelSummary` and rows present, `histModelSummaryHtml`; otherwise the table. The fallback is the same one an empty or too-old response gets today. Update the comment there to name both modes.
- `docs/cli.md`, the "Watch run history" row: after "the TUI's History pane shows the same per-role summary with `Ctrl+Y`", add "; the dashboard's History view has Summary and By model modes for the two groupings".

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/gui-endpoints.test.ts`, new case "handleHistory ?summary also folds the served rows per model". Seed `run_start` events carrying `model` (two models) with their `run_end`s, plus one `run_end` with no start. Assert that `modelSummary` deep-equals `summarizeTickRowsByModel(rows)` of the served rows, in both the `?n=50&summary=1` and the `?sinceMs=3600000&summary=1` arm. Assert that the null bucket is last with `model: null`, and that `?n=50` without the flag has no `modelSummary` key. The existing "handleHistory ?summary folds the served rows into an additive per-role summary" case passes unchanged.
- `test/gui-client-history.test.ts`:
  - The `HIST_MODES` regex assertion is updated to the three-mode literal.
  - A new case loads the `history-summary` block via `clientScope` (as the existing `histSummaryHtml` case does). It asserts that `histModelSummaryHtml` renders a `Model` header, one row per model, `(unknown)` for `model: null`, an escaped `<` in a model id, and a `hist-total` row.
  - The existing `histSummaryHtml` case passes unchanged.
  - The "fetchHistory rides the server summary…" pattern is extended (or copied) with `recall("hist-mode")` returning `"models"` and a response carrying `modelSummary`. It asserts that `histMode` restores as `"models"` and that the fetched `modelSummary` is kept.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 8/14: Convert the orchestrator and its tests (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 7/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/orchestrator/ + test/orchestrator*.test.ts + test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The orchestrator and its unit and e2e tests use `RoleRunner`, `RunnerState` and runner/role wording.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).

The poll loop stays the poll loop.
- Tests: every test/orchestrator*.test.ts and test/orchestrator*.e2e.test.ts (`loadLoopState` alone is about 170 lines here), plus test/fixtures/orchestrator-fixtures.ts. Rename test locals per the series rules; test/orchestrator-2.e2e.test.ts's `loopOrder` → `roleOrder`.
- Locals such as `dryTicks` and `dryFailedAt` carry role-id and tick words, which belong to later series; leave them.

- `grep -rnwiE 'loops?'` over the same files lists only the poll loop and other kept senses.

### `tumwater pause --role` and `resume --role` take a comma-separated list of role ids, so one command holds or releases every role an operator is steering (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it touches only `cmdPause`/`cmdResume` in src/operator/operator-commands.ts, the pause/resume help lines and docs/cli.md's "Control the roles" row) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Holding a group of roles today takes one `pause --role` per role (for example, holding `clean`, `dedupe` and `organize` while a large feature merges), and releasing them takes one `resume --role` each. `history --role` already takes a comma list (`parseRoleListScope`, src/cli/cli-args.ts). Give `pause --role` and `resume --role` the same spelling: `tumwater pause --role clean,dedupe,organize [--for 2h]` and `tumwater resume --role clean,dedupe,organize`. Each listed role gets exactly the write and the confirmation line it gets today, and every id is validated before any marker is written.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts`:
  - Replace `pauseTargetRole(root, args): string | null` with `pauseTargetRoles(root, args): string[] | null`. It returns null when `flagValue(args, "--role")` is null, so the team branches stay as they are. Otherwise:
    - Split the value on `,`, trim each piece and drop empty pieces. When none remain (`--role ""` or `--role ,`), `fail(ROLE_VALUE_ERROR)`.
    - Resolve each piece the way `pauseTargetRole` resolves the whole value today: an instance-1 key (`[...INSTANCE_ROLES].some((base) => piece === \`${base}-1\`)`) is kept verbatim; any other piece goes through `namedRole(root, ["--role", piece])`, so an unknown id fails with the existing `unknown role: <id>` message. Every piece resolves before anything is written, so a bad id anywhere in the list writes no marker.
    - Deduplicate, keeping first-seen order.
  - `cmdPause`: replace the `const role = pauseTargetRole(...)` / `if (role)` block with `const roles = pauseTargetRoles(root, args)` / `if (roles)`. The `--reason` refusal stays first and unchanged. Then, for each role in order, `say(rolePauseMessage(root, role, pauseRole(root, role, untilMs), timed, now))`, so a `--for` gives each listed role the same deadline and each prints its own line.
  - `cmdResume`: same shape. Loop `say(roleResumeMessage(root, role, resumeRole(root, role)))` over the list.
  - The doc comment of each command names the comma list.
  - `pauseRole`/`resumeRole` (src/team/team-state.ts), `rolePauseMessage`/`roleResumeMessage` (src/operator/operator-intent.ts), the TUI, the GUI and `wake`/`abort`/`reset-counters` are unchanged.
- `src/cli/help.ts`:
  - The usage lines read `tumwater pause [--role <id>[,<id>...]] [--for <dur>] [--reason <text>]` and `tumwater resume [--role <id>[,<id>...]]`.
  - The pause prose adds `--role takes a comma list, pausing each listed role`.
  - Re-wrap so the description column stays aligned (the `history` stanza is the model).
- `docs/cli.md`: in the "Control the roles" row, the `tumwater resume [--role <id>]` clause becomes `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`. Add one parenthetical: `--role clean,dedupe` pauses or resumes each listed role, the same as one command per role.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/operator-commands.test.ts`, new case "cmdPause and cmdResume --role take a comma list":
  - `cmdPause(root, ["--role", "clean, dedupe,clean"])` leaves `pausedRolesPath` roles `["clean", "dedupe"]`. Stdout holds a `role clean paused` line and a `role dedupe paused` line, and no second `clean` line.
  - A re-run with `["--role", "clean,organize"]` prints `role clean is already paused` and `role organize paused`.
  - `cmdResume(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe"])` prints both `resumed` lines and leaves roles `["organize"]`.
  - `["--role", "feature-1,clean"]` pauses both, keeping the instance-1 key verbatim.
- New case "a comma list with an unknown id writes no marker": `cmdPause(root, ["--role", "clean,ghost"])` fails with `unknown role: ghost`, and `pausedRolesPath` does not exist afterwards. `["--role", ","]` fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`'s text.
- New case: `cmdPause(root, ["--role", "clean,dedupe", "--for", "1h"], NOON)` writes the same deadline for both roles, read back the way the existing "cmdPause --role --for writes the role marker…" case reads one.
- The existing per-role cases ("cmdPause --role pauses one role…", "cmdPause --role --reason fails fast…", "per-role pause and resume reject unknown role ids…") pass unchanged.
- `tumwater help pause` shows the `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]` usage. `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater revert <sha> --dry-run` previews the revert: the commit it would undo, the paths the inverse touches, and whether it applies cleanly on main, without writing anything (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — it touches only src/operator/revert.ts, `cmdRevert`, the revert help line and docs/cli.md's revert clause) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `tumwater revert <sha>` acts at once. It commits the inverse on main, and the only way to learn whether a revert conflicts is to try it. An operator weighing a revert of a change merged a few commits back has no way to see first what it would undo, or whether later commits have built on it. `--dry-run` answers both from git's object store. It runs the same refusals as the real revert, then a three-way merge with `git merge-tree`. It never touches the index, the worktree or a ref, and it takes no lock. This is the same preview idea that `reclaim --dry-run` and `retire --dry-run` already offer.

**Approach.**
- `src/operator/revert.ts`:
  - Factor the read-only refusals of `revertMergedCommit` into a private `resolveRevertTarget(root, ref): Promise<{ ok: true; full: string; primary: string } | { ok: false; error: string }>`. These are the base-branch check, `rev-parse --verify ref^{commit}` and `isMergedInto`. `revertMergedCommit` calls it inside its lock, keeping its existing error strings and order. The clean-tree check stays in `revertMergedCommit`.
  - Export `previewRevert(root, ref): Promise<RevertPreview | { ok: false; error: string }>`. `RevertPreview` is `{ ok: true; sha: string; subject: string; paths: string[]; head: string; applies: boolean; dirty: boolean }`. The function never throws; a thrown git failure comes back as `{ ok: false, error: "the revert preview did not complete (git failed); nothing was written" }`. Its steps:
    - Call `resolveRevertTarget`. It takes no lock, because it writes nothing.
    - Count parents with `git rev-list --parents -n 1 <full>`. A commit with no parent, or with more than one, returns `{ ok: false, error: "<short> has <n> parents; revert previews a single-parent commit only" }`.
    - `subject` comes from `git log -1 --format=%s <full>`.
    - `paths` comes from `git diff --name-only --no-renames <full>^ <full>`, the same path rule `revertCommitIn` commits with.
    - `head` is `headOf(root, "HEAD")`.
    - `applies` comes from `runGit(root, ["merge-tree", "--write-tree", "--merge-base=" + full, "HEAD", full + "^"])`. This is the same three-way merge `git revert` performs: base = the commit, ours = HEAD, theirs = its parent. Exit 0 → `true`. A `GitError` with `code === 1` → `false` (conflict). Any other `GitError` returns `{ ok: false, error: "could not preview the revert: <message>" }`. That covers git older than 2.40, which lacks `--merge-base`.
    - `dirty` is `true` when `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` is non-empty. That is the same condition on which `revertMergedCommit` refuses.
- `src/operator/operator-commands.ts` (`cmdRevert`):
  - Accept exactly `[<sha>]` or `[<sha>, "--dry-run"]` or `["--dry-run", <sha>]`. Any other flag-shaped token still fails with the existing `revert takes no flags (got …)` message, reworded to `revert takes only --dry-run (got …)`. The arity message is unchanged.
  - With `--dry-run`, call `previewRevert` and `fail(error)` on `ok: false`. Otherwise print:
    - `would revert <short sha> <subject>`
    - each path indented two spaces
    - then one verdict line:
      - `applies cleanly on <primary> (HEAD <short head>); nothing was written` when `applies && !dirty`, exiting 0
      - `would conflict on <primary> (HEAD <short head>); nothing was written` when `!applies`
      - `the checkout has staged or unstaged changes, so tumwater revert would refuse until they are committed or stashed; nothing was written` when `dirty`
    - The conflict and dirty outcomes exit 1 (`process.exitCode = 1` after printing), so a script can gate the real revert on the dry run. When both hold, print both verdict lines.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: change the usage line to `tumwater revert <sha> [--dry-run]` and add one sentence: `--dry-run names the commit and the paths its inverse touches and says whether it applies cleanly on main, writing nothing (exit 1 when the revert would conflict or refuse)`. Completion derives the flag from this line.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the "Steer the project" row's `tumwater revert <sha>` clause, add the `--dry-run` sentence.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/operator-revert.test.ts`, new cases calling `previewRevert`:
  - On a non-tip commit whose paths no later commit touched, it returns `applies: true, dirty: false`, the commit's subject, and its paths. HEAD, `git status --porcelain` and `git stash list` are unchanged afterwards.
  - On the "a later commit edited the same region" fixture, it returns `applies: false`, and HEAD and the tree are unchanged.
  - With an unstaged edit to a tracked file, it returns `dirty: true`, and the edit is still in the worktree byte for byte.
  - An unknown ref returns `no such commit: <ref>`. The repo's root commit returns the `has 0 parents` error.
- The existing `revertMergedCommit` cases in test/operator-revert.test.ts pass unchanged.
- `test/cli-operators.test.ts`, new case "revert --dry-run previews without writing":
  - On a clean revert it exits 0. Stdout starts `would revert <short>`, lists the path, and contains `applies cleanly`.
  - On a conflicting one it exits 1 with `would conflict`.
  - In both, HEAD and `git status --porcelain` are as before.
- The existing "revert rejects a flag-shaped token…" case is updated to the new `revert takes only --dry-run (got --json)` wording and still asserts that no commit is written.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history --summary --by model` tallies runs per model instead of per role, so an operator mixing providers can compare what each model merged (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — none of them names src/history, src/cli, src/cli.ts or docs/cli.md; the blocked plain-terms parts run 6/20 and 7/20 rename symbols in src/history and the history tests, a rebase; touches src/history/history-data.ts src/history/history-render.ts src/history/history.ts src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts src/cli/cli-command-args.ts src/cli.ts src/cli/help.ts docs/cli.md test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts test/history-data.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** A team can mix models: a pi default tier, a claude strong tier, an OpenCode free tier, plus a fallback (README "Mixing providers"). Every history row already carries the model its run started on (`TickRow.model`, read from `run_start` by `tickStartModel` in src/history/history-data.ts). The report's `Runs by model` line counts starts only. Nothing tallies outcomes per model: `history --summary` groups by role (`summarizeTickRows`), and `history --grep <model>` filters rows but still groups by role. So an operator cannot answer "how many runs on the free tier merged, and what did they cost?" in one command. This plan adds `--by model` to `history --summary`. The outcome columns stay the same, and each line is one model instead of one role. Out of scope: the TUI History pane, the dashboard's History view and `/api/history` keep the per-role summary.

**Approach.**
- `src/history/history-data.ts`:
  - Move the body of `summarizeTickRows` into a private `tallyRows(rows: TickRow[], keyOf: (row: TickRow) => string): { groups: HistorySummaryRow[]; total: HistorySummaryRow }`. `keyOf` gives each row's group key. The key is stored in the group row's `role` field. `summarizeTickRows` becomes `tallyRows(rows, (r) => r.role)`, renamed to `{ roles, total }`. Its output, order and JSON stay as they are.
  - Export `HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS = ["role", "model"] as const` and `type HistorySummaryGroup`.
  - Export `interface HistoryModelSummaryRow`: `Omit<HistorySummaryRow, "role"> & { model: string | null }`. `null` is the bucket of rows whose `model` is null; their start was outside the scanned window or carried no model.
  - Export `summarizeTickRowsByModel(rows: TickRow[]): { models: HistoryModelSummaryRow[]; total: HistorySummaryRow }`. It calls `tallyRows` with a key that maps a null model to a private sentinel no selector can equal, such as `"\u0000"`. It then maps each group to `{ model, ...counts }`, with the sentinel becoming `null`. Order is `compareCodeUnits` over the model strings, with the null bucket last. `total` is the same `{ role: "total", … }` object `summarizeTickRows` builds, so `total` is identical under both groupings.
- `src/history/history-render.ts`:
  - Move the table body of `renderSummary` into a private `renderSummaryTable(header: string, lines: { label: string; row: HistorySummaryRow | HistoryModelSummaryRow }[])`. `renderSummary` calls it with header `"role"`, each role's `roleLabel(r.role)` and the `total` line. Its output stays byte-for-byte the same; the existing test "history --summary tallies each loop's outcomes over the rows the table would print" pins this.
  - Export `renderModelSummary(summary: { models: HistoryModelSummaryRow[]; total: HistorySummaryRow })`. It uses header `"model"`, with label `model ?? "(unknown)"` and `"total"` for the total line.
- `src/history/history.ts` (`cmdHistory`):
  - Export `HISTORY_BY_VALUE_ERROR = "history --by needs role or model"`.
  - After the `--result` block, read `flagValue(rest, "--by")`. If it is missing or empty, fail with `HISTORY_BY_VALUE_ERROR`. A value other than `role`/`model` fails with `history --by must be one of role, model${gotSuffix(v)}${typoSuffix(v, [...HISTORY_SUMMARY_GROUPS])}`. If `--by` is present without `--summary`, fail with `history --by needs --summary (it picks how the summary groups runs)`.
  - With `--by model`, the summary branch calls `summarizeTickRowsByModel` and prints `renderModelSummary`. With `--json`, it prints the `{ models, total }` payload.
  - `--by role` is the default and behaves exactly as `--summary` does today.
  - The empty-rows paths stay as they are: `{"rows":[]}` under `--json`, plus the existing prose.
- `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`: add `byFlagSpec(missingValue: string): FlagSpec` beside `resultFlagSpec`, as `{ names: ["--by"], value: true, valueName: "<role|model>", missingValue }`.
- `src/cli.ts`: in the `history` case, import `HISTORY_BY_VALUE_ERROR` with the other two errors. Add `byFlagSpec(HISTORY_BY_VALUE_ERROR)` to the `rejectUnknownArgs("history", …)` list.
- `src/cli/cli-command-args.ts`: add `"--by"` to `HISTORY_LISTING_VALUED_FLAGS`, so that `history --summary --by model` stays the listing form and is not read as the `history <role> <n>` trail form.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: add `[--by role|model]` after `[--summary]` in the history usage line. Add one sentence after the `--summary` sentence: `--by model groups the summary by the model each run started on instead of by role; with --json, { models, total }`. The completion script derives flag names from this help text (`completionSpec` in src/cli/completion.ts), so `--by` completes with no completion.ts change.
- `docs/cli.md`: in the "Watch run history" row, add `[--by role|model]` to the synopsis, plus a clause saying that `--summary --by model` prints one line per model with the same columns (`(unknown)` for runs whose start the log no longer holds).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `test/history-data.test.ts`, new case:
  - Over hand-built rows (two on model `a/m1`, one changed and one no_change; one on `b/m2`, error; one with `model: null`), `summarizeTickRowsByModel` returns `models` in the order `a/m1`, `b/m2`, `null`, with `a/m1` = `{ runs: 2, changes: 1, none: 1, … }`.
  - Its `total` deep-equals `summarizeTickRows(sameRows).total`.
- `test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts`, new case "history --summary --by model tallies runs per model". Seed `run_start` events carrying `model` (two models), their `run_end`s, and one `run_end` with no start.
  - Stdout's header starts `model `, it has one line per model plus a `(unknown)` line and a `total` line, and the counts are as seeded.
  - `--json` parses to `{ models, total }` with `models[2].model === null`.
  - `--summary --by role` prints exactly what `--summary` prints.
  - `--by model --role feature` narrows to feature's runs.
  - `--by model` without `--summary` exits non-zero, naming `--summary`.
  - `--by modle` exits non-zero, naming `role, model`.
  - A trailing `--by` exits non-zero with `history --by needs role or model`.
- The existing "history --summary tallies each loop's outcomes over the rows the table would print" and "history --summary keeps the empty-state output on an empty log" pass unchanged, and so do the `summarizeTickRows` cases in test/cli-run.test.ts.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Backend/model split, part 2/5: A fallback step takes `backend` beside `model` (planned 2026-10-19 by user, split 2026-10-19 by the plan role; requires part 1/5 landed; touches src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/config-fallbacks.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/config/config-views.ts test/config-views.test.ts test/config-validation.test.ts test/config-live.test.ts test/config-write.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** A fallback step can cross backends by saying so — `{ "backend": "pi", "model": "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b" }` — instead of by the shape of its model id. Series goal and siblings: part 1/5.

**Approach.**
- `FallbackStep`'s object form becomes `{ backend?, model, thinking?, maxDailyCostUsd? }`; `FALLBACK_STEP_KEYS` gains `"backend"` (src/config/config-schema.ts). `checkFallbackStep` (src/config/config-validation.ts) checks `backend` against `AGENT_IDS` and applies part 1/5's explicit-claude and explicit-pi id checks to the step's `model`.
- src/config/config-fallbacks.ts: where a step's selector is parsed into a pair, an explicit step `backend` decides the pair's backend through `routeModel`'s `explicitBackend` (claude/opencode take the id verbatim); a step without one keeps `seamKeyedFallbackProvider`'s rule exactly as today. The pair's provider field keeps its current seam-keyed meaning (a non-pi pair carries its backend name), so gate-polls' `tickOnPair` handback and `fallbackDisplayPair` (src/config/config-views.ts) need no new case — add one test proving the display label of a `{ backend: "claude", model: "claude-sonnet-5-5" }` step equals today's `claude/claude-sonnet-5-5` step's.
- A whole-config write (config-write's object path) round-trips a `{ backend, model, maxDailyCostUsd }` step unchanged.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `{ "backend": "pi", "model": "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b" }` and the string `"qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b"` resolve to the same fallback pair under a claude team; `{ "backend": "claude", "model": "claude-sonnet-5-5" }` resolves to the same pair (and display label, and `maxDailyCostUsd` spend key) as `"claude/claude-sonnet-5-5"`.
- A step's unknown `backend`, a `/` id under a claude step and a provider-less id under a pi step fail validation naming `fallback.<tier>[i].backend`/`.model`.
- Every existing fallback test passes unmodified; `npm test` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 7/14: Rename the dashboard's role card and drawer code (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires parts 6a/14, 6b/14 and 6c/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/ui/gui/ + src/gui/ + test/gui*.test.ts + test/cli-gui.test.ts + test/helpers/gui-client-scope.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The dashboard's browser code and server glue name the Roles card, drawer and rank by role, including `GUI_CLIENT_ROLES_JS` and the DOM ids and CSS classes the card uses.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message. Dashboard hashes were renamed by Plain terms scripting, and the legacy `#loop/<id>` route must keep working.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). ### Fast merge, part 6/14: `check.mergeCommand` runs a cheaper check inside the merge lock and moves the full check after the merge (planned 2026-10-19 by user; requires parts 3/14, 4c/14 and 5/14 landed; design in plans/fast-merge.md "Lever 2: merge on the gate, full check after the merge"; touches src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/build/build-check-detect.ts src/build/build-check-scoped.ts src/build/build-check-events.ts src/merge/merge-to-main.ts src/merge/merge-batch.ts src/merge/merge-stack.ts src/baseline/main-red.ts src/review/review-precheck.ts tumwater.json docs/config.md docs/how-it-works.md DEVELOPMENT.md test/affected-tests.ts and their tests) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Every code merge runs the full `npm test` inside the merge lock: `verifyMerge`'s no-op-rebase and inherited-green skips are both off while `check.gateCommand` is set (src/merge/merge-to-main.ts ~266-349). That is 96 s at p50 per merge on the serial slot. A first red there sends the change back through the whole pipeline. With parts 3–5 catching and reverting a break after the merge, the lock only needs what must never reach main: lint, compile and the change's affected tests. Those stay before every merge (decided 2026-10-19 by you).

**Approach.**
- Config: `check.mergeCommand?: string`.
  - Add it to `CheckConfig` and `CHECK_KEYS` (src/config/config-schema.ts).
  - Validate it like `gateCommand` (src/config/config-validation.ts ~315-323); blank means off.
  - Add an accessor `mergeCommandOf` beside `gateCommandOf` (src/build/build-check-detect.ts).
  - Update the valid-keys string in test/config-validation-check.test.ts.
- With `mergeCommand` set:
  - `verifyMerge` and the batch path (src/merge/merge-batch.ts, src/merge/merge-stack.ts) run it instead of the full check. Swap the command per scope in src/build/build-check-scoped.ts (~74).
  - The in-lock run is skipped when the rebased head is the head the gate verified (`rebasedHead === verifiedHead`).
  - Its green never calls `noteGreenBaseline`: main's verdicts come from the watch.
  - Its `build_check` events carry `full: false`. Code that reads `isFullCheckScope`/`MERGE_SCOPES` (src/build/build-check-events.ts) as "this was the full check" treats them as not full: attribution, reports, doctor's merge-check median.
  - `mainRedGate` and `bugfixMainRedNote` (src/baseline/main-red.ts) read the watch's newest verdict for main's tip or its nearest checked ancestor and never start a full check themselves. No verdict yet reads as green.
  - The gate's re-attribution (src/review/review-precheck.ts ~135) uses the watch's verdict for the tip when it has one, and attributes as today when it has none.
- Unset, nothing changes.
- tumwater.json: `"check": { …, "mergeCommand": "npm run test:gate" }`.
- Docs that promise a full check per merge or "never a red main" now say what happens instead: docs/config.md (the `check` row), docs/how-it-works.md (~65-69), DEVELOPMENT.md (~37-42), the comment in test/affected-tests.ts (~7-8), and the comments in src/merge/merge-batch.ts (~159, ~296).

**Files touched.**
- Source: src/config/config-schema.ts, src/config/config-validation.ts, src/build/build-check-detect.ts, src/build/build-check-scoped.ts, src/build/build-check-events.ts, src/merge/merge-to-main.ts, src/merge/merge-batch.ts, src/merge/merge-stack.ts, src/baseline/main-red.ts, src/review/review-precheck.ts.
- Config and docs: tumwater.json, docs/config.md, docs/how-it-works.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, test/affected-tests.ts (comment only).
- Tests: test/config-validation-check.test.ts, test/build-check-detect.test.ts, test/build-check.test.ts, test/merge-to-main.test.ts, test/main-red.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With `mergeCommand` set to a passing fake command and a full check that would fail, a change merges. The watch then reports the tip red and part 4b/14 reverts the change.
- When the rebased head equals the verified head, no in-lock `build_check` runs.

**Implementation note (2026-10-19).** tumwater.json was not edited: that file is off limits to the feature role, so enabling `"mergeCommand": "npm run test:gate"` there is left to the operator. The watch-verdict read is `watchedBaseline` (src/baseline/main-baseline.ts), used by `mainRedGate` and `bugfixMainRedNote` only. `mainTipVerdict` (which serves the gate's re-attribution and the merge attribution) does not read the watch: it goes through `checkMainBaseline`, whose per-SHA cache no merge seeds with a `mergeCommand` set, so it runs the check there. `isFullCheckScope` now takes the event's `full` field. ### `tumwater status`, the TUI header and the dashboard's team panel show the workspace pool once it is full (`workspaces 8/8`, plus `, 2 waiting` when runs queue for a slot) (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; touches nothing the other eligible entries name except the in-flight check-permit entry above, which edits the same seven observer files — src/team/orchestrator-info.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/badges.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts and their tests. This entry adds a sibling field and badge right after that entry's `checkPermits`/`checksBadge`, so whichever lands second rebases over the lines next to it. When that entry has landed, put each addition after its `checkPermits` counterpart; until then, put it after the `permits` counterpart. The blocked plain-terms parts reach src/ui/badges.ts and src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts only in far-behind parts; touches src/git/worktree-pool.ts + src/team/orchestrator-info.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts + src/status/status-data.ts + src/ui/badges.ts + src/ui/status-payload.ts + src/ui/status-render.ts + src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts + docs/how-it-works.md + test/worktree-pool.test.ts + test/orchestrator-info.test.ts + test/badges.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** Runs and approvals share `worktreeSlots` pooled workspaces (src/git/worktree-pool.ts). A run that finds every slot leased waits on the in-process `waiters` set. The wait is visible only afterwards: as a `slot_wait` event once it passes `SLOT_WAIT_EVENT_MS`, in the doctor's contention row, or in the report's workspace wait median. While the pool is saturated, an operator cannot see that all eight workspaces are leased and two runs are queued, which is the moment raising `worktreeSlots` would help. This plan publishes the pool's live state through the orchestrator info file, the same way `permits` is published, and shows it only while the pool is full or something waits. A team with spare workspaces keeps its header unchanged.

**Approach.**
- `src/git/worktree-pool.ts`: export `slotPoolSnapshot(root: string): { leased: number; limit: number; waiting: number }`.
  - `leased` counts `readSlotsState(root).slots` whose `lease` is non-null and whose `lease.pid === process.pid`. A lease from another pid is dead (see the `SlotLease` doc in src/git/slots-state.ts).
  - `limit` is `liveCount(root)`.
  - `waiting` is `waiters.get(rootKey(root))?.size ?? 0`.
  - Doc it as the pool's live state for observers. `wakeWaiters` empties the set before woken waiters re-register, so `waiting` can read low for one turn. Observers poll, so the next poll corrects it.
- `src/team/orchestrator-info.ts`: add `export interface SlotPoolSnapshot { leased: number; limit: number; waiting: number }` beside `PermitSnapshot`.
  - Add `slotPool?: SlotPoolSnapshot` to `OrchestratorInfo`, with a doc in the style of `permits` ("written by the orchestrator's poll whenever it changes; absent when the running orchestrator predates it").
  - Add `parseSlotPool(v)`, which returns undefined unless all three fields are finite numbers (`isFiniteNumber`).
  - Register it in `normalizeInfoFields` with `parseOrDelete(rec, "slotPool", parseSlotPool)`.
- `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts`: add a tuple `["slotPool", slotPoolSnapshot(root)]` to the `publishInfoFields(root, ctx.info, [["permits", …]])` call, plus one comment sentence. That sentence says the read is one small slots.json read per poll, and that `publishInfoFields` rewrites the info file only when the value changed.
- `src/status/status-data.ts`: add `slotPool?: SlotPoolSnapshot` to `StatusSnapshot` and fill it as `running && info?.slotPool ? info.slotPool : undefined`, with the same stale-info reasoning as `permits`.
- `src/ui/badges.ts`: add `export function workspacesBadge(pool: StatusSnapshot["slotPool"]): string`.
  - It returns `""` when `pool` is undefined, and also when `pool.waiting === 0 && pool.leased < pool.limit` (spare capacity).
  - Otherwise it returns `` ` · workspaces ${leased}/${limit}` ``, plus `` `, ${waiting} waiting` `` when `waiting > 0`.
  - Its doc says a pool with a free workspace leaves the header byte-identical.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: beside the `permitsBadge` line, add `...(snap.slotPool ? { slotPool: snap.slotPool } : {})` and `workspacesBadge: workspacesBadge(snap.slotPool)`.
- `src/ui/status-render.ts`: beside the `permitsBadge` spans, add `...badgeSpans(workspacesBadge(snap.slotPool), snap.slotPool && snap.slotPool.waiting > 0 ? "yellow" : "blue")`.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts`: beside the `permitsBadge` row, add `if (d.workspacesBadge)`. It renders a row the same way, from `String(d.workspacesBadge).replace(/^ · /, "")` with tone `"blue"`, and uses an icon the file already imports. Its tooltip reads "Pooled workspaces leased out of worktreeSlots, shown once the pool is full, then how many runs wait for one; raise worktreeSlots when runs keep waiting."
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: in the "Workspace pool" bullet, add a sentence. It says that while every workspace is leased, `tumwater status`, the TUI header and the dashboard's team panel show `workspaces <leased>/<worktreeSlots>`, plus `, <n> waiting` when runs queue for one.

**Files touched.** src/git/worktree-pool.ts, src/team/orchestrator-info.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/badges.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/worktree-pool.test.ts, test/orchestrator-info.test.ts, test/badges.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/worktree-pool.test.ts: add a case "slotPoolSnapshot reports leased slots out of worktreeSlots and the leases waiting for one".
  - With `writeConfig(root, { worktreeSlots: 1 })`, hold one `leaseSlot` and start a second without awaiting it. The snapshot reads `{ leased: 1, limit: 1, waiting: 1 }`.
  - After the first lease is released and the second resolves, it reads `leased: 1, waiting: 0`.
  - After both are released, it reads `leased: 0, waiting: 0`.
- test/orchestrator-info.test.ts: add a case "readOrchestratorInfo keeps a well-formed slotPool and drops a malformed one". `slotPool: { leased: 8, limit: 8, waiting: 2 }` comes back unchanged. `slotPool: { leased: "8", limit: 8, waiting: 0 }` leaves `slotPool` undefined, and the file's other fields are still read.
- test/badges.test.ts: add a case "workspacesBadge shows the pool only while it is full or a run waits". It asserts:
  - `workspacesBadge(undefined) === ""`
  - `workspacesBadge({ leased: 3, limit: 8, waiting: 0 }) === ""`
  - `workspacesBadge({ leased: 8, limit: 8, waiting: 0 }) === " · workspaces 8/8"`
  - `workspacesBadge({ leased: 8, limit: 8, waiting: 2 }) === " · workspaces 8/8, 2 waiting"`
- The existing `permitsBadge` case and the existing worktree-pool cases pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### Backend/model split, part 1/5: Tier and role entries take `backend` beside `model`, and an explicit backend routes the id verbatim (planned 2026-10-19 by user, split 2026-10-19 by the plan role, replanned 2026-10-19 by the plan role after review; independent of every other eligible Planned entry — the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/config in parts 10/14, 17/20 and cleanup 3/7-4/7, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/config/config-schema.ts src/config/model-selector.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/config/config-validation.ts src/config/config-write.ts test/model-selector.test.ts test/config-views.test.ts test/config-validation-model.test.ts test/config-write.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19

**Series goal (all five parts).** One config value carries two independent choices today: which agent CLI runs a seam (`pi`, `claude`, `opencode`) and which model it runs. The model string encodes the backend in six overlapping spellings — `claude/<id>` (a backend id used as a provider namespace, `isAgentId(provider)` in `routeModel`), `opencode/<id>`, a bare `claude-…` id (rule 3a, whatever `backend` says), `anthropic/<id>` (pi), any other `provider/<id>` (pi), and a bare id (the top-level `backend`). The operator's complaint is the proof: the opencode CLI with an Anthropic model needs `opencode/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`. The series makes `backend` a sibling of `model` (and `thinking`) wherever a model is chosen — top level, a `model` map's tier entry, a `roles`/`review` entry, a `fallback` step — so a model id is only ever a model id in the vocabulary of the backend that runs it. The key keeps its shipped name; the code's adapter-seam identifiers (`AgentBackend`, backend-traits.ts) are out of scope (plain-terms cleanup 3/7-4/7), and the legacy `provider` key and `fallbackModel` object keep parsing as today. Parts: 1/5 tier and role entries (this), 2/5 fallback steps, 3/5 docs, 4/5 test fixtures move to the explicit form, 5/5 retire the namespace spellings (held for the operator's live-config migration). Parts 1/5-4/5 are additive: every spelling that loads today still loads and routes the same.

**Goal.** A `model` map's tier entry and a `roles.<id>` or `review` entry can name `backend`; an entry's explicit `backend` decides the backend of the model written in that same entry, which passes to that backend as written.

**The rule (decided here; the first attempt was rejected for getting it wrong).** An explicit `backend` binds only to the model id in the same entry, never to a model inherited from elsewhere, and never overrides how an inherited model routes:
- A tier entry `{ backend: B, model: M }` routes M on B. A tier entry with `backend` and no `model` takes `default`'s model only when `default`'s selector routes to B (see "routes to" below); otherwise B's tier default (`AGENT_DEFAULT_MODELS`; none for pi and opencode).
- A role or `review` naming both `backend` and `model` routes its model on its backend.
- A role or `review` naming only `model` routes it by today's rules (namespace provider, rule 3a, the top-level `backend`). It does **not** inherit the tier entry's `backend`: `strong: { backend: "claude", … }` plus `roles.director.model: "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b"` runs the director on pi.
- A role or `review` naming only `backend: B` inherits its tier's resolved model (and pi provider) only when that tier's selector actually routes to B — computed by running the tier's own resolution (its entry's `backend`, else `routeModel`'s legacy rules over its spelling), not by comparing B with the tier entry's `backend ?? config.backend`. Otherwise the seam gets B's tier default. So under a pi default, `model: { default: "claude-opus-5-5" }` (rule 3a → claude) plus a role with `backend: "pi"` gets no model (pi's own default), not `claude-opus-5-5` on pi; and `model: { default: "claude/claude-opus-5-5" }` plus a role with `backend: "claude"` inherits `claude-opus-5-5`, not claude's default-tier `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- A role naming neither runs exactly as its tier resolves.
"Routes to" is the `agent` that `withModelOverrides(config, tier, {})` returns — one helper, used by both the tier-entry and role cases.

**Approach.**
- **Schema** (src/config/config-schema.ts): a tier entry of the top-level `model` map may be a string (as today) or `{ backend?, model?, thinking? }` — export a `ModelSelectorEntry` type and `SELECTOR_ENTRY_KEYS = ["backend", "model", "thinking"]`. `RoleConfig` and the review section gain `backend?: string`; add `"backend"` to `ROLE_ENTRY_KEYS` and `REVIEW_KEYS`. `customRoles[]` entries are untouched — they hold only `name`/`task` (`CUSTOM_LOOP_KEYS`); a custom role picks its model and now its backend through `roles.<name>` like a built-in. The top-level `model` string form and the top-level `backend` are unchanged.
- **Routing** (src/config/model-selector.ts): `routeModel` gains a trailing optional `explicitBackend?: string`, so its existing call in src/agent/claude/claude-backend.ts (`CLAUDE_GATED_MODELS`) needs no edit. When it is set it is the agent: pi keeps `provider`/`model` as parsed; claude and opencode take the whole id — `provider/model` rejoined when a provider was parsed — with no provider. When unset, today's rules apply unchanged. The tier-default fill applies to both paths.
- **Resolution** (src/config/config-views.ts): `topTierSelector` reads an object tier entry's `model`/`thinking`; a new `topTierBackend(config, tier)` returns the entry's `backend` per the rule above (an entry with `backend` but no `model` whose backend differs from `default`'s routed agent yields no inherited model). `withModelOverrides` takes `backend?` in `o` and implements the four role cases above; `seamOverrides` forwards the section's `backend`. `teamModelLabel` passes the tier entry's backend, so flipping it relabels that tier and the reload logs `model_changed`. Keep it one code path: compute the tier's routed `{ agent, provider, model }` first, then apply `o`.
- **Validation** (src/config/config-validation.ts): an object tier entry runs `checkKnownKeys` against `SELECTOR_ENTRY_KEYS`; `backend` on a tier entry, a `roles.<id>` entry or `review` must be one of `AGENT_IDS` (the same check and message the top-level `backend` uses). For every entry naming both `backend` and `model`: explicit `claude` with a `/` in the id is a load error (claude's `--model` takes its own ids); explicit `pi` with no provider is a load error ("pi needs `provider/id`"); explicit `pi` whose provider segment is a backend id (`claude/…`, `opencode/…`) is a load error naming the namespace to drop. Inherited models need no check: the rule only inherits a model already routed to the same backend.
- **`config set model.<tier>`** (src/config/config-write.ts) keeps taking a string; over an object entry it replaces the whole entry with the string and the message names the dropped `backend`. No dotted `model.<tier>.backend` key in this part.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- **No regression, pinned by golden values.** test/config-views.test.ts gains one `ROUTING_GOLDENS` table test: before changing any src file, the implementer builds configs covering each routing shape the file's existing tests exercise — top-level string model; string model with legacy `provider`; map form with a tier entry and with a missing tier (inheriting `default`); bare `claude-…` under pi (rule 3a); `claude/<id>` and `opencode/<id>` under pi; `anthropic/<id>` under `backend: "claude"`; `backend: "claude"` and `backend: "opencode"` with no model; a role selector override; a role tier-name override; a `review` override; a `fallback` chain — records `seamsInUse(config)`'s `{ label, agent, provider, model, thinking }` list for each from the unchanged code, and inlines those lists as the expected values. The test passes unmodified after the src change.
- **Discriminating cases** (each one fails under the rejected rules): (a) pi default, `model: { default: "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b", strong: { backend: "claude", model: "claude-opus-5-5" } }` routes each strong-tier seam to claude `claude-opus-5-5` and every other seam to pi; (b) the same config plus `roles.director.model: "qwenrunner/qwen3.8-27b"` runs the director on pi with provider `qwenrunner`; (c) pi default, `model: { default: "claude-opus-5-5" }`, a role with only `backend: "pi"` resolves agent `pi` with no model and no provider; (d) pi default, `model: { default: "claude/claude-opus-5-5" }`, a role with only `backend: "claude"` resolves `claude-opus-5-5`; (e) a role with `backend: "opencode", model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"` resolves agent `opencode`, model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5`, no provider; (f) a tier entry `{ backend: "claude" }` under a pi default whose `default` is `qwenrunner/…` gets claude's tier default. Delete or rewrite any test comment that says a role naming only `model` inherits its tier entry's backend.
- An unknown `backend` in a tier entry, role or review; an unknown key in an object tier entry; a `/` id under explicit claude; a provider-less id under explicit pi; and `claude/…` under explicit pi each fail `validateConfig` with a message naming the path and value (test/config-validation-model.test.ts).
- `npm test` passes.

### `tumwater status`, the TUI header and the dashboard's team panel show the check permits in use out of `maxConcurrentChecks`, and how many checks wait for one (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — none of them touches src/concurrency/check-permit.ts, src/team/orchestrator-info.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts or src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts; the report check-wait plan above also edits the `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet in docs/how-it-works.md, so whichever lands second rebases one sentence; the blocked plain-terms parts reach src/ui/badges.ts and src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts only in far-behind parts; touches src/concurrency/check-permit.ts + src/team/orchestrator-info.ts + src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts + src/status/status-data.ts + src/ui/badges.ts + src/ui/status-payload.ts + src/ui/status-render.ts + src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts + docs/how-it-works.md + test/check-permit.test.ts + test/orchestrator-info.test.ts + test/badges.test.ts); done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The run-permit pool is visible live: the orchestrator's poll publishes `ctx.semaphore.snapshot()` as the info file's `permits` field, and `permitsBadge` (src/ui/badges.ts) renders `running 5 of 8 · omlx 3/3` in the status/TUI header and the dashboard's team panel. The check-permit pool (`checkPermits`, src/concurrency/check-permit.ts) has no live readout. A check that waits shows up only after the fact, as a `check_wait` event or the doctor's 24 h "check contention" row. While merges stall, an operator cannot see that both check slots are busy and three checks are queued, which is the moment `maxConcurrentChecks` matters. This plan publishes the check pool's state the same way and shows it only while a check runs or waits, so an idle team's header does not change.

**Approach.**
- `src/concurrency/check-permit.ts`: export `checkPermitSnapshot(): { inUse: number; limit: number; waiting: number }`. It reads `checkPermits.snapshot().inUse`, `checkPermits.limit` and `checkPermits.waiting` (the Semaphore getters that already exist). Doc it as the check pool's live state for observers. `limit` is the cap set by the most recent `withCheckPermit` call, or the default before any check has run.
- `src/team/orchestrator-info.ts`: add `export interface CheckPermitSnapshot { inUse: number; limit: number; waiting: number }` beside `PermitSnapshot`. Add `checkPermits?: CheckPermitSnapshot` to `OrchestratorInfo` after `permits`, with a doc in the same style ("written by the orchestrator's poll whenever it changes; absent when the running orchestrator predates it"). Add `parseCheckPermits(v)`, which returns undefined unless all three fields are finite numbers (`isFiniteNumber`). Register it in `normalizeInfoFields` with `parseOrDelete(rec, "checkPermits", parseCheckPermits)`.
- `src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts`: in the existing `publishInfoFields(root, ctx.info, [["permits", …]])` call, add a second tuple `["checkPermits", checkPermitSnapshot()]`, and extend the comment above it by one sentence about the check pool.
- `src/status/status-data.ts`: add `checkPermits?: CheckPermitSnapshot` to `StatusSnapshot` after `permits`. Fill it as `running && info?.checkPermits ? info.checkPermits : undefined`, with the same stale-info comment as `permits`.
- `src/ui/badges.ts`: add `export function checksBadge(checks: StatusSnapshot["checkPermits"]): string` after `permitsBadge`. It returns `""` when `checks` is undefined or when `inUse === 0 && waiting === 0`. Otherwise it returns `` ` · checks ${inUse}/${limit}` ``, plus `` `, ${waiting} waiting` `` when `waiting > 0`. Its doc says that an idle check pool leaves the header byte-identical.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: after the `permitsBadge` line, add `...(snap.checkPermits ? { checkPermits: snap.checkPermits } : {})` and `checksBadge: checksBadge(snap.checkPermits)`.
- `src/ui/status-render.ts`: after the `permitsBadge` spans, add `...badgeSpans(checksBadge(snap.checkPermits), snap.checkPermits && snap.checkPermits.waiting > 0 ? "yellow" : "blue")`, with a one-line comment.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts`: after the `permitsBadge` row, add `if (d.checksBadge)`. It renders a row the same way, from `String(d.checksBadge).replace(/^ · /, "")` with `icon("gauge")`, tone `"blue"`, and the tooltip "Checks of the project's suite running at once out of maxConcurrentChecks, then how many wait for a check slot; merge checks go first."
- `docs/how-it-works.md`: in the `maxConcurrentChecks` bullet, add a sentence saying that while a check runs or waits, `tumwater status`, the TUI header and the dashboard's team panel show `checks <running>/<cap>`, plus `, <n> waiting` when checks are queued.

**Files touched.** src/concurrency/check-permit.ts, src/team/orchestrator-info.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-poll.ts, src/status/status-data.ts, src/ui/badges.ts, src/ui/status-payload.ts, src/ui/status-render.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-team.ts, docs/how-it-works.md, test/check-permit.test.ts, test/orchestrator-info.test.ts, test/badges.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- test/check-permit.test.ts: a new case "checkPermitSnapshot reports the checks holding a permit and the checks waiting for one". With `{ maxConcurrentChecks: 1 }`, hold one `withCheckPermit` open on a deferred promise and start a second. The snapshot reads `{ inUse: 1, limit: 1, waiting: 1 }`. After both settle it reads `inUse: 0, waiting: 0`.
- test/orchestrator-info.test.ts: a new case "readOrchestratorInfo keeps a well-formed checkPermits and drops a malformed one". It writes the info file with `checkPermits: { inUse: 2, limit: 2, waiting: 1 }`, then with `checkPermits: { inUse: "2", limit: 2, waiting: 0 }`. The first comes back unchanged. The second leaves `checkPermits` undefined, and the file's other fields are still read.
- test/badges.test.ts: a new case "checksBadge shows the check pool only while a check runs or waits". It asserts `checksBadge(undefined) === ""`, `checksBadge({ inUse: 0, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }) === ""`, `checksBadge({ inUse: 1, limit: 2, waiting: 0 }) === " · checks 1/2"`, and `checksBadge({ inUse: 2, limit: 2, waiting: 3 }) === " · checks 2/2, 3 waiting"`.
- The existing "permitsBadge shows the team line slots and stays byte-identical without a pool" case and the check-permit cases pass unchanged.
- `npm run test:gate` passes.

### `tumwater history --role` takes a comma-separated list of role ids, so one listing or summary covers every role an operator is comparing (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry: it touches only src/cli/cli-args.ts, src/history/history.ts, src/history/history-data.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md's Watch run history row and two history tests, and none of the in-flight entries edits those files. The blocked plain-terms run parts 6/20 and 7/20 rename symbols in history-data.ts and history.ts, which means at most a rebase) — done 2026-10-19

**Goal.** `history --role` narrows to ONE role today. `cmdHistory` (`src/history/history.ts`) resolves it through `parseRoleScope` (`src/cli/cli-args.ts`), which calls `parseRoleFlag` and returns a single id. So "every feature instance" (`feature,feature-2,feature-3`) or "the two code-cleaning roles" (`clean,dedupe`) takes one command per role, and `--summary`/`--json`/`-n` cannot cover the union in one document. The sibling `--result` flag already takes a comma list (PLANS-DONE.md, "`tumwater history --result` takes a comma-separated list…"). This plan gives `--role` the same shape on the same command. A single id behaves exactly as it does now.

**Approach.**
- `src/cli/cli-args.ts`: add `parseRoleListScope(root: string, args: string[]): string[] | null`, next to `parseRoleScope`. It returns null when `--role` is absent, and reads no config in that case, the same rule `parseRoleScope`'s doc states. A missing or empty value fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR` (`src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`). Otherwise it splits on `,`, trims each piece and drops empty pieces; when no piece is left it fails with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`. Each piece goes through `canonicalRoleId` (`src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts`) and is checked against `knownRoleIdsCached(root)`. The first unknown piece fails with `unknownRoleMessage(piece, ids)` (`src/roles/roles.ts`). Duplicates are removed and first-seen order is kept. Leave `parseRoleScope` and its other callers (`cmdLogs` in src/cli/log-commands.ts, `src/report/report.ts`) unchanged: `logs --role` is a single-transcript view and `report --role` scopes one role's report, so a list means nothing there.
- `src/history/history-data.ts`: widen the `role` parameter of `tickRows`, `readTickRows` and `readTickRowsSince` from `string | null` to `string | readonly string[] | null`. At the top of `tickRows`, normalize it to a `Set` (`null` keeps every event). Both the `scoped` filter and the `joinScoped` filter then test `wanted.has(e.source)` instead of `e.source === role`. The `readTickRows` memo key joins an array with `,`, so a one-element list and its bare string share a key. The GUI (`src/gui/`) and TUI (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-history.ts`) callers keep passing a string and stay untouched. The window-growth loop in `readTickRows` already grows on "rows fall short", so `-n` keeps its meaning: the last N runs across the listed roles.
- `src/history/history.ts`: `cmdHistory` calls `parseRoleListScope` in both the `--since` and the `-n` branch, replacing `parseRoleScope`, and passes the list through. Update `cmdHistory`'s doc comment and the usage line in its header comment to `--role <id>[,<id>...]`. No empty-state wording changes: a role filter has never been named in the empty-state line.
- `src/cli/help.ts`: the history usage line reads `[--role <id>[,<id>...]]`, and one clause says a comma list keeps the rows of any listed role. docs/cli.md's "Watch run history" row gets the same spelling and an example (`--role feature,feature-2 --summary` tallies both feature instances).

**Files touched.** src/cli/cli-args.ts, src/history/history.ts, src/history/history-data.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md, test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts, test/history-data.test.ts, test/cli-history.test.ts (the help-stanza regex).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- New test in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts, "history --role takes a comma list of role ids": on a log holding feature, clean and bugfix runs, `history --role feature,clean --json` lists exactly the feature and clean rows, newest first. `--role feature,clean --summary --json` has exactly those two roles in `roles`. `--role clean,clean` equals `--role clean`.
- The list composes with `--since`, `-n` (`-n 2 --role feature,clean` returns the two newest runs across both roles even when a third role's runs sit between them), `--grep` and `--result`.
- `--role feature,nosuch` fails naming `nosuch` with the `unknown role:` wording and its valid ids. `--role ,` and a bare trailing `--role` fail with `ROLE_VALUE_ERROR`.
- A `tickRows` unit case in test/history-data.test.ts: an array of two ids keeps both sources' rows, including a queued row's merge verdict resolved through the join. A one-element array returns the same rows as the bare string.
- The existing single-id tests in test/cli-history-filtering.test.ts ("history --grep composes with --role", "history --result composes with --since and --role") pass unchanged. `logs --role a,b` still fails as an unknown role, because `parseRoleScope` is untouched.
