The pause editor's three Activity-view arms (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+Q, Ctrl+R in `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`) and the shared `/` search editor's arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-search.ts`) each gained `!session.held.fallback` in their own held-flag guard lists, so none of them opens or fires over the fallback editor on the shared prompt line — a second guard direction beside `heldEditorFlash` — and `onArrow`'s no-editor condition in `src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts` gained `!session.held.fallback` too, keeping Up/Down from recalling prompt history into its text. `tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes with the table's `Ctrl+L | Activity, Transcript` row.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's agent backends (`backends`) with Ctrl+X, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Agent backends (JSON)` field and `tumwater config set backends` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 2/14 moves src/runner, src/roles/runner-ids.ts and their tests and reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts; the in-flight TUI editors (worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L, notify Ctrl+E) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-backends.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-backends.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team's agent-backends section — the top-level `backends` key, a map from the reserved backend ids (`pi`, `claude`) to their per-backend `bin`/`args` (and claude's `configDir`) entries (`backends?: Record<string, AgentConfig>`, `src/config/config-schema.ts`; each entry validated by `checkObjectSection(r, "backends", …)` in `validateConfig`, `src/config/config-validation.ts`) — is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Agent backends (JSON)`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose `settingsFieldValue` renders the object as compact JSON) and `tumwater config set backends '{"pi":{"bin":"…"}}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: no `tui-editor-backends.ts` exists and `grep -rn backends src/ui/tui` finds no editor (only the plain-terms rename comments of the blocked series). The Activity view (view 0) already edits every other dashboard Settings row — the daily cap (`Ctrl+B`), provider caps (`Ctrl+P`), run cap (`Ctrl+N`), quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`), and, once the in-flight entries land, slots, model, fallback and notify — so `backends` is the last row without a terminal twin; add it beside them. `Ctrl+X` is free on Activity: `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`); the panes' `Ctrl+X` router (`src/ui/tui/tui-panes.ts`) sends the key to the Transcript notes-clear arm (guarded by `noteMode`), the Queued cancel arm and the Backlog cancel arm, all of which are guarded to their own views, and the retire editor's `Ctrl+X` arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-retire.ts`, mnemonic “**x** remove”) is guarded to the Health view (`ctx.view === ctx.roleIds.length + 7`), so on Activity no arm consumes it today. Mnemonic: the section names the backend **eX**ecutables (each entry's `bin`/`args`).

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-backends.ts** (new) — `createBackendsEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createProviderCapsEditor` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts`): a private `backendsMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitBackendsMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.backends` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "x"`: toggle out when `backendsMode`, return false when `ctx.view !== 0` (the Transcript/Inbox/Backlog/Health `Ctrl+X` arms keep their meaning), otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("backends")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `backendsMode` and `session.held.backends`, pre-fill `session.input` with the compact JSON of the section the file actually holds and `""` when it holds none — read from the raw file (`parseJsonConfig`) rather than the merged config, because init/saveConfig write an empty `{}` section even when the operator never set it, so the merged view can't tell "unset" from a set-but-empty section (an empty section also pre-fills empty, matching "empty clears" on save); the dashboard's merged `GET /api/config` source is where the provider-caps editor reads from, but its `backends` always defaults to `{}`, so the raw read is what gives the pinned "empty when unset", place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's agent backends (backends, a JSON object like {"pi":{"bin":"/path/to/pi"}}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "backends")` and, on `ok`, flashes `agent backends cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "backends", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `agent backends set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a compact object becomes the section, while `pi` collapses to the literal string) and, because the key is the whole section, its top-level arm runs `collapseAgentAliases` so a legacy `agentBin`/`piArgs` can never sit beside the new `backends.pi` spelling; `validateConfig` owns the value's truth through `checkObjectSection`, rejecting a non-object with `backends must be an object (got …)` and a non-object entry with `backends.<id> must be an object with optional bin and args (got …)`; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitBackendsMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitBackendsMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and provider-caps editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `backends: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+X agent-backends editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"backends"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. In the guard body add, beside the sibling early clauses, `if (h.backends && entering !== "backends") return session.busyFlash("agent backends");`, and add an `entering === "backends"` clause at the bottom that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions`/`h.providerCaps`/`h.concurrency` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use; the early clause above only covers flags with their own `!== entering` clause, so the bottom clause is what holds `h.budget` out). If the in-flight `slots`/`model`/`fallback`/`notify` flags have landed, name them in the same two places the sibling entries already do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `backendsMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `providerCapsMode`; import `createBackendsEditor` and add `createBackendsEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createProviderCapsEditor(session)` (it must sit before `createRetireEditor(session)` so the Activity view reaches it, and the retire arm still gets `Ctrl+X` on Health because this arm returns false off view 0); return `backendsMode: session.held.backends` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.backends` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.providerCaps`), adding any in-flight flags that are present there too.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `backendsMode: s.backendsMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `backendsMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "agent backends", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.backendsMode`, placed with the existing provider-caps/budget prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.backendsMode) keys = [["Enter", "save agent backends"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside those branches; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+X", "agent backends"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]` and `["Ctrl+P", "provider caps"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — in the `## TUI keys` table, add `Activity` to the `Ctrl+X` rows' Where columns (the cancel rows for Backlog/Inbox and the Health retire row are keyed by view, so add a distinct `Ctrl+X | Activity | edit the team's agent backends (backends, a JSON object of per-backend bin/args such as {"pi":{"bin":"/path/to/pi"}}; empty clears it)` row rather than folding it into another view's row), and in the Configure row extend the `backends` clause that already names the dashboard Agent backends row with the Activity `Ctrl+X` editor.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-backends.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+X opens with the footer `agent backends ›` and the line empty when `tumwater.json` leaves the key unset, and pre-filled with compact JSON when it holds `backends`; Enter on a valid object (`{"pi":{"bin":"/opt/pi"}}`) writes it and flashes `agent backends set to <text>`; Enter on a non-object (`pi`) or a bad entry (`{"pi":5}`) flashes the validator's `backends …` message and stays open with the text kept and `tumwater.json` byte-identical; Enter on an empty line removes the key (it disappears from the file) and flashes `agent backends cleared`, leaving the file unchanged when it was already absent; a file with a legacy `agentBin` and a saved `backends.pi.bin` round-trips to the single `backends.pi.bin` spelling (no `agentBin` left); Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with the budget editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+X flashes the busy message and leaves the budget editor open. With `makeTuiRepo` seeding a legacy `agentBin`, open, confirm the pre-fill, type a new object and Enter, then assert `agentBin` is gone from the file.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+X on Activity opens the backends editor (`session.state().backendsMode`), while Ctrl+X on a role's Transcript notes view still clears notes and on the Health view still opens the retire editor, so the new arm does not swallow those keys.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, backendsMode: true })` reading `agent backends ›` and the hint branch's `save agent backends`; and the Activity hint line naming `Ctrl+X agent backends`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+X opens the editor; the footer reads `agent backends › `, the line pre-fills compact JSON from a set `backends` (empty when unset) and the open flash names `backends` and the JSON-object shape. On Transcript/Inbox/Backlog/Health, Ctrl+X keeps its existing meaning (the new arm returns false off view 0).
- Enter with a JSON object writes `backends` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `agent backends set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `agent backends cleared`; a non-object or a non-object entry flashes the validator's `backends …` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Saving over a file that carries the legacy `agentBin`/`piArgs` leaves exactly one spelling (`backends.pi.bin`/`.args`), thanks to the whole-section arm's `collapseAgentAliases`. A successful save rewrites the whole default-expanded config through `setConfigKey` → `writeConfigMutation`, so it is not byte-identical even for a no-op open/Enter on an already single-spelling object — the file is reformatted; byte-identity is only asserted for a rejected save (the `{ok:false}` path leaves the file untouched).
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line (e.g. the budget editor on Ctrl+B), and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, backendsMode: true })` reads `agent backends › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s backends branch names `save agent backends`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+X agent backends`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+X | Activity` row naming the agent backends and `backends`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm test` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 3/14: Rename RoleRunner and the run pipeline context (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 2/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/ + test/runner*.test.ts + test/revision.test.ts + test/leftover.test.ts + test/model-fallback.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** `LoopRunner` becomes `RoleRunner` and `LoopTickContext` becomes `RunnerRunContext`; the rest of src/runner/ and its tests read "runner" and "role" instead of "loop".

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show.
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier, and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names (state-file fields, event fields, `--json`/`/api` keys, config keys, env vars) are out of scope; name any leftover in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners` (or `role`/`roles` for ids or display rows), never shadowing a name already bound in an enclosing scope.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role", or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Leave quoted PLANS.md/BUGS.md titles, `plans/*.md` names and commit subjects alone; rewrap comments past 100 columns; update docs/invariants.md quotes of test titles you change.
  - Exports used outside this part get a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen; members get none. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. Migrate this part's uses of earlier renames (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test`), and delete any alias no other file names (test/exports.test.ts).
- src/runner/runner.ts: `class LoopRunner` → `class RoleRunner`, with the two-line aliases `/** @deprecated Use RoleRunner. */` + `export const LoopRunner = RoleRunner;` and `/** @deprecated Use RoleRunner. */` + `export type LoopRunner = RoleRunner;` (26 src and 18 test files name it). Its comments ("this role loop", "the loop's …") follow the series rules.
- src/runner/runner-run.ts: `LoopTickContext` → `RunnerRunContext` (used only by runner.ts and runner-run.ts, so no alias). It takes its final name here; the tick-named members inside it are Plain terms code run's.
- Comments in src/runner/leftover.ts, model-fallback.ts, revision.ts, runner-fallback.ts and runner-recovery.ts.
- Tests: test/runner.test.ts, test/runner-2.test.ts through test/runner-5.test.ts, and test/runner-{counters,fallback,interrupted,leftover-recovery,merge-conflicts,prompt-requeue,quiet-watchdog,recovery,red-main,refusal,transient-retry}.test.ts, test/revision.test.ts, test/leftover.test.ts, test/model-fallback.test.ts: migrate `makeLoopRunner`, `LoopRunner`, `LoopState`, `freshLoopState`, `loadLoopState`, `saveLoopState` and `LoopPi` to the new names, and convert comments and test titles.

**Files touched.** All of src/runner/ except runner-state.ts and runner-pi.ts (done in part 2/14), plus the test files listed above. Two part-2/14 files are touched despite that line: runner-pi.ts loses its now-dead `LoopPi` deprecated re-export (no code user remains, so test/exports.test.ts would fail; only comment mentions of `LoopPi` survive), and runner-state.ts's `freshlyWoken` doc has its two "the loop" comment senses fixed to "the runner" so the `loops?` acceptance grep lists only kept senses. No identifier or behavior in either file changes.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `RoleRunner` and `RunnerRunContext` are the declared names; `LoopRunner` exists only as the deprecated alias pair in src/runner/runner.ts.
- `grep -rnwiE 'loops?' src/runner test/runner*.test.ts test/revision.test.ts test/leftover.test.ts test/model-fallback.test.ts` lists only kept senses: JavaScript, poll, event, retry or crash loops.
- No behavior change: the suite's test count is unchanged.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's notify hook (`notify`) with Ctrl+E, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Notify hook` field and `tumwater config set notify` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — runner part 2/14 moves src/runner and test/runner*, and the in-flight TUI editors (run cap Ctrl+N, worktree slots Ctrl+W, model Ctrl+A, fallback Ctrl+L) each add one editor module beside this one and share its seams — src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts — plus docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table, so whichever lands second rebases; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-notify.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-notify.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The team's `notify` key (an optional string, the shell command the orchestrator runs when a notable event fires; absent or empty means off — `notify?: string` in `src/config/config-schema.ts`, validated by the `if ("notify" in r && typeof r.notify !== "string")` block in `validateConfig`, `src/config/config-validation.ts`) is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Notify hook`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, which also gives it a Send test) and `tumwater config set notify`, and testable from the TUI's Health view (`Ctrl+N`, `createHealthPane` in `src/ui/tui/tui-pane-health.ts`) — but the TUI cannot edit it: `grep -rn notify src/ui/tui` finds only that Health test. The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`), per-provider caps (`Ctrl+P`, `createProviderCapsEditor`), quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`, `createQuietEditor`) and, once the in-flight entries land, its run cap, slots, model and fallback. Add the notify hook beside them. `Ctrl+E` is free for the editor subsystem on Activity: `createTuiKeys` routes every key through the editor modules before the pane arms (`src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts`, `editors.handleKey(...)` ahead of `panes.handleKey(...)`), the `createReportPane` Ctrl+E arm (`src/ui/tui/tui-pane-report.ts`) is therefore only reached when no editor consumed the key, and off its Usage/Failures views it merely advances a report window that draws nothing there; every other `Ctrl+E` editor arm requires a view or selection Activity never has (`ctx.briefMode`, `noteMode`, `entryEditFor`, `queuedEditFor`).

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-notify.ts** (new) — `createNotifyEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createProviderCapsEditor`: a private `notifyMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitNotifyMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.notify` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "e"`: toggle out when `notifyMode`, return false when `ctx.view !== 0` (every other view keeps its own Ctrl+E — the Usage/Failures window, the Health reclaim, the notes/Brief file replace), otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("notify")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft((t) => (savedInput = t), (n) => (savedCursor = n))`, set `notifyMode` and `session.held.notify`, pre-fill `session.input` with `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.notify ?? ""`, place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's notify hook (notify, the shell command run on notable events; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "notify")` and, on `ok`, flashes `notify hook cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "notify", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `notify hook set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so a bare `notify-me` stays the literal string, while a typed `42` or `{"a":1}` becomes a non-string) and `validateConfig`'s notify block owns the value's truth, rejecting a non-string with `notify must be a string (the shell command to run on notable events, empty string disables; got …)`; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitNotifyMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitNotifyMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and provider-caps editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `notify: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+E notify-hook editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"notify"` to the union of `entering` values in `heldEditorFlash`. In the guard body add, beside the sibling early clauses, `if (h.notify && entering !== "notify") return session.busyFlash("notify hook");`, and add an `entering === "notify"` clause at the bottom that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions`/`h.providerCaps` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use; the early clause above only covers flags with their own `!== entering` clause, so the bottom clause is what holds `h.budget` out, exactly as the fallback entry words its `entering === "fallback"` clause). If the in-flight `concurrency`/`slots`/`model`/`fallback` flags have landed, name them in the same two places the sibling entries already do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `notifyMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `providerCapsMode`; import `createNotifyEditor` and add `createNotifyEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createProviderCapsEditor(session)`; return `notifyMode: session.held.notify` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.notify` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.providerCaps`), adding any in-flight flags that are present there too.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `notifyMode: s.notifyMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `notifyMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "notify hook", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.notifyMode`, placed with the existing provider-caps/budget prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.notifyMode) keys = [["Enter", "save the notify hook"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside those branches; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+E", "notify hook"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.

**Tests.**

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+E opens the editor; the footer reads `notify hook › `, the line pre-fills the file's `notify` string (empty when unset) and the open flash names `notify` and the empty-clears rule. On Usage/Failures/Health/Transcript/Brief, Ctrl+E keeps its existing meaning (the new arm returns false off view 0).
- Enter with a command writes `notify` as that string through `setConfigKey` and flashes `notify hook set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `notify hook cleared`; a number or object (`42`, `{"a":1}`) flashes the validator's `notify must be a string` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line (e.g. the budget editor on Ctrl+B), and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team's worktree pool size (`worktreeSlots`) with Ctrl+W, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `Worktree slots` field and `tumwater config set worktreeSlots` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the plan-rerun entry edits src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling, src/orchestrator and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, the queue-order entry src/roles and src/prompt, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; the in-flight quiet-hours and Ctrl+N run-cap entries also edit src/ui/tui and share src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx and tui-frame.ts with this one — each adds one editor module, one held flag, one state field and one frame branch — and share docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table as different rows, a rebase either way; when the Ctrl+N run-cap entry has landed, this plan's new `heldEditorFlash` clause includes its `concurrency` flag in the held-flag list; the blocked plain-terms series reaches src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase; touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-slots.ts (new) src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-slots.test.ts (new) test/tui-keys.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The worktree pool's slot budget `worktreeSlots` (an optional positive integer; `slotCount(config)` in `src/config/config.ts` reads it live as `worktreeSlots ?? maxConcurrent + 1`, validated by `checkNumber(r, "", "worktreeSlots", POSITIVE_INTEGER)` in `src/config/config-validation.ts`) is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Worktree slots`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`) and `tumwater config set worktreeSlots`, but the TUI has no editor for it: `grep -rn worktreeSlots src/ui/tui` finds nothing. `tumwater doctor`'s `checkWorktreePool` names the key when the pool is the contended resource. The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`), its run cap (`Ctrl+N`, `createConcurrencyEditor`, in flight) and, once the in-flight quiet-hours plan lands, its quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`). Add the pool size beside them, so a terminal operator can widen the disk knob without leaving the TUI. `Ctrl+W` is free on Activity: the only `Ctrl+W` arm today is the shared pause editor's wake key, guarded by `pauseEditRole !== null` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`), so on Activity (where `pauseEditRole` is null and the team editors use `Ctrl+F`/`Ctrl+Q`) it falls through; on a role's Transcript it still opens the wake editor.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-slots.ts** (new) — `createSlotsEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createQuietEditor`/`createConcurrencyEditor`: a private `slotsMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitSlotsMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.slots` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "w"`: enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (the team scope), otherwise return false so the pause editor's wake arm keeps the key on a role's Transcript; toggle out when already open; otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("slots")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft(...)`, set `slotsMode` and `session.held.slots`, pre-fill `session.input` with `String(loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.worktreeSlots ?? "")` (empty when unset), place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's worktree pool size (worktreeSlots, an integer ≥ 1; empty restores the default of maxConcurrent + 1): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "worktreeSlots")` and, on `ok`, flashes `worktree slots reset to the default`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "worktreeSlots", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `worktree slots set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text and `validateConfig` (whose `checkNumber` names `worktreeSlots must be an integer of at least 1`) owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitSlotsMode()`, restoring the draft. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the quiet and budget editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `slots: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+W worktree-pool editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"slots"` to the `heldEditorFlash(entering: ...)` union; extend the guard body: `if (h.slots && entering !== "slots") return session.busyFlash("worktree slots");`, and a `if (entering === "slots" && (h.attach || h.notes || h.budget || h.brief || h.retire || h.quiet || h.interval || h.instructions)) return session.busyFlash(...)` clause mirroring the quiet/interval/instructions entries (naming whichever held editor is set), extended with `h.concurrency` if the Ctrl+N run-cap entry has landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `slotsMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createSlotsEditor` and add it to the `editors` array (directly after the concurrency editor when that plan has landed, else after `createBudgetEditor(session)`); return `slotsMode: session.held.slots` from `state()`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `slotsMode: s.slotsMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `slotsMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "worktree slots", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.slotsMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.slotsMode) keys = [["Enter", "save worktree slots"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table gains a `| Ctrl+W | Activity | edit the team's worktree pool size (`worktreeSlots`, an integer ≥ 1; empty restores the `maxConcurrent + 1` default) |` row, one row per (key, view) beside the existing Transcript `Ctrl+W` in the `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+V` row.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-slots.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+W opens with the footer `worktree slots ›` and the line pre-filled from `tumwater.json`'s `worktreeSlots` (empty when unset); Enter on a valid integer writes the number to `tumwater.json` and flashes `worktree slots set to <n>`; Enter on `0`/`two` flashes the `worktreeSlots must be an integer of at least 1` message and leaves the editor open and the file byte-identical; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line unsets the key (it disappears from the file) and flashes the reset wording, leaving the file bytes unchanged when the key was already absent; Esc and Ctrl+T from the editor restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with another editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+W flashes the busy message and leaves it open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+W on Activity opens the worktree-slots editor (`session.held.slots`), while Ctrl+W on a role's Transcript still opens the wake editor (`session.held.pauseWake`), so the new arm does not swallow the wake key.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, slotsMode: true })` reading `worktree slots ›` and the hint branch's `save worktree slots`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+W opens the editor; the footer reads `worktree slots › `, the line pre-fills the file's numeric `worktreeSlots` (empty when unset) and the open flash names `worktreeSlots` and the empty-restores-default rule. On a role's Transcript, Ctrl+W still opens the wake editor.
- Enter with a valid integer writes a JSON number `worktreeSlots` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `worktree slots set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `worktree slots reset to the default`; a non-integer or `0` flashes the validator's `worktreeSlots must be an integer of at least 1` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line, and another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, slotsMode: true })` reads `worktree slots › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s slots branch names `save worktree slots`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+W | Activity` row naming the worktree pool size and `worktreeSlots`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.
- `npm test` passes.

### Plain terms code runner, part 2/14: Rename runner state and instance ids and the runner pi wrapper (planned 2026-10-16 by user; requires part 1/14 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/runner/runner-state.ts + src/runner/runner-pi.ts + src/roles/runner-ids.ts + test/runner-state.test.ts + test/runner-ids.test.ts + test/runner-pi*.test.ts + test/fixtures/runner-*.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The most widely used runner exports take their new names, `RunnerState`, `freshRunnerState`, `loadRunnerState`, `saveRunnerState`, `runnerIds`, `runnerEnabled` and `RunnerPi`, behind deprecated aliases, so later parts migrate callers one directory at a time.

**Approach.**
- Series rules (every code-runner part):
  - Identifier words follow plans/terminology.md "Code names", row "loop": `runner` for the worker object, its state and an instance id; `role` for what the status table, dashboard and TUI show (rows, cells, rank, phase, drawer).
  - Keep `loopback*`, `pollLoop`, `crashLoop`, `onCrashLoop`, every `customLoop*`/`CUSTOM_LOOP_*` identifier (Plain terms code cleanup renames them), and "loop" meaning a JavaScript loop, the poll loop, the event loop, or a retry, crash or feedback loop.
  - Serialized names are out of scope: state-file fields, event fields, `--json` and `/api` keys, config keys and env vars were renamed by earlier series with legacy readers. If one still says "loop", leave it and name it in the commit message.
  - Legacy readers keep the old names on purpose; rename nothing inside them: the legacy-name tables in `normalizeLegacyEvent`, the state loaders' legacy-key maps, the `legacyLand*` path helpers, src/orchestrator/startup-migrations.ts and startup-migration-steps.ts, `CONFIG_KEY_RENAMES` in src/config/config-aliases.ts, src/roles/legacy-role-ids.ts, and test fixtures that deliberately write old event names or state keys to disk. test/retired-names.test.ts exempts them through `LEGACY_FILES`, identifiers whose first word is `legacy`, `// retired-name-ok: <reason>` lines and `retired-name-ok:start`/`end` regions; mark any new such site with one of those, never a new mechanism.
  - A bare `loop`/`loops` binding becomes `runner`/`runners`, or `role`/`roles` when it holds role ids or display rows. If that name is already bound in an enclosing scope of the same file, pick a distinct one (`roleRunner`, `runnerId`): never shadow.
  - Comments and test titles: "loop" → "role" ("the feature role", "per-role", "custom role"), or "runner" when the sentence is about the `RoleRunner` object or one instance's state. Never edit a quoted PLANS.md or BUGS.md title, a `plans/*.md` name or a quoted commit subject (test/plan-citations.test.ts checks cited titles). Rewrap any comment line pushed past 100 columns (test/comment-width.test.ts). If docs/invariants.md quotes a test title you change, update the quote.
  - An export used by files outside this part keeps a two-line alias, `/** @deprecated Use NewName. */` on its own line above `export const OldName = NewName;` (`export type` for a type; for the `LoopPi` class the re-export form `export { RunnerPi as LoopPi };` is used instead, because a `const` class alias trips the no-unsafe-* eslint rules on `this.pi`). Never write it on one line: test/exports.test.ts skips lines starting `/**`, so a dead one-line alias would linger unseen. A new name needs a user outside its own file in the same part (its test counts), or test/exports.test.ts fails. A member (method, property, interface field) gets no alias: rename all its uses in this part. Migrate every use, in this part's files, of a name an earlier part renamed (`grep -rn '@deprecated Use' src test` lists the live aliases). Delete any alias whose old name no other file mentions any more, because test/exports.test.ts fails an export nothing else names.
- src/runner/runner-state.ts: `LoopState` → `RunnerState`, `freshLoopState` → `freshRunnerState`, `loadLoopState` → `loadRunnerState`, `saveLoopState` → `saveRunnerState`, each with a two-line alias (`/** @deprecated Use RunnerState. */` then `export type LoopState = RunnerState;`; `/** @deprecated Use freshRunnerState. */` then `export const freshLoopState = freshRunnerState;`; …). The private `liveClaimLoopIds` → `liveClaimRunnerIds`. Do not touch the persisted field names inside `RunnerState`.
- src/roles/runner-ids.ts: `loopIds` → `runnerIds`, `loopEnabled` → `runnerEnabled`, and the grep-required `loopPaused` → `runnerPaused`, all with aliases.
- src/runner/runner-pi.ts: `LoopPi` → `RunnerPi` (alias), `LoopPiHost` → `RunnerPiHost` (renamed directly — `LoopPiHost` has no user outside this file, so an alias would fail test/exports.test.ts).
- test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts: `makeLoopRunner` → `makeRoleRunner`, `spentLoopState` → `spentRunnerState`, with aliases (25 and 8 test files use them). test/fixtures/runner-pi-fixtures.ts and the runner-pi tests: `loopPi` → `runnerPi`, `loopPiOpts` → `runnerPiOpts`.
- Comments and test titles in all files of this part, per the series rules.

**Implementation notes (added 2026-10-19).** The new-name-needs-a-user rule (test/exports.test.ts) had no natural in-part user for `makeRoleRunner`, so runner-pi.test.ts gains one focused test that assembles a full runner via `makeRoleRunner` (the suite's test count rises by 1); `spentRunnerState` is used by runner-ids.test.ts. The `LoopRunner` class references that remain in test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts and test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts are owned by part 3/14 (which renames the class to `RoleRunner`), so the acceptance grep's "only aliases" holds for this part's files apart from those two; left in place so part 3 has its class. test/runner-pi-opencode.test.ts (a sibling runner-pi suite not in the files-touched list) is migrated `loopPi` → `runnerPi` too because it consumes the shared makeHost fixture. docs/invariants.md's `LoopState.imageReroute` reference is updated to `RunnerState.imageReroute`.

**Files touched.** src/runner/runner-state.ts, src/runner/runner-pi.ts, src/roles/runner-ids.ts, test/runner-state.test.ts, test/runner-ids.test.ts, test/runner-pi.test.ts, test/runner-pi-claude.test.ts, test/runner-pi-followups.test.ts, test/runner-pi-retry.test.ts, test/fixtures/runner-fixtures.ts, test/fixtures/runner-pi-fixtures.ts, plus test/runner-pi-opencode.test.ts and docs/invariants.md (see Implementation notes).

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `RunnerState`, `freshRunnerState`, `loadRunnerState`, `saveRunnerState`, `runnerIds`, `runnerEnabled`, `RunnerPi`, `makeRoleRunner` and `spentRunnerState` are the declared names; each old name exists only as a `@deprecated` alias.
- `grep -nE '[Ll]oop[A-Z]|[a-z0-9]Loop|LOOP_' ` over this part's files lists only the aliases (apart from the part-3-owned `LoopRunner` class in runner-fixtures.ts and runner-pi-retry.test.ts; see Implementation notes).
- No behavior change: no assertion changed except renamed identifiers and test titles; the suite's test count rises by exactly one (the `makeRoleRunner` assembly test, see Implementation notes).
- `npm run test` passes.

**Goal.** The team's per-provider run caps `maxConcurrentPerProvider` (an optional JSON object mapping a provider key to a positive integer, validated by `checkProviderConcurrencyCap` (`src/config/config-keys.ts`) and the map block in `validateConfig` (`src/config/config-validation.ts`)) is editable from the dashboard Settings view (`Provider concurrency caps (JSON)`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`, whose field renders an object as compact JSON) and `tumwater config set maxConcurrentPerProvider '{"key":2}'`, but the TUI has no editor for it: `grep -rn maxConcurrentPerProvider src/ui/tui` finds nothing. `tumwater doctor`'s `checkProviderContention` (`src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`) names the exact cap to raise. The Activity view (view 0) already edits the team's daily cost cap (`Ctrl+B`, `createBudgetEditor`) and, once the in-flight entries land, its run cap (`Ctrl+N`), worktree slots (`Ctrl+W`) and quiet hours (`Ctrl+S`). Add the provider caps beside them, completing the run-concurrency knob set the doctor points at. `Ctrl+P` is free on Activity: the only `Ctrl+P` arm today is the shared pause editor's pause key, guarded by `pauseEditRole !== null` (`src/ui/tui/tui-editor-pause.ts`), and `pauseEditRole` is null on Activity (the team pause is `Ctrl+F`), so the key falls through there while a role's Transcript keeps it.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-provider-caps.ts** (new) — `createProviderCapsEditor(session: TuiEditorSession)`, mirroring `createBudgetEditor`/`createQuietEditor`: a private `providerCapsMode` flag, a saved-draft pair (`savedInput`/`savedCursor`), an `exitProviderCapsMode()` that clears the flag, clears `session.held.providerCaps` and calls `session.restorePromptFrom(savedInput, savedCursor)`, and a `handleKey` arm keyed on `key.ctrl && key.name === "p"`: enter only when `ctx.view === 0` (the team scope; a role's Transcript keeps its pause/resume key), toggle out when already open, otherwise take the shared `session.heldEditorFlash("providerCaps")` busy guard (flash and return when it names another editor), run `session.settleDraft(...)`, set `providerCapsMode` and `session.held.providerCaps`, pre-fill `session.input` with `JSON.stringify(loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.maxConcurrentPerProvider)` when that map is defined and `""` when it is not, place the cursor at its end, and flash `edit the team's provider concurrency caps (maxConcurrentPerProvider, a JSON object like {"anthropic":2}; empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The Escape arm exits when open. The Enter arm: a whitespace-trimmed empty line calls `unsetConfigKey(session.root, "maxConcurrentPerProvider")` and, on `ok`, flashes `provider concurrency caps cleared`; otherwise `setConfigKey(session.root, "maxConcurrentPerProvider", session.input.trim())` and, on `ok`, flashes `provider concurrency caps set to ${session.input.trim()}` — `setConfigKey` JSON-parses the text (so `{"anthropic":2}` becomes the object, while `anthropic` falls back to the literal string) and `validateConfig` (whose map message is `maxConcurrentPerProvider must be an object mapping provider names to concurrency caps`) owns the value's truth; on `{ok:false}` flash the error and stay open (the file is untouched). Success and cancel both `exitProviderCapsMode()`, restoring the draft. Return `{ handleKey, exit: exitProviderCapsMode }`. Import `loadConfigSafe` from `../../config/config.js` and `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` from `../../config/config-write.js`, as the budget and quiet editors do.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `providerCaps: boolean` to the `TuiHeld` interface, documented as the Activity view's Ctrl+P provider-caps editor, and initialize it `false`; add `"providerCaps"` to the `heldEditorFlash(entering: ...)` union; extend the guard body with `if (h.providerCaps && entering !== "providerCaps") return session.busyFlash("provider caps");` — that holds any other editor out while this one holds the line — and, because `budget` is only excluded through the bottom `entering === "..."` clauses (the guard body has no generic `h.budget && entering !== "budget"` early clause), also add an `entering === "providerCaps"` clause that returns the busy flash for whichever of `h.attach`/`h.notes`/`h.budget`/`h.brief`/`h.retire`/`h.quiet`/`h.interval`/`h.instructions` is set (the same nested-ternary wording the sibling clauses use). The bottom clause is required, not redundant: without it, Ctrl+P while the budget editor holds the shared line would not flash busy and would open over it. If the in-flight Ctrl+N run-cap entry has landed, prefix its `concurrency` flag (and, when landed, the Ctrl+W slots entry's `slots` flag) to this clause's subject list the same way, since those editors add flags to the same `TuiHeld`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `providerCapsMode: boolean` to `TuiEditorState` beside `budgetMode`; import `createProviderCapsEditor` and add `createProviderCapsEditor(session)` to the `editors` array directly after `createBudgetEditor(session)`; return `providerCapsMode: session.held.providerCaps` from `state()`; and add `!session.held.providerCaps` to the `onArrow` no-editor condition that keeps Up/Down from recalling prompt history into a held editor's text (beside `!session.held.budget`), adding `!session.held.concurrency`/`!session.held.slots` there too if those in-flight entries have landed.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `providerCapsMode: s.providerCapsMode` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — add `providerCapsMode?: boolean` to both inline `mode` types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix`; `promptPrefix` returns `[{ text: "provider caps", tone: "brand" }, { text: " › " }]` when `mode.providerCapsMode`, placed with the existing budget/quiet/interval prefix branches; `hintLine` gains `else if (mode.providerCapsMode) keys = [["Enter", "save provider caps"], ["Esc", "cancel"], ["Ctrl+D", "quit"]]` beside the budget branch; and the Activity `else`-branch key list gains `["Ctrl+P", "provider caps"]` beside `["Ctrl+B", "daily cap"]`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys table gains a `| Ctrl+P | Activity | edit the team's per-provider concurrency caps (`maxConcurrentPerProvider`, a JSON object like `{"anthropic":2}`; empty clears it) |` row, one row per (key, view), distinct from the Transcript `Ctrl+P` inside the `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+W`/`Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+V` row.

**Tests.**
- **test/tui-provider-caps.test.ts** (new) — drive the full TUI with `makeTuiRepo`/`withTui` (`test/fixtures/tui-fixtures.js`), on the default Activity view: Ctrl+P opens with the footer `provider caps ›` and the line empty when `tumwater.json` leaves the key unset, and pre-filled with compact JSON when it holds `maxConcurrentPerProvider`; Enter on valid JSON writes the object to `tumwater.json` and flashes `provider concurrency caps set to <text>`; Enter on a non-object (`anthropic`) or a cap of `0` flashes the validator's `maxConcurrentPerProvider …` message, leaves the editor open with the text kept and the file byte-identical; Enter on an empty line removes the key and flashes the cleared wording; Esc and Ctrl+T restore a pre-typed draft byte-for-byte; with another editor open (Ctrl+B), Ctrl+P flashes the busy message and leaves it open.
- **test/tui-keys.test.ts** — pin the scope: Ctrl+P on Activity opens the provider-caps editor (`session.held.providerCaps`), while Ctrl+P on a role's Transcript still opens the pause editor (`session.held.pauseEditRole`), so the new arm does not swallow the pause key.
- **test/tui-frame.test.ts** — pin `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, providerCapsMode: true })` reading `provider caps ›` and the hint branch's `save provider caps`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+P opens the editor; the footer reads `provider caps › `, the line pre-fills compact JSON from a set `maxConcurrentPerProvider` (empty when unset) and the open flash names `maxConcurrentPerProvider`, the JSON-object shape and the empty-clears rule. On a role's Transcript, Ctrl+P still opens the pause editor.
- Enter with a JSON object writes `maxConcurrentPerProvider` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `provider concurrency caps set to <value>`; Enter on an empty or whitespace-only line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `provider concurrency caps cleared`; a non-object or a non-positive-integer cap flashes the validator's `maxConcurrentPerProvider …` message and stays open with the text kept and the file byte-identical.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the editor and restore the prompt draft byte-for-byte; entering it while another prompt-line editor holds the line, and entering another editor while it holds the line, both flash the busy message; Up/Down do not recall prompt history into its text.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, providerCapsMode: true })` reads `provider caps › `, pinned directly; `hintLine`'s provider-caps branch names `save provider caps`; the Activity hint names `Ctrl+P provider caps`.
- docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table has a `Ctrl+P | Activity` row naming the per-provider caps and `maxConcurrentPerProvider`, and `test/tui-keys-doc.test.ts` passes.

### The plan loop reruns after a productive plan tick while PLANS.md still has planning room (planned 2026-10-19 by the director role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the git-author entry edits src/git, src/merge, src/init, src/backlog/backlog-commit.ts, src/backlog/backlog-archive.ts and src/operator/revert.ts, the dashboard-settings entry src/config/config-editable-keys.ts and src/ui/gui, the TUI-instructions entry src/ui/tui and docs/cli.md, and the backlog-grep entry src/backlog, src/cli and docs/cli.md, none of which is src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts or docs/config.md; touches src/brief/brief.ts src/config/config-views.ts src/scheduling/scheduling.ts src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts src/runner/runner-run.ts plans/work-ratio.md docs/config.md test/brief.test.ts test/scheduling.test.ts test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts test/main-red.test.ts; done 2026-10-19 by the feature role)

**Goal.** The plan loop's tight loop is keyed on whether the product still needs plans, not on the brief's placeholder status. Today the plan role schedules a zero min gap only while `briefStatusIncomplete(root)` is true — `scheduleConfigForRole`'s `descriptionIncomplete` flag, read in `orchestrator-scheduling.ts` and `runner-run.ts`. The readme role replaces the placeholder early, so the zero gap turns off while the project is still being planned: the plan role drops to its 3600 s slow clock (or bootstrap's 20 s) even right after a productive run. The user's rule: "If the product is not yet finished, and the plan role produced a change last time it ran, the plan loop should run again." The plan role's own machine signal that it still has planning work is `planBacklogFull` (`src/scheduling/claims.ts`): PLANS.md's `## Planned` holds at least `planBacklogTarget` eligible plans and no needs-review/needs-replan mark. While it is false there is planning room, so a productive (`changed`/`queued`) plan tick should rerun on the next poll (zero gap) and an unproductive (`no_change`) tick should drop to the idle backoff; once the backlog reaches target, `planDeferral` already holds the plan tick (`plans-full`) until work frees a slot. This subsumes both current triggers — a fresh project's empty backlog is not full — so `bootstrapActive` and `briefStatusIncomplete` no longer need to reach `scheduleConfigForRole`.

**Approach.**
- **src/config/config-views.ts** — change `scheduleConfigForRole(config, role, bootstrapActive, descriptionIncomplete = false)` to `scheduleConfigForRole(config, role, planBacklogOpen = false)`: when `planBacklogOpen && baseRoleOf(role) === "plan"`, return `{ ...configForRole(config, role), minRunIntervalSeconds: 0 }`; every other role and the closed case return `configForRole(config, role)`. Rewrite the doc comment to state the rule — the plan role's zero gap is on while PLANS.md still has planning room (below `planBacklogTarget`, or holding a marked plan) — replacing the bootstrap and placeholder wording.
- **src/scheduling/scheduling.ts** — in `EligibilityOptions`, delete `bootstrapActive` and `descriptionIncomplete` and add `planBacklogOpen?: boolean` with the new doc comment; in `isEligible`'s `minGapSeconds`, call `scheduleConfigForRole(runner.config, runner.role, opts.planBacklogOpen === true)` and update the comment above it.
- **src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts** — delete the `briefStatusIncomplete` import and the `const descriptionIncomplete = briefStatusIncomplete(root);` read; at the `isEligible` call pass `{ once: once.active, planBacklogOpen: !planBacklogFull }` (`planBacklogFull` is already destructured from `ctx`). Also remove the now write-only `bootstrapActive` from `SchedulingPassCtx`, break it out of `orchestrator.ts`'s two poll context objects, delete it from `gate-polls.ts` (no reader left after the above), and drop it from the test ctx fixtures.
- **src/runner/runner-run.ts** (formerly src/loop/loop-tick.ts) — delete the `bootstrapStatus` and `briefStatusIncomplete` imports and their two reads; import `planBacklogFull` from `../scheduling/claims.js`; compute `const planBacklogOpen = !planBacklogFull(ctx.root, ctx.config);` and pass it as `scheduleConfigForRole(ctx.config, ctx.role, planBacklogOpen)`; update the comment.
- **src/brief/brief.ts** — delete `briefStatusIncomplete` (its only callers are the two scheduling sites above); `EMPTY_STATUS` and `managedSections` stay. Deviation: `EMPTY_STATUS` keeps as a module-private constant (the exports-unused guard, test/exports.test.ts, flags an export no other file references, and its only external consumers were `briefStatusIncomplete` and the two removed test imports), so the `export` is dropped while the constant and `managedSections` stay.
- **docs/config.md** — in the `minRunIntervalSeconds` row, replace the placeholder clause: while PLANS.md's `## Planned` still has planning room (`planBacklogFull` false) the plan role schedules with a zero gap, so a productive plan run reruns on the next poll and an unproductive one drops to the idle backoff; once the target is met the plan loop defers (`plans-full`) and this interval applies.

**Tests.**
- **test/brief.test.ts** — remove the "briefStatusIncomplete is true for the templates…" test and the now-unused `briefStatusIncomplete`/`EMPTY_STATUS` imports (line 11/13; `EMPTY_STATUS` has no other use in the file).
- **test/scheduling.test.ts** — replace "bootstrap schedules plan on the global gap…" and "a placeholder-status brief schedules plan on a zero gap…" with: `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", true).minRunIntervalSeconds === 0`, `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", false).minRunIntervalSeconds === configForRole(cfg, "plan").minRunIntervalSeconds`, and `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "feature", true)` equal to `configForRole(cfg, "feature")`; then a plan runner ticked `changed` under the two-argument zero-gap config leaves `nextRunAt - Date.now() < 1000` and `isEligible(r, afterChanged + 1, "", 0, { planBacklogOpen: true })` returns `{ run: true, reason: "scheduled" }`; a following `no_change` tick moves `nextRunAt` at least `cfg.idleBackoff.initialSeconds` into the future and, with `lastMainHead` unchanged, `isEligible(..., { planBacklogOpen: true }).run` is `false`. Keep the closed case: `isEligible` without `planBacklogOpen` holds a just-productive plan on its 3600 s clock.
- **test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts** — replace "a plan runner is admitted while the brief status is the placeholder…" with one that keeps a due-now plan runner (`runs = 1`, `lastRunEndedAt = T0`, `nextRunAt = T0`, non-empty `lastMainHead`) and, via `ctx.planBacklogFull`, asserts `pollRunnerReasons` admits it when `planBacklogFull` is false and skips it when true; drop the `EMPTY_STATUS`/`readmeTemplate` imports if no longer used elsewhere in the file. The bootstrap-held test's `ctx.bootstrapActive = true` line and the ctx builder's `bootstrapActive: false` are dropped with the field.
- **test/main-red.test.ts** — the queued-healer test's `isEligible` call drops the removed `descriptionIncomplete: false` flag (now the empty `{}`), the only edit the scheduling-option rename forces here.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", true).minRunIntervalSeconds === 0`; `scheduleConfigForRole(cfg, "plan", false)` and every non-plan role equal `configForRole(...)`.
- After a `changed` plan tick under `planBacklogOpen`, a plan runner whose `lastRunEndedAt` is that tick is admitted immediately by `isEligible` with reason `"scheduled"`; after a `no_change` tick, with `lastMainHead` unchanged, it is not admitted and `nextRunAt` is the idle backoff out.
- `pollRunnerReasons` admits a due-now plan runner with `ctx.planBacklogFull` false and skips it with `ctx.planBacklogFull` true.
- `briefStatusIncomplete` is gone and no source file imports it.
- `npm test` passes.

**Files touched.** Source: src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts, src/runner/runner-run.ts, src/gates/gate-polls.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts. Docs: docs/config.md, plans/work-ratio.md. Tests: test/brief.test.ts, test/scheduling.test.ts, test/orchestrator-scheduling.test.ts, test/main-red.test.ts.

### The TUI's Activity view edits the team-wide quiet-hours window with Ctrl+S, the terminal twin of the dashboard Settings `quietHours` field and `tumwater config set quietHours` (planned 2026-10-19 by the plan role; independent of every eligible Planned entry — the healer entry edits src/baseline/main-red.ts, the plan-rerun entry src/brief/brief.ts, src/config/config-views.ts, src/scheduling/scheduling.ts, src/orchestrator/orchestrator-scheduling.ts and src/loop/loop-tick.ts, and runner part 1/14 moves src/loop and test/loop*; none touches src/ui/tui. It shares src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts and the shared editor seams (tui-editor-session.ts, tui-editors.ts, tui.tsx, tui-frame.ts) and docs/cli.md's TUI-keys table with the in-flight backlog-search and Ctrl+L instructions entries, which each add one editor target/leaf and one hint token — a rebase either way; the blocked plain-terms runner/run/cleanup series renames identifiers in src/ui/tui only in far-behind parts, a rebase. touches src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts src/ui/tui/tui.tsx src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts docs/cli.md test/tui-quiet.test.ts test/tui-frame.test.ts) — done 2026-10-19 by the feature role

**Goal.** The per-role quiet-hours window is editable from the TUI (Ctrl+O on a role's Transcript, `createQuietEditor`, `src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts`) and the dashboard role drawer, and the team-wide top-level `quietHours` window is editable from the dashboard Settings view (the `quietHours` row, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-settings.ts`) and `tumwater config set quietHours`. The TUI has no team-wide editor: `grep -n quietHours src/ui/tui/*.ts` finds only `quietHoursPerRole` in `tui-editor-quiet.ts`, and Ctrl+S is free on the Activity view (view 0) — the view that already owns the team-wide daily cap (Ctrl+B) and pause/stop (Ctrl+F/Ctrl+Q). Add the team-wide window to the existing quiet editor, so an operator can put the whole team to sleep for a nightly window without leaving the terminal.

**Approach.**
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts** — `createQuietEditor` gains a `let quietTeam = false` scope flag, cleared by `exitQuietMode`. Split the entry arms so each key toggles its own scope and neither steals the other: the Ctrl+O arm enters only `ctx.view >= 1 && ctx.view <= ctx.roleIds.length` and, while open, exits only the per-role scope (Ctrl+O in team mode is consumed and does nothing); the new Ctrl+S arm, added after it, enters only when `ctx.view === 0` and closed, and while open exits only the team scope. Both arms keep the `session.heldEditorFlash("quiet")` busy guard, set `session.held.quiet` and `session.held.quietTeam`, save/restore the draft through `session.settleDraft`/`session.restorePromptFrom`, and open with the flash `edit the team's quiet hours (e.g. 23:00-07:00, empty clears): Enter to save, Esc to cancel`. The team arm pre-fills `loadConfigSafe(session.root).config?.quietHours ?? ""` (the per-role arm keeps `quietHoursPerRole.<base>`), and `lockedRole` stays null. The Enter arm computes `const cfgKey = quietTeam ? "quietHours" : \`quietHoursPerRole.${baseRoleOf(lockedRole!)}\`` and words the success flash `team: quiet hours set to <window>` / `team: quiet hours cleared` for the team scope, keeping the existing role wording. `setConfigKey`/`unsetConfigKey` and `validateConfig` (whose `parseQuietHours` error names `quietHours` for the top-level key) own the window's truth; an invalid window flashes and stays open.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts** — add `quietTeam: boolean` to `TuiHeld` beside `quiet`, documented as the quiet editor's scope, and initialize it `false`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts** — add `quietTeam: boolean` to `TuiEditorState`, and return `quietTeam: session.held.quietTeam` from `state()` beside `quietMode`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui.tsx** — add `quietTeam: s.quietTeam` to the `mode` object handed to `hintLine`/`promptPrefix`.
- **src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts** — both inline mode types on `hintLine` and `promptPrefix` gain `quietTeam?: boolean`; `promptPrefix` returns `team quiet hours › ` when `quietMode && quietTeam` (else the existing `quiet hours › `), and `hintLine`'s quiet branch says `save team quiet hours` when `quietTeam`.
- **docs/cli.md** — the TUI-keys `Ctrl+S` row gains Activity with `edit the team's quiet-hours window (quietHours; an empty line clears it)`.

**Files touched.** Source: src/ui/tui/tui-editor-quiet.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editor-session.ts, src/ui/tui/tui-editors.ts, src/ui/tui/tui.tsx, src/ui/tui/tui-frame.ts. Docs: docs/cli.md. Tests: test/tui-quiet.test.ts, test/tui-frame.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- On the Activity view with an empty prompt line, Ctrl+S opens the editor; the footer reads `team quiet hours › ` and the prompt line pre-fills the file's top-level `quietHours` (empty when unset); on a role's Transcript Ctrl+S still opens the min-run-interval editor (`tui-editor-interval.ts`), not this one.
- Enter with a valid window writes top-level `quietHours` through `setConfigKey` and flashes `team: quiet hours set to <window>`; an empty line removes the key through `unsetConfigKey` and flashes `team: quiet hours cleared`; a malformed window flashes the `quietHours` parse error and stays open with the text kept.
- Ctrl+O on a role's Transcript still writes `quietHoursPerRole.<base>` with its existing wording; while the team editor is open, Ctrl+S exits it and restores the draft byte-for-byte, and Ctrl+O leaves it open.
- Esc and Ctrl+T cancel the team editor and restore the draft byte-for-byte; entering another prompt-line editor while it is open, and it while another holds the line, both flash the busy message.
- `promptPrefix({ budget: false, rolePromptFor: null, queuedEditFor: null, answerFor: null, quietMode: true, quietTeam: true })` reads `team quiet hours › `, pinned directly.

### Plain terms code runner, part 1/14: Move the loop modules to src/runner and their tests to runner names (done 2026-10-19 by the feature role; requires Plain terms code merge 11a/11, Plain terms code merge 11b/11, Plain terms code merge 11c/11, Plain terms code merge 11d/11, Plain terms code merge 11e/11 and Plain terms code merge 11f/11 landed; design in plans/terminology.md "Code names"; touches src/loop/ + src/roles/loop-ids.ts + src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts + test/loop*.test.ts + test/fixtures/loop-*.ts + every importer + docs/invariants.md + DEVELOPMENT.md)

**Goal.** Mechanical. The per-instance worker's modules and their tests move to `runner` names, with every import path and path citation updated and no identifier changed, so later parts rename symbols inside files that already carry their final names.

**Approach.**
- `git mv` only (keeps history), then fix paths. No identifier, comment wording or test title changes beyond the paths themselves.
- Leave record prose alone: do not edit BUGS.md, PLANS.md, QUESTIONS.md, PLANS-DONE.md, BUGS-FIXED.md or any `plans/*.md`. Their old paths are correct as written. Finished entries record files as they were, and open plans (this series' own entries included) name both sides of the moves they describe, so a find-and-replace over them turns `src/loop/` → `src/runner/` into `src/runner/` → `src/runner/`. That sweep got this part rejected five times on 2026-10-18 and -19 (bullet added 2026-10-19 by user). The pre-queue self-check no longer lists these files; a review objection asking for them to be swept is outside this part's scope, so say so in RISK.
