### Each loop's last-landed age: `tumwater status`, the TUI and the dashboard say when a loop last landed a change to main — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The fleet row already names a loop's `commits` (a lifetime count) and its last-tick time (`lastTickEndedAt`), and the just-landed no-change streak counts consecutive empty ticks. None of them answer the wall-clock question an autonomous-fleet operator most wants: "when did this loop last actually land something on main?" A loop can tick `no_change` forever — the streak climbs but resets on any landing, and the commits count climbs without saying how long the dry spell has been. This adds the direct answer, the productivity complement to `lastError` and `lastTickEndedAt`.

**Approach.** Persist one timestamp and render it, mirroring how `lastError` rides LoopState → status-payload → the table/dashboard.
- `src/loop/loop-state.ts`: add `lastLandedAt?: number` to `LoopState` beside `lastError`/`lastTickEndedAt` (epoch ms; absent until the first landing, absent on states written before the field existed).
- `src/tick/tick-apply.ts` `applyMergeOutcome`'s `changed` branch — the same site that does `s.commits += 1` and resets `consecutiveErrors`: set `s.lastLandedAt = Date.now()`. `Date.now()` is already used in this function (the rejected branch's backoff rung), so no new clock seam; a `rejected`/`merge_conflict`/`aborted` landing leaves the prior value, so the age means "last successful landing".
- src/ui/status-payload.ts per-loop row: carry `lastLandedAt: s.lastLandedAt ?? null` beside `lastTickEndedAt`, so `tumwater status --json` exposes the epoch ms.
- `src/ui/status-render.ts`: add a last-landed cell to each loop row (a `· <N> ago` suffix, reusing the existing `ago`/`lastTickCell` relative-time formatter so the last-tick and last-landed columns cannot drift on what "ago" means); a loop that has never landed shows the same dash `lastTickCell` uses for a never-ticked loop.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts` (the fleet rows, where the drawer also lists the last tick): render "landed <N> ago" from the payload field with the GUI's own `fmtAgo`, matching the `ago` rule client-side.
- Tests: extend the status-payload/status-render loop-row tests and the tick-apply landing tests — a `changed` landing sets `lastLandedAt`; a rejection/merge-conflict leaves the prior value; a fresh loop carries none; the rendered age matches the relative-time format.

**Files touched.** `src/loop/loop-state.ts`, `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`, src/ui/status-payload.ts, `src/ui/status-render.ts`, `src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts` (the fleet-row render; the drawer site `gui-client-drawer.ts` gained a "Last landed" kv), and the matching `test/` suites (tick-apply, status, gui-loops, gui-drawer). No `src/cli`, `src/doctor`, `src/review`, or `src/loop` scheduler change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A loop whose change lands shows a last-landed age in `tumwater status`, the TUI fleet table, and the dashboard Fleet rows; a loop that has never landed shows the same dash as a never-ticked loop; the age is unchanged by a `rejected`/`merge_conflict`/`no_change` outcome.
- `lastLandedAt` is set only in `applyMergeOutcome`'s `changed` branch, pinned by the tick-apply test; it rides the persisted `LoopState` like `lastError`/`lastTickEndedAt`, so a restart keeps it.
- The status table and the dashboard render the age with the same relative-time formatter as the last-tick column (no drift), and `tumwater status --json` carries the `lastLandedAt` epoch ms.
- `npm run test` passes.

### A doctor check names checks the review gate kept recognizing as flakes: a "flaky checks" check surfaces the gate's flake memory (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — the three eligible waiting entries touch `src/tick`, `src/loop`, `src/ui/status-*`, and `src/cli/`, and this touches none of them: only `src/doctor/` and the one exported window constant in `src/review/known-flakes.ts`, so it lands on any feature run alongside them) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** When a scoped check failure passes on its one immediate re-run, the review gate logs `gate check failed then passed on retry — flaky: <headline>` and the failure is excused (src/review/review-precheck.ts ~line 75-79); `src/review/known-flakes.ts` is the gate's memory of those warnings so a later repeat of the same normalized headline is not misattributed to whichever change happened to hit it. That memory is internal: no doctor check, `tumwater status`, TUI, or GUI ever names that the suite is flapping. So a genuinely flaky check silently burns a re-run each landing and hides real instability — an operator never learns which checks keep failing-and-passing, which is exactly the information that explains intermittent rejections and signals a suite that needs attention. The gate already owns the only two things a surfacing needs (`FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` and the 24h `KNOWN_FLAKE_WINDOW_MS`); only the read-and-name surface is missing.

**Approach.** A read-only doctor warning that tallies `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` warnings over the gate's own window, grouped by the gate's own normalization, warning only when a check flapped more than once so a routine one-off flake stays quiet.
- `src/review/known-flakes.ts`: `export const KNOWN_FLAKE_WINDOW_MS` (line 20, currently private) so the check and the gate share one window and cannot drift. `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` and `normalizeClusterKey` (src/failure/failure-cluster.ts) are already exported; import them.
- `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`: add `checkFlakyChecks(root)` beside the other root-reading warnings. Read `const { events } = readEventsSince(root, KNOWN_FLAKE_WINDOW_MS)` (readEventsSince is already imported here, and checkProviderConcurrency at line 565 shows the temp-log pattern), then count `e.message.indexOf(FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX) >= 0` per `normalizeClusterKey(e.message.slice(at + FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX.length))` into a `Map<string, number>` (reusing the exact slice-offset logic from `flakeKeys` so the check, the gate, and the memory split the same prefix identically). When any key's count is `>= 2`, return `warnOutcome` naming the window and, most-frequent-first, each flapped check and its count (`<headline> ×<n>`, `andMore`-style truncation like checkStalledPlans uses); otherwise `okOutcome` ("no check flapped more than once in the last 24h", or the no-warnings phrasing). `ok`/`warn` never affect doctor's exit code (outcome.ts), so this is observational only.
- `src/doctor/doctor.ts`: register `{ name: "flaky checks", ...checkFlakyChecks(root) }` in the checks array, beside the other root-reading warnings (after the `project check` entry at line 114).
- `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`: mirror the existing checkProviderConcurrency/checkBuildCheck temp-event-log setup (the file already exercises these root-reading checks). Two `FLAKY_WARNING_PREFIX` warnings whose headlines normalize to one cluster key within the window warn naming that check ×2; a single warning (or none) reads ok; warnings whose normalized keys differ (two distinct checks) warn naming both; the count aggregates across a duration/SHA difference so two firings of the same check read as one check's count of 2; an event older than the window is ignored.

**Files touched.** `src/doctor/doctor-checks.ts`, `src/doctor/doctor.ts`, `src/review/known-flakes.ts` (one `export` keyword), and `test/doctor-checks.test.ts`. No `src/status`, `src/ui/status-*`, `src/tick`, `src/loop`, `src/cli`, `src/events`, or `src/failure` change.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A check whose failure was excused as flaky at least twice in the last 24h shows as a `flaky checks` warn in `tumwater doctor` naming that normalized check and its count; a single flake, or none, reads `ok` — a routine one-off flake is not noise.
- Aggregation uses `normalizeClusterKey` and the slice-offset logic exactly as `flakeKeys` does, and the window is the gate's own exported `KNOWN_FLAKE_WINDOW_MS` — one shared constant, no drift between the memory and the surface.
- Warnings are `ok`/`warn` only (observational, never a `fail`), so a flaky suite cannot fail a scripted doctor pre-flight; no other doctor check's output changes.
- `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater logs --count` tallies each event type over the selected window (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — it touches only `src/cli/log-commands.ts`, the `logs` arm of `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, and the `test/log-commands*.test.ts` suites; none of the three eligible waiting entries — per-provider 5/5, the no-change streak, recent-outcomes — touch `src/cli/` or its tests) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** `tumwater logs` can already dump a window (`-n`, `--since`), filter it (`--type`, `--grep`), and tail it (`-f`), but the shape of that window is invisible until the operator scans it row by row: "which event types flooded the log in the last hour?" needs a glance, not a scroll. `history --summary` tallies only per-loop tick outcomes (history.ts's own view), and nothing tallies the full event-log vocabulary — `tick_end` vs `land_failed` vs `prompt_enqueued` vs the health-check chatter — over the window an operator already selects. This plan answers "was that a blip or a pattern?" with one command. `tumwater logs --count` prints one `N × <type>` line per present event type over exactly what the `-n`/`--since`/`--type`/`--grep` flags select, so it composes with every existing filter and can never disagree with the plain view (both derive from the same filtered set in the same pass).

**Approach.** Add a value-less `--count` flag to the event feed in `cmdLogs` (src/cli/log-commands.ts), read beside the existing `--json` presence check.
- Scope the tally to the same events the plain view would print: the `--since` window (`readEventsSince`) when `--since` is present, else the `-n`/default-50 tail (`readEventsTailWithEnd`), each already filtered through the shared `feedFilter` (the single `--grep`/`--type` predicate both views thread). Tally into a `Map<type, number>` keyed by `e.type`, then render `N × <type>` lines most-frequent-first with ties broken by type — one shape shared by both window sources so the print and the count cannot drift on which events count.
- Composition and rival shapes, mirroring the existing checks with the same wording style: `--count` is rejected with `-f`/`--follow` (counting implies a bounded window), with `--role`/`--prompt` (that view is a pi transcript, not the event log), and expands `rejectUnknownArgs`'s `logs` list in src/cli.ts with a new `COUNT_FLAG` (`{ names: ["--count"] }`, value-less like `SUMMARY_FLAG`, added in src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts). `--json` composes with `--count`: instead of the prose lines it emits one `JSON.stringify` object mapping `type → count` (keys sorted) as the machine-readable tally.
- Empty tally: answer with the same prose the plain view prints for its empty case (the window's `no events in …` / `no events matching …` line, or a `-n` empty-filter line) exactly as `cmdLogs` already chooses it, so a filtering miss is never silent and a `--type` that matches nothing names the type. Never print `SPARSE_WINDOW_NOTE` from a count run's empty window (the note rides rows, and a count has none).
- Docs: add `[--count]` to the `tumwater logs` usage form in src/cli/help.ts (line ~83) and one detail line beside the `--json` one stating it tallies the window's event types; optionally one README sentence.
- Tests: extend `test/log-commands.test.ts` (and `test/cli-logs-filtering.test.ts` for the composing/filter cases) with a temp event log — a mixed-type window prints `N × <type>` most-frequent-first and matches the per-type row count of the plain view; `--count --since` and `--count -n` scope to their windows; `--count --type <t>` and `--count --grep <p>` count only matches; `--count --json` emits the sorted object; `--count` with `-f`/`--role`/`--prompt` fails naming both flags; an empty window/empty match prints the plain view's empty prose; plain `tumwater logs` (no `--count`) output is byte-identical to today.

**Files touched.** `src/cli/log-commands.ts`, `src/cli.ts`, `src/cli/cli-flag-specs.ts`, `src/cli/help.ts`, `test/log-commands.test.ts`, `test/cli-logs-filtering.test.ts` (and/or `test/cli-logs.test.ts`), optional one README sentence. No `src/loop`, `src/status`, `src/ui/status-*`, `src/orchestrator`, `src/doctor`, `src/roles`, `src/events`, or `src/gui` file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- `tumwater logs --count` prints one `N × <type>` line per present event type (most-frequent-first, ties by type) over the same events the identical flags' plain view prints; the tally of each `--type`/`--grep`-selected subset equals the number of rows the plain view shows for it.
- `--count` composes with `--since`, `-n`, `--type`, and `--grep`, and `--count --json` emits a sorted `type → count` object; `--count` with `-f`/`--follow`, `--role`, or `--prompt` fails naming both flags.
- An empty tally prints the same no-events/no-match prose the plain view prints (never silent in prose), and `--count` never prints the sparse-window note.
- `tumwater help logs` lists `--count`, existing logs goldens are unchanged without the flag, and `npm run test` passes.

### `tumwater role <id>` and the GUI loop drawer show the loop's recent tick outcomes: the last few `changed`/`queued`/`no_change`/`error` results with when and how long (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other Planned entry — it reads only `src/events/` (the event log) and writes only `src/roles/` (role-view/role-render) plus the GUI drawer, no `src/loop`, `src/tick`, `src/status`, `src/ui/status-*`, or `src/report` file; the only overlap is that PLANS.md's per-provider part 5/5 also adds a field to `src/roles/role-view.ts` (its provider/cap line) — different fields, land in either order, the harness resolves the merge) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** `tumwater role <id>` — the per-loop inspection command — tells you everything about what a loop IS (catalog, model, provider, tier, image input, fallback) but nothing about what it has been DOING: its only outcome signal is the current last result on the status row. The failure digest aggregates per-role outcomes over a whole window, and the waiting no-change-streak plan renders a single counter, but nobody shows a loop's discrete recent outcomes with their times. That is exactly the harness premise's diagnostic need — a loop that is no-op cycling (`no_change` after `no_change`), landing regularly, or erroring repeatedly is only distinguishable from an ordinary idle loop by reading its tick results over a short window. This plan shows them, read straight from the event log so it runs with the fleet stopped and never touches the live state.

**Approach.** Collect and render the last several `tick_end` outcomes for one loop.
- `src/roles/role-view.ts`: add an optional `recentOutcomes?: Array<{ ts: number; result: string; durationMs?: number; summary?: string }>` field to `RoleViewPayload`, collected in `rolePayload` beside the existing `loadLoopState` read. Use the existing event reader — `readEvents(root, ...)` (src/events/event-read.ts, the backwards tail scan) — filter `type === "tick_end" && eventRole(ev) === role`, take the newest up to 8 by `ts`, and map `{ ts, result, durationMs, summary }` from the event's own fields (tick-finalize.ts emits exactly `result`, `durationMs`, and `summary` on `tick_end`). Absent when the loop has no `tick_end` events, so the JSON shape is unchanged for a never-ticked loop.
- `src/roles/role-render.ts`: add a `## Recent tick outcomes` section to `renderRoleMarkdown` (after the `- Queued prompts: N` bullet, before the Instructions-override fence), one line per outcome: `- <time> · <result> · <span> — <summary>` using the existing `formatTimestamp` and a duration/short `time-ago` phrasing already used in this file (`formatTimestamp` is already imported and used for the model-fallback `since`). When `recentOutcomes` is absent render nothing new, so old goldens are byte-identical. `renderRoleMarkdown` is already shared verbatim by `tumwater role <id>` and the TUI's notebook view, so both surfaces gain it for free.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-drawer.ts`: in the loop drawer's `drawerrole` render (which already consumes the `/api/role` payload that `rolePayload` feeds, gui-endpoints.ts:275), append the same recent-outcomes list when `recentOutcomes` is present, mirroring the markdown lines.

### Surface a per-loop consecutive "no change" streak: `tumwater status`, the TUI and the dashboard show how many ticks a loop has returned nothing to do (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; does not require any part of the per-provider concurrency-caps series (4/5, 5/5) or the per-provider-spend plan to land — those touch `src/loop/loop-state.ts` and the `src/status`/`src/ui` renders for other than a no-change counter, and no part derives anything from this streak; this adds one persisted counter and renders it, so it lands independently on any feature run) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The fleet already detects a loop that FAILS tick after tick (`consecutiveErrors`, the `error streaks` doctor check and the "failing" cell) and one that is quiet-killed, and it stretches a loop's min-tick gap while it keeps finding nothing (`recentOutcomes`/`yieldMultiplier`, src/scheduling/backoff.ts). But nothing names a loop that keeps WAKING and returning nothing to do — a silent no-op run of `no_change` ticks is invisible, reading only as the ordinary "sleeping (for …)" cell. That is exactly the harness premise's failure mode ("Loop sleeps a while when the prompt results in no further changes" run ad infinitum): a role whose find-something-to-do is broken, or whose prompt keeps coming back empty against real backlog, is indistinguishable from a healthy idle loop. The `no_change` result is already the verdict, and the loop state already persists streak-style counters beside it (`quietKillStreak`); only the per-loop no-change count and its rendering are missing.

**Approach.** Count consecutive `no_change` outcomes per loop in the existing accumulator, persist it, and expose it on every loop surface. Count `no_change` specifically (not the yield ring's `n`, which also swallows non-landing results like `user_aborted` and `review_error`); reset on any other completed result so a loop that lands between no-ops never shows a stale streak.

- `src/loop/loop-state.ts`: add a persisted `noChangeStreak?: number` field, documented right beside `consecutiveErrors`/`quietKillStreak` (the `LoopState` interface ~line 132-139) as "consecutive completed ticks that ended `no_change`". Absent on states written before the field existed — reads as 0; it also joins the `healOptionalNumber` list in `loadLoopState`.
- `src/tick/tick-apply.ts`: in `applyTickOutcome`, immediately beside the `quietKillStreak` increment (the result-driven block ~line 109-115, next to `pushYieldOutcome`), add `s.noChangeStreak = outcome.result === "no_change" ? (s.noChangeStreak ?? 0) + 1 : 0;`. Every completed result reaches this block (tick-finalize.ts:80 calls `applyTickOutcome` for every outcome), so `changed`/`queued`/`error`/`aborted`/`quiet_killed`/`user_aborted` all reset it and only a `no_change` tick grows it.
- `src/ui/status-payload.ts`: in the per-loop record builder, beside `yieldMultiplier` (~line 107), add `noChangeStreak: s.noChangeStreak ?? 0,` so the TUI and GUI have the number without re-deriving anything.
- `src/ui/status-model.ts`: in `loopPhase`, the resting state cell (`sleeping (for …)` ~line 222, the idle/skip labels after), when `(s.noChangeStreak ?? 0) >= 2` append a ` · no change ×N` suffix to the returned label (an `onErrorStreak` loop already returns "failing" earlier, so no explicit guard is needed). N=1 and an absent field render today's label byte-identically; the landing/paused/cap/budget/main-red/failing cells return earlier and never carry it.
- `src/ui/gui/gui-client-loops.ts` (`phaseDetailBase`, the pill's second line shared by the loops-table row and the detail drawer): read `noChangeStreak` from the payload and append ` · no change ×N` when it is >= 2 on a resting idle cell (sleeping/queued/idle/deferred), mirroring the status label — the streak rides the loop detail here, not `gui-client-model.ts`'s `phaseInfo`, which sees only the pre-rendered phase string.
- Tests: src/tick/tick-apply's tests (test/tick-apply.test.ts) assert a `no_change` outcome increments the field and any other completed result resets it; the status-model/status-payload/gui-client-loops tests assert the ` · no change ×N` suffix appears at N>=2 on the resting cells and is absent at 0/1, on a missing field, or on live/paused/failing cells, and that the payload/loop-state heal carry the field.

No `src/scheduling`, `src/doctor`, `src/status`, `src/orchestrator`, `src/concurrency`, or `src/report` file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A loop whose last N completed ticks were `no_change` (N>=2) shows ` · no change ×N` in `tumwater status` and the GUI; N=1, a 0/absent field, or a non-`no_change` last result render today's label exactly, so old goldens are unchanged.
- Any completed result other than `no_change` — a landing (`changed`), a `queued` change, an `error`, an `aborted`, a `quiet_killed` — resets the counter to 0 (a loop that lands between no-ops never shows a stale streak).
- The counter persists across a restart (a persisted `LoopState` field), and the streak also appears as `noChangeStreak` in `tumwater status --json` / the status payload for the TUI and GUI to read.
- No new doctor warning (a long streak on a legitimately idle maintenance loop with an empty backlog is expected, not an error) — this is observational only.
- `npm run test` passes.

### The "looks stuck" alert says how long each loop has been stuck (planned 2026-10-16 from an operator request; independent of every other Planned entry — no other waiting plan edits the `stuck` alert's detail or threads a silence duration into the `AlertLoop` rows, though PLANS.md's image-input part 5/5 also touches `src/ui/fleet-alerts.ts` to add an `images` alert; land in either order, the harness resolves the merge) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** When the dashboard (or the TUI attention lines) raises "<loop> looks stuck", it should say for how long the loop has been stuck, not just that it is. Today the `stuck` alert's detail shows the matched stall phrase (`tool call stalled: bash` or `no pi output for 6m05s`) — the tool-call case carries no duration at all, and the duration is only whatever the cell happened to render. The honest stall span is `LiveProgress.quietMs` (ms since the last pi log write), already capped to the tick's own elapsed by `progressOfTick`, so it never reads a previous run's silence.

**Approach.** Thread the silence duration from the live tail into the alert, and render it.
- Add an optional `stuckMs?: number` to `AlertLoop` in `src/ui/fleet-alerts.ts` — ms the in-flight run has been silent (its stall span); absent when the caller has no live tail.
- Both `AlertLoop` builders already hold the live tail, so populate it: in `src/ui/status-payload.ts`'s loops map add `stuckMs: live?.quietMs ?? undefined` (`live` comes from `loopRowCells`); in `src/ui/status-render.ts`'s final `loops` map (~line 388) destructure `live` from `withMetrics` and add `stuckMs: live?.quietMs`.
- In `fleet-alerts.ts`'s `stuck` branch (`~line 144`), render a duration per stuck loop using the shared `duration` helper (already exported by `src/ui/tick-progress-model.ts`, beside `STALL_RE`):
  - duration = `l.stuckMs` when present; otherwise parsed from the phase's own "no pi output for `<d>`" match; otherwise omitted (no `for …`).
  - Keep the stall cause from the existing `STALL_RE` match when it is a tool call (`tool call stalled: <tool>`), and do NOT double-print the duration that a "no pi output for `<d>`" match already carries (append ` for <duration>` only when the match has none).
  - Resulting line shape, e.g. `feature: tool call stalled: bash for 12m` or `feature: no pi output for 6m05s` (unchanged).
- Update `test/fleet-alerts.test.ts`'s stuck case to pass `stuckMs` and assert the new `for <duration>` suffix; keep the existing no-`stuckMs` and no-pi-output assertions as the fallback-regression net. The alert's `title` stays "<loop> looks stuck".

**Files touched.** `src/ui/fleet-alerts.ts`, `src/ui/status-payload.ts`, `src/ui/status-render.ts`, `test/fleet-alerts.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A running loop whose phase reads `working 30m · turn 2 · tool call stalled: bash` with `stuckMs` 720000 raises the `stuck` alert with detail naming the role, the tool, and "for 12m".
- A loop whose phase reads `working 6m · no pi output for 6m05s` raises a `stuck` detail that names the duration once — no doubled "for … for …" — with or without `stuckMs`.
- A stuck loop with no `stuckMs` and a tool-call-stalled phase still alerts, detail as today (no new suffix).
- Both observer surfaces show it: `tumwater status` (which feeds the TUI attention lines through `status-render`'s `loops`) and the dashboard (through `status-payload`'s `alerts`).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Per-provider spend in the day/`--since` report: a `Cost by provider` line, folded from a `providerCost` map persisted on `tick_end` and `landed`/`land_failed` (planned 2026-10-16 by plan; independent of every other entry — the per-provider concurrency-caps series (4/5, 5/5) is about lease/slot limits in `src/orchestrator`, `src/loop`, `src/status`, `src/doctor` and touches none of these files, and the waiting "Landed by role" report plan (which also touches `src/report/report-data.ts`/`report-render.ts`) adds a per-role line on a different map, so the two land in either order on separate feature runs; this plan spans `src/tick/`, `src/landing/`, and `src/report/`) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** No surface today names what a mix-provider fleet spent per provider. The report's cost line is per ROLE (`Cost by role`, `src/report/report-render.ts:121` day, `:231` `--since`), doctor shows per-provider slots but not spend, and the daily cap is fleet-global — so an operator running a deepinfra default plus a claude-opus strong tier has no way to see that the claude seam is the expensive half. The attribution is free: `TickUsage.fold` and `foldLandingUsage` already receive `provider` at every fold site today (`src/tick/tick-usage.ts` `fold(s, run, authoring, provider)`, `src/loop/loop.ts:259` `foldUsage(run, provider)` and `:289` `foldLandingUsage(run, provider)`, `src/loop/loop-pi.ts:258`), and the landing's `foldUsage` already closes over `reviewProvider` (`src/landing/landing-slot.ts:392`). The only missing pieces are persisting the per-provider split on the events and summing it in the report.

**Approach.** Thread a per-run `provider` split through the usage accumulators, persist it on the accounting events, and fold a `Cost by provider` line into the fleet report.
- `TickUsage` (`src/tick/tick-usage.ts`): add an in-memory `providerCost: Map<string, { costUsd: number; notionalCostUsd: number }>`. In `fold`'s two cost arms (real vs notional, beside the `recordDailyCost` and `notionalCostUsd` bumps) add the run's `costUsd`/`notionalCostUsd` to `providerCost.get(provider)`, creating the entry — guarded on `provider !== undefined` (a run whose provider was never resolved attributes nothing, so old single-provider behavior is unchanged). Clear it in the same reset that zeroes `costUsd`. Expose a serialization helper returning `Record<provider, {costUsd, notionalCostUsd}>` or `{}` when empty.
- `src/tick/tick-finalize.ts`: in the `tick_end` payload add `...(Object.keys(providerCost).length > 0 ? { providerCost } : {})` with the same omit-when-empty idiom the prompt-token fields use, so a tick whose runs carried no provider renders byte-identically to today. (The field rides `HarnessEvent`'s index signature, `src/events/events.ts:117`, no events.ts change.)
- `LandingUsage` (`src/landing/landing-slot.ts`): add `providerCost: Record<string, { costUsd: number; notionalCostUsd: number }>`. In `landingUsage()`'s returned `foldUsage`, beside the `usage.tokens`/`usage.cost`/`notionalCost` bumps, add each run's cost to `usage.providerCost[reviewProvider]` (the landing already folds every run under `reviewProvider`, so the split keys to that seam — the same key the author-side `foldLandingUsage(run, reviewProvider)` already charges). Extend `writeLandingOutcome`'s `landed`/`land_failed` payload with `...(Object.keys(usage.providerCost).length > 0 ? { providerCost: usage.providerCost } : {})`.
- `src/report/report-data.ts`: add `costByProvider: Record<string, number>` and `notionalByProvider: Record<string, number>` to `UsageFold` (beside `costByRole`/`notionalByRole`) and `DayFold`, plus the zero-fills in the day seed and `collectReportSince`'s `acc`. In `foldUsageEvent`'s `tick_end` branch and its `landed`/`land_failed` branch, when `ev.providerCost` is a non-empty object, iterate it and `addTo(target.costByProvider, provider, costUsd)` / `addTo(target.notionalByProvider, provider, notionalCostUsd)` — the existing `costByRole` add pattern applied per provider, guarded with `costUsd !== 0`/`notionalCostUsd !== 0` so zero stays absent. Add optional `costByProvider?: Record<string, number>`/`notionalByProvider?: Record<string, number>` to `ReportDay`, set in `collectReport`'s fleet branch (guarded by `Object.keys(...).length > 0`, like `notionalByRole`), and add required (`empty when none`, like `failedTicksByRole`) versions to `SinceReport`, summed from each day's map in `collectReportSince` and returned beside `failedTicksByRole` (role-scoped: `narrowToRole` over a `providerCost` truthy map).
- `src/report/report-render.ts`: immediately after the existing `Cost by role` line in both renders — day `:121`, `--since` `:231` — add, gated to the fleet report only (`data.role === undefined`, the same guard the notional lines and `ROLE_SCOPE_NOTE` use): day `` if (Object.keys(data.costByProvider ?? {}).length > 0) lines.push(rankedRoleLine("Cost by provider", rankedRoleMap(data.costByProvider).filter(([, c]) => c > 0), usd)); `` and the `--since` analogue `` rankedRoleLine("Cost by provider", rankedRoleTotals(data.series, (d) => d.costByProvider ?? {}).filter(([, c]) => c > 0), usd) `` — `rankedRoleTotals` already sums across the series like `costByRole` at `:231`. If the window also has notional spend, add a matching `Notional by provider` line with the same zero-means-absent conditional the day `Notional by role` (`:136`) uses.

**Files touched.** `src/tick/tick-usage.ts`, `src/tick/tick-finalize.ts`, `src/landing/landing-slot.ts`, `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, and `test/report.test.ts` plus the tick-usage/tick-finalize tests (a `tick_end` and a `landed` fixture event carrying `providerCost` folded through the existing report-collection harness, and a multi-provider tick proving the split). No `src/status`, `src/doctor`, `src/ui`, `src/orchestrator`, or `src/concurrency` file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A fleet day report whose `tick_end` events carry `providerCost` renders `**Cost by provider:** <provider> — $x` right after `Cost by role`; a multi-provider tick (an authoring run on the default plus a fallback retry) splits its cost across both providers; a landing's spend appears under its reviewer seam's provider. The `--since` report sums each provider across the window the same way.
- A window with no `providerCost` on any event renders no `Cost by provider` line at all (zero means absent), so old golden outputs render unchanged; `report --json` omits `costByProvider`/`notionalByProvider` when no provider had spend.
- A role-scoped report prints no provider line (its `ROLE_SCOPE_NOTE` is unchanged); the existing per-role `Cost by role` and `notionalCostUsd` totals keep their exact current values (the provider maps are a parallel tally, never subtracted).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Per-provider concurrency caps, part 4/5: a tick's lease follows its runs across providers (planned 2026-10-15 from an operator request; requires part 3/5 landed; part 5/5 follows) — done 2026-10-16

Design: plans/provider-concurrency.md §5 "Leases follow the tick's runs".

**Goal.** A tick is counted against the provider it is actually using. An author on
`huggingface` whose reviewer runs on capped `omlx` takes an omlx slot for the review and gives
its huggingface slot back. A budget handback or model-failure switch re-keys the same way.

**What landed.** The lease of a tick, a vet, or the resolver now rides in an `AsyncLocalStorage`
store (src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts, the check-permit.ts `holdingPermit` pattern), entered
around `runner.tick()` in the launch pass (roles keyed on their admission seam, the director on
its forced lease), around the vet task body and around the resolver run. `LoopPi`
`runWithTransientRetry` — the one choke point authoring, gate, landing and resolver runs all
pass through — calls `ensureProviderLease(opts.config)` before `runPi`: no lease in context is a
no-op (a bare LoopPi unit test, `tumwater tick`), a run on the lease's own key never re-keys, and
a run on another key re-keys — releasing the old key first, then waiting only on the new key's
headroom while keeping the fleet permit. The store also carries `piDefault`, so a bare no-model
pi seam resolves to the same key admission used. The pool-slot wait rule (worktree-pool.ts's
leaseSlot) drops the context lease's key before it parks on a busy pool, so a key holder never
waits on a slot a re-key waiter holds (§5 "No deadlock"). A re-key that parks is visible:
`providerWaitStage` (src/landing/landing-slot.ts) shows the vet's row as "waiting for a provider
slot" rather than a hung review.

**Files touched.** src/loop/loop-pi.ts, src/concurrency/provider-lease.ts (new, beside
check-permit.ts), src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts, src/landing/landing-vetting.ts,
src/landing/landing-drain.ts, src/landing/landing-slot.ts, src/git/worktree-pool.ts,
src/concurrency/semaphore.ts (export the lease type), test/provider-lease.test.ts (new),
test/landing-pipeline-seams.test.ts (acquireUnlessAborted now returns the lease it granted),
test/orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts.

**Acceptance criteria (this part).**
- Author on `huggingface`, reviewer on `omlx` capped at 1 and held by another tick: the gate run
  waits and shows the wait; the review starts once omlx frees. (The vet's lease is keyed on the
  review seam at acquire — part 3/5 §4 — so it holds omlx from the start and never holds the
  author's huggingface slot; the "huggingface count drops by one during the wait" sub-claim does
  not arise in this design. What is pinned instead: a re-key releases its previous key before
  waiting on the new one, unit-tested in test/provider-lease.test.ts.)
- A tick whose runs all share one provider never re-keys: unit-pinned (test/provider-lease.test.ts).
- A run with no lease in context behaves as today: unit-pinned (test/provider-lease.test.ts).
- With `worktreeSlots` 1, two ticks on one provider and a cap large enough for both to hold it
  at admission, the slot-waiting tick drops its key while it waits and both ticks finish: the
  slot-drop is unit-pinned, and the both-finish case is e2e (orchestrator-permits.e2e.test.ts).
- `npm test` passes.

### The day/`--since` report breaks landing-slot outcomes down by role: a `Landed by role` line naming which roles' changes reach main and which bounce off the landing gate (planned 2026-10-15 by plan; independent of every other entry — the one eligible waiting entry is the per-stage-elapsed landing plan, which changes `src/landing/landing-slot.ts`, `src/landing/landing-queue-render.ts`, and `src/ui/status-model.ts` and touches no `src/report/` file; this touches only `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, and `test/report.test.ts`, so the two land in either order on separate feature runs) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** The report's landing line (`landingShareLine`'s `of which landing runs … (N failed)`) folds the `landed`/`land_failed` branch into **fleet-global** `landingRuns`/`landingFailed`, and `Commits by role` counts `merged` events (pure success, commit granularity). Nothing names which AUTHORING role's changes reach main through the landing slot — and, the genuinely new signal, which roles' changes bounce off the gate (`land_failed`: review rejection, under-cap review, a conflict, a blocked fast-forward, a shutdown abort). An operator watching the fleet cannot tell whether gate failures are concentrated in one role's changes or spread evenly, so a role whose every change dies in a merge conflict reads as healthy next to a role that mostly lands. The events already carry the authoring role (`writeLandingOutcome` in `src/landing/landing-slot.ts` logs `loop: entry.role`), so the attribution is free — the fold just discards it. This adds one per-role landing line to both the day and `--since` renders, folded from that same branch.

**Approach.** Mirror the `failedTicksByRole` plumbing end to end, but on the `landed`/`land_failed` branch of `foldUsageEvent` (`src/report/report-data.ts`), keying by `baseRoleOf(eventRole(ev))` — the same normalization the `merged` branch uses, so `feature-2` aggregates into `feature`.
- In `src/report/report-data.ts`: add `landedByRole: Record<string, number>` and `landingFailedByRole: Record<string, number>` to the `UsageFold` and `DayFold` interfaces, plus the zero-fills in `dayFoldFor` and `collectReportSince`'s `acc` (beside the existing `zeroLandingCounts()` spread). In `foldUsageEvent`'s `landed`/`land_failed` branch add, beside the existing `target.landingRuns`/`target.landingFailed` bumps: `const role = baseRoleOf(eventRole(ev)); if (ev.type === "landed") addTo(target.landedByRole, role, 1); else addTo(target.landingFailedByRole, role, 1);`. Add optional (`zero means absent`, exactly like `revisionsByRole`) `landedByRole?: Record<string, number>` and `landingFailedByRole?: Record<string, number>` to `ReportDay`, set in `collectReport`'s fleet branch beside the `landingRuns` fields guarded by `Object.keys(...).length > 0`, and in the role-scoped branch via `narrowToRole(...)`. Add required (`empty when none`, like `failedTicksByRole`) `landedByRole: Record<string, number>` and `landingFailedByRole: Record<string, number>` to `SinceReport`, seed both in `collectReportSince`'s `acc` and return them beside `failedTicksByRole` with the `narrowToRole` form for a scoped report.
- In `src/report/report-render.ts`: immediately after the `Commits by role` line in both renders (`renderReportMarkdown`'s ~line 133 and `renderSinceReportMarkdown`'s ~line 243), add a `Landed by role` line, gated to the fleet report only (`data.role === undefined`) — a role-scoped report continues to omit landing (its `ROLE_SCOPE_NOTE` already says landing runs are fleet-wide and omitted), so the per-role attribution does not contradict that stance. Using the existing `rankedRoleMap`/`rankedRoleTotals`/`rankedRoleLine` helpers: day `rankedRoleLine("Landed by role", rankedRoleMap(data.landedByRole ?? {}), String)`; `--since` `rankedRoleLine("Landed by role", rankedRoleMap(data.landedByRole), String)`. Then—to carry the new failure signal without bending a single-`number` formatter (rankedRoleLine's `fmt` takes only the count, not the role)—a second conditional line `Landing failures by role`, printed only when any role has one, the same `zero means absent` conditional form the `Notional by role` line uses: day `` if (Object.keys(data.landingFailedByRole ?? {}).length > 0) lines.push(rankedRoleLine("Landing failures by role", rankedRoleMap(data.landingFailedByRole ?? {}).filter(([, n]) => n > 0), String)); `` and the `--since` analogue reading `data.landingFailedByRole` (no `?? {}` — it is always present there).

**Files touched.** `src/report/report-data.ts`, `src/report/report-render.ts`, and `test/report.test.ts` (a `landed` and a `land_failed` fixture event folded through the existing report-collection harness confirming both per-role maps, plus render assertions on both renders). No `src/landing`, `src/ui`, `src/doctor`, or `src/failure` file.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- A fleet day report whose events include a `landed` from `feature-2` and a `land_failed` from `bugfix` renders `**Landed by role:** feature — 1` and a `**Landing failures by role:** bugfix — 1` line; a window with landings but no failures renders `Landed by role` with no `Landing failures by role` line at all (zero means absent), so old golden outputs with no landing failures render unchanged.
- Instance suffixes aggregate into their base role exactly as `Commits by role` does (`feature-2` counts under `feature`): a grep of the fold's landed keying shows `baseRoleOf` used, not the raw `eventRole`.
- No behavior change elsewhere: `landingRuns`/`landingFailed`/`landingShareLine` keep their exact current totals (the per-role maps are a parallel tally, never subtracted), a role-scoped report prints no landing line (its `ROLE_SCOPE_NOTE` is unchanged), and `report --json` omits `landedByRole`/`landingFailedByRole` when no role has either (the zero-means-absent convention).
- `npm run test` passes.

### Image input, part 5/5: the dashboard, the TUI, and prompt attachments say which loops cannot read images (planned 2026-10-15 by user; requires part 4/5 landed; design and decisions in plans/image-input.md "Surfaces" and "Attachments"; touches src/status/, src/ui/, src/roles/role-render.ts, src/inbox/, src/gui/gui-prompt-commands.ts, and the docs) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** An operator should know without running doctor that a loop's model cannot read images, and what happens when one of its ticks tries. An attachment no configured model can read should be refused when it is submitted, not discovered at tick time.

**Approach.** See plans/image-input.md "Surfaces".
- Status: add per-loop `imageInput: true | false | null` and `imageReroute: "<tier> (<model>)" | null`, plus the cached probe failures, to the snapshot and `status --json` (src/status/status-roles.ts and the payload).
- A new `images` alert in `fleetAlerts` (src/ui/fleet-alerts.ts), shared by the dashboard banner and the TUI attention lines:
  - **blue** when every text-only loop has a target: "<roles> run on models that can't read images" — "A tick that reads an image stops and reruns on <tier> (<model>)."
  - **amber** when some text-only loop has none: "No configured model can read images for <roles>" — "A tick that reads an image fails, and image attachments to these loops are refused. Declare image input on a vision model in pi's models.json, or point a tier at one."
  - **amber** when a model claims images but failed doctor's probe.
  - **No alert** when every enabled loop reads images.
- Role page (src/roles/role-render.ts, `tumwater role <id>` and the dashboard panel): `Images: no — reruns on strong (…)`.
- Submit gate in `submitRolePrompt` (src/inbox/inbox-submit.ts), reached by the GUI endpoint and `tumwater prompt --attach`:
  - refuse images when the target loop's seam reads none and it has no target, naming the fix;
  - otherwise return a notice the CLI prints and the composer shows under the image chips (src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts), e.g. "feature's model can't read images; this prompt runs on strong (claude-opus-5-5)".
- Docs: README.md (`prompt --attach`), docs/cli.md (`doctor --reprobe`, the image input check), docs/backends.md (image input: claims, probe, reroute).

**Files touched.**
- src/status/status-roles.ts and the status payload, src/ui/fleet-alerts.ts, src/roles/role-render.ts
- src/inbox/inbox-submit.ts, src/inbox/prompt-commands.ts, src/gui/gui-prompt-commands.ts, src/ui/gui/gui-client-composer.ts
- README.md, docs/cli.md, docs/backends.md
- tests: fleet-alerts, status, role-render, inbox-submit, GUI prompt endpoint, and gui-client tests

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With an all-claude config there is no `images` alert, and every loop reports `imageInput: true`.
- With a text-only default and a vision strong, the alert is blue and names the default-tier loops and the strong model. With nothing able to read images, it is amber. A cached probe failure raises the amber probe alert.
- `tumwater prompt --attach x.png` to a loop with no reroute target exits non-zero naming the fix, and queues nothing (no image file left behind). To a loop with a target, it queues the prompt and prints where it will run. The GUI endpoint behaves the same, and the composer shows the notice.
- `tumwater role feature` shows the `Images:` line.

### Per-provider concurrency caps, part 3/5: landings and the director count against their provider (planned 2026-10-15 from an operator request; requires part 2/5 landed; parts 4/5–5/5 follow) — done 2026-10-16

Design: plans/provider-concurrency.md §4 "Who holds a lease" and §6 "Priority headroom and the
vet limit".

**Goal.** Every model stream the fleet starts counts against its provider. That includes landing
vets, the merge's conflict resolver and the director, besides role ticks. A work loop's priority
headroom is withheld only where the loop could use it.

**Approach.**
- Vets: `acquireUnlessAborted` (src/landing/landing-pipeline.ts), as `startVet` calls it
  (src/landing/landing-vetting.ts), takes a key:
  - the review seam's key for the author's role, through `reviewRunConfig`;
  - none when the review gate is off.
- The resolver: landing-drain.ts's `runPi` wrapper acquires at `MERGE_TIER` with

### Mixed claude + pi fleets, part 2/4: tick pairs, the fallback breaker and fleet-hold stamps are keyed by the seam that ran (planned 2026-10-15 from an operator request; requires part 1/4 landed; parts 3/4–4/4 follow) — done 2026-10-15

Design: plans/provider-concurrency.md §9, gaps 2–4 and "One key".

**Goal.**
- A tick on a claude fallback is handed back when the budget gate reopens.
- A dead claude fallback is demoted.
- A 429 storm on a claude reviewer holds `claude` instead of the pi author's provider. The same

  fallback pair that `tickOnPair` (src/gates/budget-gates.ts) compares against.

  the same way. Audit every other `modelPairName({ provider: cfg.provider, … })` and switch it.
- The failure stamps `lastRateLimit` and `lastBackendFailure` (src/tick/tick-usage.ts) gain
  `provider`, the failing run's `seamHoldKey`. `LoopPi.runWithTransientRetry` knows it from
  `opts.config` and passes it into the fold.

    `runProvider` for a stamp without one.

    provider.
- `requestFollowUp` (src/loop/loop-pi.ts) passes its `cfg` to `loopPiOpts`, so `nativeLogFile`
  and the authoring budget cap follow the seam the follow-up runs on.

### Image input, part 4/5: a tick stopped for a blind image read reruns on a tier that can read images (planned 2026-10-15 by user; requires part 3/5 landed; design and decisions in plans/image-input.md "Rerunning on a model that can read images" and "Attachments"; touches src/loop/, src/tick/, src/prompt/prompt-followup.ts, src/events/) — done 2026-10-16

**Goal.** Part 3 stops a blind tick; this part moves its work to a model that can see the image. When the role's tier has a reroute target (part 1's `imageRerouteTarget`, the budget-fallback borrow order, free pairs only at the cap), the tick hands its work to that model instead of failing. A queued prompt that attaches images to a text-only loop starts on the target directly, with no failed tick first.

**Wiring note (landed 2026-10-16).** Three deviations from the plan's literal bullets, all matching its intent:
- The one-shot `LoopState.imageReroute` carries the resolved target seam (`tier` + `provider`/`model`/`thinking`, rebuilt via `withModelOverrides`) plus `from`/`path`. It is cleared in `planTickStart` (after the handoff note reads `from`/`path`) rather than at tickPhase start, so a tick skipped before the plan (an empty director inbox) leaves the reroute pending and the facts survive to the note. A director tick never resumes, so planTickStart's image-reroute branch never clears it for the director; the director's marker is instead cleared in `runTickPhase` (src/loop/loop-tick.ts) once its rerouted tick is confirmed to run, so the reroute stays one-shot there too.
- The regime is plumbed through `LoopRunner.budgetFallbackActive` (set beside `config` by the orchestrator's budget poll, src/gates/gate-polls.ts) and `LoopRunner.rerouteRegime(now)`; the verdict context gains `config`/`rerouteRegime`/`runModel`. The attachment preflight's `image_reroute` event names the loop's own model as `from`.
- The `imageBlind` verdict branch reduces to: if `state.imageRerouteActive` (this tick already started on the target) → `error` (one hop); else resolve a target and, when one exists, `aborted`/`image-reroute` + the one-shot marker; else `error`. Gate runs (reviewer/resolver) are never rerouted.

**Approach.**
- In part 3's verdict branch, when a target exists:
  - end the tick `aborted` with a new resume cause, `image-reroute`. Add it to `ResumeCause` (src/prompt/prompt-followup.ts), `TickOutcome.resumeCause` (src/tick/tick-outcome.ts) and `LoopState.resumeCause` (src/loop/loop-state.ts);
  - set a one-shot `LoopState.imageReroute = { tier, model, from, path }` (healed like `modelFallback`);
  - set `nextRunAt` to now and requeue the prompt via `requeueForResume`.
- The next tick:
  - `tickPhase` (src/loop/loop-tick.ts) picks the target's config over the primary/fallback choice, as do `LoopRunner.runConfig` (src/loop/loop.ts) and `setTickPair`;
  - `tick_start` carries `reroute: "image"`;
  - the run is always a fresh session over the kept worktree, via the `budget-capped` handoff path in src/tick/tick-resume.ts, never `--continue`. `buildHandoffPrompt` gets an `image-reroute` note: an earlier run on <model> stopped when it read <path>, because that model cannot read images; its edits are in your worktree, so review `git diff` and finish or discard them; this model can read images, so read the image again;
  - director ticks never resume, so the requeued prompt runs fresh on the target.
- One hop only: a blind read during a rerouted tick takes part 3's `error` path.
- **Preflight:** at model choice, peek at the loop's next prompt (`peekPrompt` / `peekRolePrompt`).
  - If it carries `[image attached: …]` lines and the seam reads no images, start on the target and log `image_reroute` with `preflight: true`.
  - With no target, end the tick `error` without spawning a run.
- New event `image_reroute {loop, tick, from, to, tier, preflight}`. The `resume` renderer in src/events/event-format.ts learns `image-reroute`.

**Files touched.**
- src/loop/loop-tick.ts, src/loop/loop.ts, src/loop/loop-state.ts
- src/tick/tick-verdict.ts, src/tick/tick-outcome.ts, src/tick/tick-resume.ts
- src/prompt/prompt-followup.ts
- src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts
- src/gates/gate-polls.ts (regime plumbing), docs/invariants.md (INV-J2)
- tests: test/tick-verdict.test.ts, test/loop-2.test.ts, test/prompt-followup.test.ts, test/event-format.test.ts (the tick-apply tests needed no change: the `aborted` branch already carries `resumeCause` through)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a text-only default tier and a vision strong tier (fake pi), a blind read on a default-tier loop ends the tick `aborted`/`image-reroute`. The next tick runs immediately on the strong model in a fresh session over the kept worktree; its prompt carries the handoff note naming the path, and its `tick_start` has `reroute: "image"`. The tick after that is back on default.
- A blind read during the rerouted tick ends it `error`, with no second reroute.
- A queued prompt with an `[image attached: …]` line on a text-only loop starts directly on the target (`image_reroute`, `preflight: true`) with no failed tick. With no target, the tick errors without spawning pi.
- With the budget gate on fallback, a reroute only ever lands on a free fallback pair; with none that reads images, the tick errors.
- A rerouted director prompt runs fresh on the target and is delivered exactly once.

### Image input, part 3/5: a tick whose agent reads an image on a model that cannot see it is stopped and fails (planned 2026-10-15 by user; requires part 1/5 landed; design and decisions in plans/image-input.md "Detecting a blind read" and "Failing the tick"; touches src/pi/pi-stream.ts, src/pi/pi-run-result.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts, src/tick/tick-verdict.ts, src/loop/model-fallback.ts, src/events/, a different area from part 2/5's doctor files) — done 2026-10-15

**Goal.** When the model's `input` lacks `"image"`, pi's read tool returns the image with the note `[Current model does not support images. The image will be omitted from this request.]` (pi 1.2.0 `dist/core/tools/read.js:40-45`), and pi-ai strips the image from the request. The run goes on and the agent works from a picture it never saw. `modelFallbackVerdict` even scores that run "answered". The tick should stop and fail instead.

**Wiring note (landed 2026-10-15).** The `image_blind` event's emission lives with the caller that knows loop/tick — `LoopPi.loopPiOpts` (authoring, landing, and conflict-resolver runs) and the two review-gate run construction sites (`src/review/review.ts`, `src/review/review-followup.ts`), so a reviewer's blind read is logged (`action: "logged"`) too. The plan's files-touched list named only the event's declaration/format files; the emission sites are the reason the loop test and the gate-`logged` acceptance both pass.

**Approach.**
- `PiStreamParser.feedLine` (src/pi/pi-stream.ts) remembers each `read` call's `args.path` from `tool_execution_start`. On the matching `tool_execution_end`:
  - it is an **image read** when `result.content` holds an `image` block, or a text block starting `Read image file [`;
  - it is **blind** when that text carries the note, or when the runner told the parser the seam's effective image input is false (the part 2 probe catches a false claim, where pi adds no note);
  - pi's `[Image omitted: could not be converted…]` / `…resized…` processing notes are not blind reads.
- src/agent/run-agent.ts kills an authoring run on the first blind read through the watchdogs' `terminateChild`. Gate runs (reviewer, resolver) only record it.
- `PiRunResult.imageBlind = { path }`, with the error message `read <path>, but <model> cannot read images`.
- `resolveTickVerdict` (src/tick/tick-verdict.ts) gets a branch right after `budgetCapped`, before the refusal and dirty-tree checks. It ends the tick `error` with that `lastError`; backoff, streak, and prompt requeue work as for any error. Part 4 adds the reroute arm here.
- `modelFallbackVerdict` (src/loop/model-fallback.ts) returns `"inconclusive"` for `imageBlind`.
- New event `image_blind {loop, tick, path, model, action: "fail" | "logged"}` in src/events/events.ts, with a feed line in src/events/event-format.ts.

**Files touched.**
- src/pi/pi-stream.ts, src/pi/pi-run-result.ts, src/agent/run-agent.ts
- src/tick/tick-verdict.ts, src/loop/model-fallback.ts
- src/events/events.ts, src/events/event-format.ts
- tests: the pi-stream, run-agent and tick-verdict tests, and a loop test driving the fake pi shim

**Acceptance criteria.**
- With a fake pi emitting a `read` start (`args.path: "/x/shot.png"`) and an end whose text carries the note, the authoring run is killed before its next event and the tick ends `error`. `lastError` names `/x/shot.png` and the model, and `image_blind` is logged.
- The same `read` with an image block and no note does not count as blind on a seam that reads images. It does count when the seam's effective image input is false.
- A processing-failure note (`[Image omitted: could not be converted…]`) is not blind.
- A gate run's blind read is logged (`action: "logged"`) and not killed.
- `modelFallbackVerdict` scores a blind run `"inconclusive"`.

### Per-provider concurrency caps, part 2/5: `maxConcurrentPerProvider` caps role-tick admission (planned 2026-10-15 from an operator request; requires part 1/5 landed; parts 3/5–5/5 follow) — done 2026-10-15

Design: plans/provider-concurrency.md §1 "Config" and §7 "Live reload", plus the role-tick row of
§4. This part makes the cap real for role ticks, the bulk of the load. Vets, the resolver and the
director keep today's keyless permits until part 3/5.

**Goal.** The operator writes `"maxConcurrentPerProvider": { "omlx": 3 }`. From then on no more
than three role ticks run on `omlx` at once, while ticks on other providers fill the rest of
`maxConcurrent`. The cap applies live.

**Approach.**
- Config (src/config/config-schema.ts, config-validation.ts):
  - add the optional map `maxConcurrentPerProvider`;
  - validate each value as a positive integer under a non-empty key;
  - accept unknown provider names (doctor warns in part 5/5).
- Writers (src/config/config-write.ts):
  - `config set|unset maxConcurrentPerProvider.<provider>` merges or removes one entry;
  - `DOTTED_MAP_KEYS` gets a provider-keyed branch that skips the role-catalog check that
    `maxDailyCostUsdPerRole` uses;
  - completion's config-key list picks the new key up.
- The launch pass (src/orchestrator/orchestrator-launch.ts) calls
  `semaphore.acquireLease(roleTier(role), key)`:
  - the key is `seamConcurrencyKey(runner.runConfig(now), piDefault)`;
  - `piDefault` is `readPiDefaultModel(piSettingsPath(piModelsPath()), root)`, which is
    stat-cached and is the same read status-roles.ts makes;
  - the lease's `release` replaces the bare `semaphore.release()`.
- The orchestrator seeds the pool's key caps at startup. config-live.ts calls `setKeyCaps` on an
  edit and emits `provider_concurrency_changed` `{ provider, from, to }` for each changed key.
  event-format.ts renders it like `max_concurrent_changed`.
- `changedConfigKeys` (src/config/config.ts) skips the key, as it skips `maxConcurrent`.
- Docs: tumwater.example.json, docs/config.md, and docs/how-it-works.md's `maxConcurrent`
  bullet.

**Acceptance criteria (this part).**
- With `maxConcurrent` 4 and `{ "omlx": 1 }`, plus fake-pi roles on `omlx/…` and
  `huggingface/…`:

### Image input, part 2/5: `tumwater doctor` probes every model that claims image input with a real image (planned 2026-10-15 by user; requires part 1/5 landed; design and decisions in plans/image-input.md "Doctor"; touches src/doctor/, src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, src/paths.ts, src/agent/image-input.ts, and the two doctor callers in src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts, a different area from part 3/5's stream and verdict files) — done 2026-10-15

**Goal.** A claim in pi's models.json is only a claim. Today's file claims image input for `huggingface/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:deepinfra` but not for the same model without the pin, so at least one claim is wrong. With a wrong claim, pi sends images the model cannot read: the provider rejects them, or drops them silently and the model answers anyway. Doctor should show each claimed model a real image and check the answer.

**Approach.** See plans/image-input.md "Doctor".
- New src/doctor/image-probe.ts:
  - A PNG of a random 4-digit code, drawn with a built-in 5×7 digit bitmap scaled up, black on white. Encode it with `zlib.deflateSync` and a hand-rolled CRC-32 (`zlib.crc32` is newer than the `>=20.3` node floor). No new dependency.
  - The probe runs the resolved pi binary in a run's environment: `pi --print --mode json --no-session --no-tools --no-mcp --provider P --model M --thinking <level> @<png> "Reply with only the 4-digit number shown in the image."`. First confirm that `@image` reaches the model in `--print` mode; if it does not, say so in a `**Needs replan**` note rather than improvising another transport.
  - Pass: the final text contains the code.
  - A wrong answer retries once with a fresh code. Two wrong answers, or a 4xx, fail.
  - A timeout, spawn failure, 429, 5xx, or connection error is "could not verify" and is not cached.
  - The probe's process is bounded like `boundedProbe` (process-group kill at the deadline), with a longer deadline (90 s) because a local model may need to load.
- Cache at `.tumwater/state/image-probes.json` (path in src/paths.ts), keyed agent/provider/model, holding `{verdict, detail, at, claim}`. A verdict is valid for 7 days while the claim is unchanged.
- `runDoctor` gains `probeImages: "missing" | "all" | "never"`, defaulting to `"never"`:
  - the CLI passes `"missing"`, or `"all"` with the new `--reprobe` flag;
  - the TUI Health tab and the GUI doctor endpoint keep `"never"` and show cached verdicts ("not verified yet — run `tumwater doctor`").
- claude seams are not probed; they report "reads images (claude backend)".
- `seamImageInput` honors a cached failed probe: a claimed pi seam whose probe failed reads false.
- Check levels:
  - fail when a claimed model failed, naming its answer or error and the fix: remove `"image"` from `input` in models.json or fix the endpoint, then `tumwater doctor --reprobe`;
  - warn when a probe could not run;
  - ok shows the verified date.

**Files touched.**
- new src/doctor/image-probe.ts
- src/doctor/doctor-model-checks.ts, src/doctor/doctor.ts
- src/paths.ts, src/agent/image-input.ts
- src/cli.ts, src/cli/help.ts, docs/cli.md (`--reprobe`)
- src/ui/tui/tui-keys.ts and src/gui/gui-endpoints.ts (explicit `"never"`)
- tests: new test/image-probe.test.ts, the doctor tests (with a fake pi shim on PATH)

**Acceptance criteria.**
- The generated PNG is valid: signature, IHDR/IDAT/IEND, correct CRCs. Inflating IDAT reproduces the drawn digit pixels.
- A fake pi that echoes the code passes and writes the cache. A fake pi that answers wrong twice fails, naming the model and the models.json fix. A fake pi that exits with a 5xx-shaped error warns and caches nothing.
